item.title: Introduction
item.description:
Hello! Welcome to my homemade wiki! Bear in mind this wiki will likely undergo further changes as I try to balance the game and fill out the lore, sorry for the inconvenience!How to play this TTRPG? Gameplay usually boils down into a simple loop: The GM describes a situation you are in. You decide what to do with the rest of the party. Depending on what you do and how well you do it, the GM describes a new situation. Repeat from step 1. There are different rules that determine how well/terribly you do something. See Rolling Dice, Character Sheet & Stats to see how these are determined.
During combat, there are a number of rules that you need to be aware of. See Melee Attacks, Ranged Attacks, Actions, Rolling Dice, Initiative and Turn Order and Damage Calculations.Don't be too worried about memorising every single rule you see, I'll do my best to ease new players into the system one step at a time. Don't be afraid to ask questions or clarify if needed?
For character creation and stats, visit Character Creation, Character Sheet & Stats and Levels.For general lore, visit the race, faction, notable concepts/events/people folders. Lower movement speed across all races, accounting for relatively small map sizes. Changes to skills system. Currently skills are made for vague roleplaying, not bound by strict rules. This will be changed to have a core of practical, rule bound skills, followed by a bunch of vague roleplaying skills. Skill point allocation will change accordingly to ensure balanced character skill compositions. Massive overhaul to crafting system. Current system is long-crafting, i.e. making things already available through shops available by crafting. The aim of the new systems is to allow players to craft their own unique and tailored gear that cannot be bought. Added weapon and armour smithing, alongside a weapon parts system. Added alchemy crafting for making customised medicine and potions. Added ammunition crafting for making customised arrows, bolts and stones. Added gunpowder chemistry for making customised grenades, firearm shots and gunpowder. Existing items changed to have stats that are reproducible through crafting systems. Changed devastating flanker to allow finishing other people's combo starters when flanking, and guaranteeing flanking attacks will hit. Changed greatsword's multi-hit combo finisher to be more flexible. Added lore entries for the canaries. Added descriptions to all weapon types. Changed foot charging mechanics to be consistent with horse charging mechanics. Changed all tiering systems to be from 1-3 for consistency. Added veterancy mechanic to allow certain stats to cap and scale with level. Added horses, mounted combat rules and horse equipment. Buffed neurotoxin to guarantee death after 5 turns. Added time mechanics to resting and crafting. Reworked initiative rules drastically to try and promote more teamwork and strategizing. Added rulings for different terrains, including swimming rules. Lowered costs of certain throwables and coatings. Lowered costs of gunpowder items and increased firearm shot crafting efficiency. Changed addiction to use exhaustion mechanics. Added lingering area of effect rules. Attempting to grapple will now make you subject to an attack of opportunity if the conditions are right. Added race paths, sort of subclasses for races at level 3. Adjusted shields to have the option to use stat scaling for defences instead of only a hard value. Adjusted dual-wielder trait to give +1 hit chance when dual wielding. Added minor and major complications and added more clear rulings for certain complications. Most situations will use major complications. Once tier 3 proficiency is reached, minor complications will be used for attacks with complications/nat 1s instead. Changed weapon wielding rules to remove potentially unclear terms. Changed arbalest slowing shot to have expert DC to account for slow fire rate. Changed bodkin ammunition to have damage penalties with a higher penetration bonus whilst broadhead ammunition now has penetration penalties with a damage bonus. Added stat scaling to damage of all weapons. Adjusted bandages bleeding amount to account for the lowered mass bleed threshold. Added label of grappling moves to distinguish between grappling moves and attack moves that can be used when grappled. Changed charging move bonuses to activate every 3m instead due to relatively small size of maps, and changed charge vulnerability against opp/zoning attacks to use the charge bonuses for simplicity. Changed weapon moves that move enemies/user to use normal attack hit chance, damage, penetration and BFT values to encourage more movement tactics. Buffed mace debuff moves to last longer. Changed damage formula for weapons that take 1 turn to reload to be more consistent. (E.g. Musket's 2d8 becomes 1d8 + 8). Affected weapons: Musket & Pistols Arbalests Buffed grapeshot to use 1d6 damage die. Added ship stats, rules and modules. Added crafting recipes for cannon ammunition. Updated splash damage ammunition descriptions to account for missed shots. Changed drunkenness and big drinker trait to be more chaotic. When level 2 drunk, all successes come with complications. When level 3 drunk, all successes against you come with complications. Added repositioning to agile trait after evading a melee attack. Added view cone stretching and cracking mechanics to account for situations where maintaining a view cone restriction makes no sense. Buffed bleeding to trigger mass damage faster. Tweaked barbed projectiles and crocodilian death roll to do less bleeding to account for this. Changed broadhead projectiles to do less extra damage but be cheaper to stop them from being a straight upgrade to bodkin projectiles. Added pinned status to combo starters to make combos more feasible. Change rapier to zone when using poking retreat and allow use of poking retreat as a zoning attack. Also fixed some inconsistencies and vague ruling. Added shellshock status to true gunpowder explosives. Added new martial art moves. Buffed bucklers to use deflecting advance with bonus action. Buffed medium shields to have stronger shield bash, and allow use of shield bash and linebreaker with bonus action. Buffed tower shields to use S/D, have stronger shield bash, and allow use of shield bash and towering shove with bonus action. Also added deflecting advance to moveset. Changed dexterity weapon mobility moves to have additional hit chance to maintain consistency with other weapons. Added and changed moves and stats of Numerian Blades. Buffed falces penetration to scale with stats. Buffed flails to do full BFT on miss. Buffed pikes to do more damage and be able to lower/raise on bonus action at tier 2 proficiency. Added centre mass shot ability to amber lances and arbalests. Added overwatch ability to crossbows and light crossbows. Fixed misleading info in recurve and longbow quickshot descriptions. Buffed guidance of the wildwood moves of muskets and pistols to not need movement, and clean up some move descriptions. Buffed daggers' throw to have more range. Changed slings to be an offhand weapon with more moves. Nerfed the optimal range of most ranged weapons due to the relatively small size of maps. Revealed wood faeries lore entry. Armour values are too high for most weapons' penetration, so I'm nerfing it. Layer 1 armours now don't give any armour value, but are needed to wear layer 2 and 3 armours. Faeries get a free arming jacket in their initial equipment to account for them not having layer 1 armours before. Crocodilian unarmed bonuses are getting reworked. To make punching and biting more distinct, punches no longer deal additional damage, but can inflict dazed. Bites have their bonus damage nerfed, capping to +2. Beer gives too much benefit for no downside during combat, so I am adding side effects. Being drunk now penalises hit chance. Dexterity bonuses to defences are too stackable given the rounding-up system, so the dual-wielding defence calculations are being changed. Now, only the melee defence from one of your weapon applies when using two weapons. In addition, melee and ranged defence bonuses from being in light load are now capped at +2. Fixed zoning typo on rapiers. Hand crossbows are now able to fire multiple times and are no longer be subject to melee debuffs. Agile trait is buffed to add dexterity to ranged defence when wielding specific weapons. Changed short sword pommel smash to use dexterity as BFT. Changed thick skin to reduce BFT by your endurance modifier. Added false dragon trait. Buffed fast adapter to give +2 hit chance on miss. Buffed punching, kicking and biting to use core stats as modifiers on hit chance. Buffed maces ankle and wrist breaker moves to use core stats as modifiers on hit chance. Buffed repeating crossbows to be less bad. Helmets have been reworked. They used to give too much armour for the weight, so I tried to rebalance them in a way that still makes sense. For clarity, tiers 1, 2 and 3 are renamed to light, medium and heavy, since the tiering name implies a tier 3 helm is better, when it is no longer necessarily the case. Light helms provide 1 armour only if you have light equipment load. Medium helms provide 1 armour with no caveats. Heavy helms provide 3 armour but restrict your view cone. Aquatines now start with a light helm instead. Added minimum BFT of 1 to weapon moves that use player stats to deal BFT. Reduced the price of toolkits to make them more accessible. Nerfed flails so missing will only deal half the BFT. Adjusted some inconsistencies with the 2-handed flail. I forgot to account for OP combo spam with altan brew, it now only lasts 1 turn but the side effects are less severe. Added concrete DCs for addiction. Added relevant lore for the Right Claw during the East-West War. Added lore entries for the War of the Meadows, Augustine the Third and Lady Numeria. Fixed health level calculations. Changed reaper's grace to offer players a better saving grace against crits. Edited grappling master trait to be less ambiguous. Changed pixie counter mastery to be useful even when not fighting pixies. Changed prone status so others can help a prone character up with an action. Changed the "free" action used to break grapples, put out fires and remove the prone status to only be usable with regular actions. Changed how putting out burning works. Changed some pixie revelation descriptions to have more information. Added tier 1, 2 and 3 traits specific to each race. Added edge case ruling for view cone restrictions. Added rounding up rule to rolling dice page. Changed the lucky trait to be less powerful. Added fire coatings and their crafting recipes. Added skill point allocation to level ups. I originally wanted to award them organically during roleplay but decided a concrete system would probably be better. Added a drug to suppress the effects of insanity. Fleshed out the right claw page to include information on vendors and places. Added shirt of scales(steel). Changed adjustment score of shirt of scales (leather). Changed weapon descriptions to be more clear. Corrected typo on map. Added more information to communal cooking regarding party size. Changed skill allocation guide to be clearer. Added initiative bonuses and maluses to equipment load. Changed equipment load thresholds to be clearer. Changed berserker chain's weighted punch crocodilian bonus. Added that berserker chain's fly combo finisher no longer triggers opportunity attacks. Changed martial arts trait description to include restrictions on initiating grappling. Added range values to grappling moves. Fixed amber lance range values. Changed amber lance shieldbreaker stacks. Changed dual wielding melee defense bonus calculations. Fix stats for javelin's quick throw. Added Wingard quickloader to tools & recipes page. Changed throwing weapons T2 passive to always inflict splintered shield. Added initiative reminder to character creation. Change the spear's bristling display move to have clearer stats. Removed two-handing restriction from the spear's combo moves. Added gunpowder recipes and lesser gunpowder capsule for slings. Tweaked gunpowder ammo recipes to better match prices. Added way to remove Numerian fire. Added goblins and dogs as races.

item.title: Distance and Directions
item.description: The maps will be on square 1m x 1m grids. For calculating diagonals, every second diagonal is doubled in movement. Going down a diagonal would count as: 1, 3, 4, 6, 7, 9, 10, 12, 13, 15... By default, view cones span 90 degrees, and can only be rotated on 45 degree intervals.

Throwing Axes
item.description:
A lighter axe made for throwing, throwing axes lack range, but deliver heavy blunt damage and can be used as a melee weapon. Often used by shock troops to soften up the enemy before charging.Hand requirement: One handed Unique traits: Throwing axes can be used in melee. Throwing axes are "reloaded" automatically.Hit chance: 2 x Strength + Proficiency Damage: 1d8 Penetration: 0 Blunt Force Trauma: Strength Optimal Range: 2m Range Penalty: Hit chance: -2 Damage: -1 Penetration: -1 Blunt Force Trauma: 0 Maximum Penalty Count: 3 Total Range: 30m Weight: 1kg Cost: 90gHit chance: Strength Damage: 1d6 Penetration: +0 Blunt Force Trauma: Strength Total Range: 1m Optimal Range: 1m Melee Defense: 0Weapon part customisations affect both melee and ranged modes. Parts: Blade Material: 2 metal units Craft Time: 4 time-units Cost: 80g Weight: 0.5kg Short-Haft Material: 1 wood units Craft Time: 2 time-units Cost: 10g Weight: 0.5kg Listed are the variants available through shops. If a stat is not stated, it is the same as the base weapon. Melee and Ranged Damage: Base - 1 Melee and Ranged Penetration: Base - 1 Rolling a 1 on an attack roll causes the short-haft to break. Cost: 21g Made of tier 1 materials. Melee and Ranged Damage: Base + 1 Cost: 270g Weight: 0.75kg Made of tier 3 materials. Values are organised as such: (Hit chance | Damage | Penetration | BFT | Range) Values below serve as add-ons to the weapon's base stats, apart from range. "S" or "D" refers to your strength or dexterity modifier. "S|D" means to use either strength or dexterity modifier, whichever is higher. "S|D" is always used as an enclosed term, meaning terms like "S|D+1" refers to "(S|D)+1" and not "S|(D+1)". +0 means no bonuses or maluses. =x means the value is set to x. "|" is used to denote "or", "/" is used to denote divide. (+0 | +0 | +0 | +0 | 1-2m) Regular action. Ranged attack. (+0 | +0 | +0 | +0 | 1m) Regular action. Melee attack. This is your default opportunity attack. (+0 | +0 | +0 | +0 | finishes at 1m) Regular action + movement speed. Melee attack. Run forwards and charge the enemy. Add your dexterity and strength modifiers as hit chance and damage for every 3m moved during the charge.
Charging only works in a straight line.
Charge bonuses also apply to any opportunity / zoning attacks against you when charging. (+Adv | =0 | =0 | =0 | 1-2m) Regular action.
Inflicts splintered shield(1) on your target if they have a shield.
Bucklers are not affected. ( -3 | =0 | =0 | =0 | 1-2m) Regular action/Bonus action. You can use quick throw twice a turn using both actions. Once you use quick throw, you cannot use any other regular throwing action for the turn. This also applies in inverse: once you use any other regular throwing action, you cannot use quick throw for the turn. ( =0 | =0 | =0 | =0 | 0m) Passive bonus.
Whenever you charge, throw an axe at your target 1m before your endpoint. (e.g. If your charge finishes at 1m away from your target, throw an axe when you're 2m away.) The throwing axe does not need to be currently held, just in your equipment load.
Inflict splintered shield(1) on the target if they have a shield, regardless of if the throw hits.

item.title: Repeating Crossbow
item.description:
An invention of the Aquatine Empire, the repeating crossbow allows one user to match the fire rate of 6 others. This comes at the cost of accuracy and punching power, so the Aquatine crossbowmen and women often use poisoned bolts to compensate.Hand requirement: Two handed Unique traits: Holds 6 bolts in a magazine. Requires reloading after the magazine is empty. Can attack more than once in a turn. Bolt type depends on your loading order in the magazine, meaning you cannot swap bolts on the fly.

item.title: Pistols
item.description:
A relatively new weapon on the battlefields, pistols utilise gunpowder to propel various projectile types at extreme speeds, nullifying any armour but requiring a lengthy reload. Used in the offhand, pistols provide an avenue for devastating burst damage when using comparatively lighter and nimble weapons. Seen in the hands of the Conclave's powder corps, the thunder of pixie gunpowder is not easily forgotten.Hand requirement: Off handed
Unique traits: Reloading is not a free action. Ignores threatened debuffs from being in melee range.
This is a faction-unique weapon, it requires specialist training from the Conclave of the Steel Faeries to gain proficiency. A relatively new weapon on the battlefields, muskets utilise gunpowder to propel various projectile types at extreme speeds, nullifying any armour but requiring a lengthy reload. Seen in the hands of the Conclave's powder corps, the thunder of pixie gunpowder is not easily forgotten.Hand requirement: Two handed

item.title: Traits
item.description:
Traits are special buffs your character obtains as they level up.Roll with disadvantage against hyperthermia and hypothermia.
Lose -1 to all your physical core stats on the 4th round of combat and beyond.Gain +10 skill points to allocate during character creation. Deal +1 blunt force trauma with all melee weapon attacks.
Deal +2 damage when flanking.
Gain +2kg to your equipment load thresholds.
Allow you to use regular action medical items with a bonus action.
Level 2 drunkenness now doubles the effect of level 1 drunkenness. Level 3 drunkenness now makes enemy success against you always have complication.
Deal +1 damage when above 8 stress or when insane. Your stress can never fall below half its maximum. When rolling insanities, roll twice and choose whichever you want.
Gain +2 time-units during long rests.Allow you to use endurance for all physical saving throws.On missing an attack, gain +2 hit chance. This effect can stack and is removed upon landing a hit.For checks that can use strength or dexterity, use both at the same time.
Ignore minor food poisoning and treat major food poisoning as minor food poisoning. Allows you to eat up to 2 units of food during short rests for 1d4 healing per unit.
+1m movement speed and +1 charge mobility when charging.Deal -2 damage when above 8 stress or when insane. Lose 1 stress per long rest.
Gain +25kg to your carrying capacity.
Allows you to spend a bonus action to switch places with an ally within 1m without either of you triggering opportunity attacks. The other party must consent to switch.
Gain back 100% of spent ammunition when searching the battlefield instead of 50%.
Ignore the effects of up to 2 points of exhaustion. This includes "addiction" exhaustion.Gain +1 hit chance during the day. Gain +1 melee defense during the night.For every 500g in your inventory, gain a charge of lined pocket up to a maximum of 3. Each charge allows you to half an instance of incoming damage. Charges replenish every combat. Gain +1 armour.Gain +1 movement speed. Unlocks certain special moves with some weapons. You still need the relevant proficiencies. When wielding any weapon that adds dexterity to melee defence, add dexterity to ranged defence also.
Allows you to move 1m without triggering opportunity attacks after a enemy misses a melee attack/grapple against you. You must still be in the enemy's range at the end of this movement.
Inflict 1 additional stack whenever you inflict bleeding.
When inflicting bleeding, instead of bleed being completely negated by a target with >0 effective armour(armour - penetration), each point of effective armour only removes 1 stack of bleed. Remove disadvantage for hitting obstacles if you are directly adjacent to the obstacle. This allows you attack from directly behind your frontliner without risking hitting them. In addition, allies are no longer considered obstacles when charging or lunging.
Allows you to get critical hits on a 19 as well. Only affects attack rolls.Allows you to dual wield all one-handed weapons without penalty. +1 hit chance when dual-wielding without shields.
With a bottle of coating, use a regular action to spit out the contents in an area, afflicting enemies with the coating's effects. Neurotoxins cannot be used this way. Tar coatings ignition requirements still apply.Extend your ranged attacks' optimal range by 1m.
Grant your team temporary hit points equal to double your cooking skill when long resting. When communal cooking, double your cooking skill for the cooking check. In addition, cooking recipes only require 0.5 time-units to make.Always succeed on one saving throw of your choice per combat.If you get a natural one, roll again. This can only happen once per roll.
Allows you to manage items and pick up items using bonus actions.Negative effects lose 1 stack when inflicted on you. The stacks cannot be reduced below 1.
Keep the defence bonuses from your weapons when flanked.Reduce incoming blunt force trauma by your endurance modifier.
Grant your party buffs depending on the number of permanent injuries. 1 permanent injury: +1 hit chance to allies within 1m. 2 permanent injuries: +2 hit chance to allies within 2m. 3 or more permanent injuries: +2 hit chance and +1 damage to allies within 3m. Effects are not cumulative. Gain an additional +1 max health per level. Applies retroactively.Half the weight of weapons when in your equipment load.Whenever you heal an ally, you recover the same amount of health.
On successful stealth ambush, your party takes all their turns before the enemy takes a single turn for the first round, ignoring the zig-zag cycle.
Gain +1 to all physical core stats when below half health.Roll initiative with advantage. Attack with advantage on your first turn.Regain a regular action on a killing blow.Inflict +50% damage under the following conditions: Using a weapon with 0 base penetration. Refers to before weapon customisations. Attacking a target with 0 effective armour.
Allows you to execute combo finishers on your allies' combo starters on flanked enemies. Flanking attacks always hit.Use expert level DC on all your grappling checks, and double your strength/dexterity modifier on saving throws involving grappling. On moves that already have expert level DC, enemies have disadvantage on their saving throws as well.
Roll your saving throws with advantage against attacks that move you.+4 time-units during long rests.
Widen your view cone by 45 degrees.Gain advantage on your damage rolls. Does not influence hit chance.
Mutually exclusive with Stalwart Defender.Enemy attacks against you have disadvantage on their damage rolls. Does not influence hit chance.
Mutually exclusive with Savage Attacker.Once per long rest, survive a single fatal blow on 1 health. Only direct weapon attacks can reduce your health to 0. All other effects (poison, bleeding, area of effect weapons) can only reduce your health to 1.
Double the effects of Godwin's Legacy.
Allows you to move without triggering an enemy's opportunity attacks if an ally is also in the view cone of the enemy.
Use expert level DC on all weapon moves that move your enemies. On moves that already have expert level DC, enemies have disadvantage on their saving throws as well.Allow passive effects from your pixie's masteries to spread to your party members within 1m. Does not include skill gains from masteries.
Opportunity attacks against you have disadvantage if you're under light equipment load.

item.title: Nebulans
item.description:
A species foreign to the continent of the laughing titan, the Nebulans are a humanoid race hailing from an island to the north called the Eye of the Storm. Nebulans have dark, purple skin, with grey, stone-like accents running along their cheeks, fingers and collar bones. Their eyes are grey, with bright, piercing irises. They are physically taller but lankier compared to humans, with two long slits along their back near their shoulder blades.
These slits are where they expel their deadly biological weapon, known as "Stardust". This gas is fatal to all who breath it in, with the exception of the Nebulans and the mushrooms they farm. Nebulans practice a class system, with rulers, warriors and workers. Ruthless and cutthroat, rebellion and uprisings are common, as are purges and crackdowns.Nebulan society is unstable and constant warring amongst itself. After having just finished a civil war, the Nebulans are finally united under a single purpose: Sail south and claim all that the stars touch with their light. Such is their birth right, such is their purpose.Average height: 180cm (Males), 175cm (Females) Average weight: 60kg (Males), 55kg (Females) Lifespan: 60 yearsHealth: 12 Armour: 0 Stress: 10 Movement Speed: 4m Jump Distance: 2m Carrying Capacity: 70kg Equipment Load: 10-20-30-40 Melee Defense: 10 Ranged Defense: 10 Initiative: 0 Free tier 1 proficiencies for the following weapons:
Spears Unending gaze of the Stars
Secrete Stardust in a 2m radius around you.
Stardust is permanent and does not dissipate naturally. It cannot be displaced by wind or movement. Only a Nebulan can remove Stardust.
A pixie with tier 3 counter mastery can convert a tile with 1m radius of Stardust to Marander gas every turn. Stardust cannot displace marander gas. Literacy Speaking Nebulan Tongue: 2 Writing Nebulan Script: 1

item.title: Goblins
item.description: You already know what a goblin is: A small green creature, usually up to no good. Goblins form small bands and gangs, usually hiding out in forests away from major settlements. Some bands are hyperviolent, ambushing travelers on the roadside until they're inevitably found and stomped out by a local patrol force. In the chaos, a few survivors scurry away, only to repeat it all a few years down the road. Some bands prefer to live away in isolation, usually as nomads, relocating whenever civilization comes too close.Average height: 110cm (Males), 100cm (Females) Average weight: 35kg (Males), 30kg (Females) Lifespan: 20 yearsHealth: 6 Armour: 0 Stress: 10 Movement Speed: 4m Jump Distance: 2m Carrying Capacity: 30kg Equipment Load: 7-12-17-22 Melee Defense: 10 Ranged Defense: 10 Initiative: 1 Strength: -1 Endurance: -1 Weasley Miscreant Stealth: 1

item.title: Humans (Wingardian)
item.description:
Humans are all the same species, but I separated them by culture for ease of organisation. Citizens of the Wingard Collective grow up in a tight knit community, with the major religion being Bodilustra. Education takes the form of local schools, although these only teach you basic math, reading and writing, just barely enough so you can start your first transaction. If you wished to learn a trade, you would form a contract with some current master and work under them. Many in the collective choose to be sailors and merchants, exploring the world via sea. The cutthroat nature of Wingardian commerce quickly teaches you to be quick with your tongue, and limber with your coin.Average height: 170cm (Males), 160cm (Females) Average weight: 70kg (Males), 60kg (Females) Lifespan: 70 yearsHealth: 12 Armour: 0 Stress: 10 Movement Speed: 4m Jump Distance: 2m Carrying Capacity: 70kg Equipment Load: 10-20-30-40 Melee Defense: 10 Ranged Defense: 10 Initiative: 0 Free tier 0 proficiencies for the following weapons:

item.title: Humans (Aquatine)
item.description:
Humans are all the same species, but I separated them by culture for ease of organisation. Citizens of the Aquatine Empire worship a diverse array of gods in the Aquatine Pantheon. All citizens go through the same education system, before being sorted into their respective trades by their exam scorings. It is possible to seek a different trade or retake a trade exam, but those who do are usually at a disadvantage compared to those who follow the path the Emperor provides. Rice and grain form the backbone of the Aquatine economy, and even the privileged and the elites will have knowledge on farming. It's taught in school, after all. At least, it was before the Tyranny of the Stars. The Aquatine Empire was all but destroyed following the Nebulan invasion, leaving most Aquatine humans as refugees, lost and wandering.Average height: 170cm (Males), 160cm (Females) Average weight: 70kg (Males), 60kg (Females) Lifespan: 70 yearsHealth: 12 Armour: 0 Stress: 10 Movement Speed: 4m Jump Distance: 2m Carrying Capacity: 70kg Equipment Load: 10-20-30-40 Melee Defense: 10 Ranged Defense: 10 Initiative: 0 Free tier 1 proficiencies for the following weapons:

item.title: Crocodilians
item.description:
Crocodilians are a race of humanoid lizards. They have a maw and tail similar to crocodiles and alligators in the real world, and walk upright, being digitigrade animals (meaning their legs are like that of cats and dogs, where the heel is high up off the ground and they walk on their toes). Crocodillians are known for their impressive strength and thick scales. However, their cold blooded nature means that whilst they require surprising little food for their size, they tend to tire easily and are more susceptible to extreme temperatures. The predominant philosophy amongst crocodilians is The Way of the Sea, and the current leading clan is the Steelscale Clan. Crocodilians grow up with the others of their batch, and undergo a form of group parenting. Your trade is usually determined by your elders, and education depends on your clan. The more physically capable are trained as warriors and sailors, whilst the less physically capable are trained as fishermen, smiths, carpenters etc. Regardless of role, almost all crocodilians are intimately familiar with the sea.Average height: 200cm (Males), 215cm (Females) Average weight: 150kg (Males), 180kg (Females) Lifespan: 60 yearsHealth: 15 Armour: 1 Stress: 10 Movement Speed: 4m Jump Distance: 2m Carrying Capacity: 90kg Equipment Load: 15-25-35-45 Melee Defense: 10 Ranged Defense: 8 Initiative: 0 Strength: +1 Free tier 0 proficiencies for the following weapons:
One-handed Axes
Two-handed Axes
Crocodilians get bonuses to their punches, bites, and have access to the crocodilian death roll at tier 2 Martial Arts.
Cold Blooded Intimidation: 1 Fishing: 1 Swimming: 1 Literacy Speaking Numerian Tongue: 1 Crocodilian Tongue: 2

item.title: Faeries
item.description:
Faeries are a humanoid species who share a symbiotic relationship with Pixies. Faeries have four translucent wings sprouting from their back, although these do not allow them to fly. Faeries are generally smaller and weaker than humans, but are more agile. Faeries provide Pixies with food, shelter, and physical labour in exchange for their mastery over matter. The two species have a innate built-in connection, allowing them to work together much more efficiently and fluidly than any other two species.
Most faeries fall under the Conclave of the Steel Faeries, worshipping The Old Wildwoods. Faeries are usually introduced to a pixie early on as a child in a formal ceremony of bonding. Most faeries spend their entire lives with the same pixie. However, exceptional faeries will sometimes have multiple pixies attached to them. From here on, a faery's undergoes education in a streamlined education system, preparing them for whatever trade they choose. Faeries all undergo mandatory military service, and are required to take up arms to defend the conclave in case of war. Most faeries spend their lives on the Ear, and leaving the island requires special permission. Usually, only emissaries or professional soldiers are allowed to leave. Faeries that leave without permission are considered outcast and are forbidden from returning.Average height: 150cm (Males), 150cm (Females) Average weight: 50kg (Males), 50kg (Females) Lifespan: 150 yearsHealth: 10 Armour: 0 Stress: 10 Movement Speed: 5m Jump Distance: 3m Carrying Capacity: 65kg Equipment Load: 10-20-30-40 Melee Defense: 10 Ranged Defense: 10 Initiative: +2 Endurance: -1 Free tier 0 proficiencies for the following weapons:

item.title: Humans (Numerian)
item.description:
Humans are all the same species, but I separated them by culture for ease of organisation. Citizens of the Kingdom of Numeria spend their entire life involved with the religion of New Illuminetres. Your trade is usually decided by your parent's trade, as most follow whatever their parents do. There are no schools, only colleges within the bigger cities. Education is usually up to your parents or firekeepers/overseers who volunteer their spare time to teach. Choosing to start your holy journey as a monk/nun is always seen as admirable, although rising the ranks of the clergy is no easy feat. With the prevalence of mining and smithing, most lowborn citizens would have some knowledge and exposure to these activities.Average height: 170cm (Males), 160cm (Females) Average weight: 70kg (Males), 60kg (Females) Lifespan: 70 yearsHealth: 12 Armour: 0 Stress: 10 Movement Speed: 4m Jump Distance: 2m Carrying Capacity: 70kg Equipment Load: 10-20-30-40 Melee Defense: 10 Ranged Defense: 10 Initiative: 0 Free tier 0 proficiencies for the following weapons:

item.title: Character Creation
item.description:
Welcome dear traveller, to the continent of the laughing titan. This page is a step-by-step guide to setting up your character.There are 5 distinct types of playable people: Humans from the Aquatine Empire
Humans from the Kingdom of Numeria
Humans from the Wingard Collective
Crocodilians
Faeries in Exile For the sake of party diversity, duplicate races are not allowed, so do consult with everyone else before you sink hours into creating your character!
Go into the individual race page of your chosen race, and take note of the base stats in your character sheet. You can visit the Character Sheet & Stats page to get a comprehensive view of what every stat means. You may also want to look at the different paths available to each race:
Human Paths (Aquatine)
Human Paths (Numerian)
Human Paths (Wingardian)
Crocodilian Paths
Faery Paths Paths are lifestyles your character can take on later down the line that have gameplay effects, so being familiar with them now can help in your backstory creation. You don't have to write an essay on your character, but there are a few questions that you should answer when creating your character.More specifically, what is your character's motivation to leave home and go on dangerous adventures? The aim here is to provide your character with some end-goal they are working towards. Your reason can be as simple as: I'm broke and want to be not broke.This is essential to make sure your character has a vested interest in keeping the party together and working as a team. Your reason can be as simple as: I am afraid to sleep alone at night. This is so I have something to put into the game tailored for you! What is something very important to your character that is not currently with them? This can be a place, a thing, a person, a pet. It can be good or bad. Your something can be as simple as: I really like my mom's blueberry pie. Of course, you will likely need to provide me with more details for me to integrate it, so don't feel shy to reach out to me to brainstorm ideas during the campaign!Faeries, pixies and their equipment are intended to be more advanced and powerful than the other races, so for the sake of balancing, a faery player will need to adhere to the following restrictions in their backstory:
You are not on speaking terms with the Conclave of the Steel Faeries for whatever reason. You can be a faery born outside of the conclave, or an exile of the conclave. You just need a justification for why you can't just stroll in and ask them to solve all your problems. You are not together with your pixie for whatever reason. You will eventually reunite with your pixie once you reach level 3, so bear that in mind. Don't have your pixie killed off in your tragic backstory! Now, it's time to allocate points to your stats. Core stat allocations are bound by these rules: All core stats begin at 0. Race-specific bonuses/maluses are applied after point allocation.
You get 2 points for core physical stats and 2 points for core mental stats. Point costs become more expensive the higher the stat is: -1 to 0: 1 0 to 1: 1 1 to 2: 2 You can lower a stat below 0 to gain a point. Stats cannot go lower than -1, and cannot go higher than +2 during character creation(before racial bonuses/maluses).
Make sure to update your initiative, equipment load and carrying capacity based on your new stats and your race.
Pick 2 major skills and 3 minor skills. These skills will start at level 1. Each race has racial-specific skills, you add +1 to those skills too.
Now, you get to choose 1 tier 0 weapon proficiency for free. Look at the melee and ranged weapon folders to see your options!
Bear in mind your race comes with its own complementary proficiencies, some weapons have restrictions to learning their proficiencies, and some weapons already grant tier 0 proficiency for free. See Weapon Rules for more information.All races begin with this: 50g.
2 bandages. In addition, you can choose 1 weapon. The weapon must cost less than 1001g. You must have proficiency in the weapon. If you chose a non-thrown ranged weapon, you will get 30 pieces of the relevant basic ammunition. If you chose a thrown ranged weapon, you will get 5 pieces of the weapon. Aquatine humans start with:
1 Spear.
1 Medium Shield.
2 Cooked Rice.
1 Light head armour.
1 Commoner's Aketon.
1 Militia's Gambeson. Numerian humans start with:
1 One-handed Mace.
2 Bread.
1 Commoner's Aketon.
1 Butted Mail Shirt.
2 Metal Bars Wingardian humans start with:
1 Short Sword.
1 Buckler
2 Dried Fish.
1 Commoner's Aketon.
1 Shirt of Scales (Leather). 50g Crocodilians start with:
1 Two-handed Axe.
2 Raw Fish. Wingardian humans start with:
1 Longsword or 1 Spear.
2 Smoked Meat.
1 Shirt of Lamellar.
1 Arming Jacket Congratulations! You are now ready to start playing!If you're playing as a faery, you will get access to your pixie at level 3.
Pixies are not playable characters, and do not engage in combat the same way as the playable races. As such, only their core mental stats are alterable: Intelligence cannot be changed.
The remaining core mental stats start at 0. You get 2 points. Point costs become more expensive the higher the stat is: -1 to 0: 1 0 to 1: 1 1 to 2: 2 You can lower a stat below 0 to gain a point. Stats cannot go lower than -1, and cannot go higher than +2 during character creation. These are largely just for show and character consistency, as your faery is still the one that will be doing most ability checks.

item.title: Steelscale Clan
item.description:
Native to the tropical serpent archipelagos in the north, the Steelscale Clan are a faction of Crocodilians. The crocodilians were originally split amongst many different petty clans, until they were united under the Steelscales in 1160. Whilst usually aggressive and clamouring for war, the new generation of Steelscale leadership is more temperate, opening the crocodilians up to trade and even emigration.Crocodilians practice a totalitarian rule. As a compromise to prevent constant bloodshed over leadership, crocodilians practice trail by combat to determine the leading clan, known as the Blood Rites. Held every two years, each greater clan sends their strongest representative in a free-for-all to the death. A winner of the Blood Rites receives great honour and status, although the clan leaders who actually run things are usually not warriors. Despite their love for battle, the crocodilians understand the need for other strengths amongst their higher ups.
Crocodilian religious worship depends on the clan, but most clans, including the leading Steelscales, practice The Way of the Sea, preferring to live their lives in the moment, rather than devoting worship to a god.The crocodilian military is not standardised, with most clans having their own distinctive fighting style. However, axes and throwing weapons are the most commonly seen amongst the ranks of soldiers. Crocodilians lack access to good smiths and metal, and so usually wear lighter armour.
Elite warriors of the Steelscale clan wield the terrifying berserker chain, a massive thick chain of crude iron, it's unpredictable swings are able to flatten foes in a single blow. Elite skirmishers from the Amber clan utilise the amber lance, a heavy javelin that has enough mass to punch a hole clean through the shield of an opposing soldier, the soldier himself and the poor guy behind him.Crocodilians are most distinct from each other by the colour of their scales, with dark dull greens and browns being the most common.Crocodilians speak the crocodilian tongue. Their dialects are the most varied amongst the major factions. Leaders and merchants may learn the Numerian tongue, but most common folk don't.
Maw of the Greats
Red Line
Maw of the Greater
Amberguild

item.title: The Last Legion
item.description:
After the Nebulans were routed off the continent following the Tyranny of the Stars, an expeditionary force was formed to chase the Nebulans back north to their homeland and destroy them forever. Relying on corpse fungus left by the Nebulans to make up for their food shortage, the Last Legion comprises a diverse mix of forces from the survivors of the invasion, all with a personal score to settle.Notable amongst them are:
Captain Hong Li Ma, captain of the town guard at The Right Claw.
Rinnie Tiderider, last survivor of Doberman squad.
Bomabomabim, brother to Rangarangarang of Canary squad.
When the Last Legion made landfall upon the Eye of the Storm, they waged a bloody and terrible war of attrition against the Nebulans with the goal of bringing about the end of their species. Even with most of their soldiers slain during the Tyranny of the Stars, the Nebulans put up fierce resistance on their home soil. Eventually after 5 long years, the Last Legion accomplished their task. Only a-fifth of those who sailed north ever came back, bodies scarred with long-term exposure to Marander Gas.

item.title: Shadows of the Nebulans
item.description:
The Shadows of the Nebulans are a group of various people from the continent of the laughing titan who chose to side with the Nebulans, conducting sabotage and helping the Nebulans scout out the continent before the invasion. They were condemned as traitors after the Tyranny of the Stars.
Curiously, despite their involvement in events leading up to the invasion, the Shadows of the Nebulans were not present for it. After the Nebulans were routed off, The Last Legion discovered their remains on the Isle of Andromeda, located between the continent of The Laughing Titan and the continent of the Eye of the Storm. They were found to have died fighting alongside The Canaries, against the Nebulans. It's not known why they were attacked, but many speculate they were either betrayed by the Nebulans and decided to go out fighting, or The Canaries persuaded them to abandon their goal and fight for the Laughing Titan instead.
Gehang was elected as a high overseer after The East-West War, and served to try and repair the damage done to the reputation of New Illuminetres during the war. About 6 months before the Tyranny of the Stars, Gehang embarked on a pilgrimage around the world. Inviting representatives from each kingdom aboard his ship, he aimed to sail around the continent as a mark of friendship and cooperation between the kingdoms. Ulysses and Basilan were aboard this voyage as representatives of the Conclave of the Steel Faeries. However, when their ship left The Left Claw for The Right Claw, they turned up a month late, missing majority of the people on board, except for Gehang, Ulysses and Basilan, and a handful of Numerian sailors. The story told then was that there had been a freak storm that had washed away most of the crew, and the situation was a huge scandal. With hindsight, many believe the ship was abducted by the Nebulans, and this was when Gehang, Ulysses and Basilan struck a deal to work with the Nebulans in their conquest of the continent.
Gehang is suspected to be the one responsible for rallying the remaining disillusioned fanatics of New Illuminetres under his banner, sending Thaddeus and the false fishermen to incite chaos in The Right Claw to stop the continent from discovering the Nebulans before the invasion occured. He is also believed to be the one originally responsible for the plot to capture ships off the northern coast and use them as Trojan horses to sneak the Nebulans past the defences of The Citadel.Gehang's exact motivation for siding with the Nebulans remains unknown, but many theorise he did it to cut a deal, having the Nebulans agree to spare the Numerians in exchange for conquering the rest of the continent. It's believed he is the reason the Numerians were spared the brunt of the invasion.
His body was found alongside his personal paladin guards on the Isle of Andromeda.
Thaddeus was a former paladin during The East-West War, rumoured to have served alongside Alexander Godfrey. Decades later, he was the one in charge of leading a band of numerian fanatics under order from Gehang Mannlicher to sow chaos in The Right Claw and sabotage investigations that could jeopardise the Nebulan war plans. Having received word of a group of numerian fishermen headed for the Right Claw, Thaddeus used the authority of Gehang to delay them, allowing his fanatics to go in posing as the fishermen. Responsible for the Insurrection at the Claw, Thaddeus would eventually meet his end in a confrontation with Canary squad and his old battle brother, Alexander Godfrey, during the the burning of the Claw. He was slain by the spear of Fregsworth of the Canary squad, who gave his life in the process.
A native Aquatine, Utari was a town guard in The Right Claw, playing a pivotal role in the fanatic's plans during the Insurrection at the Claw. She was the one responsible for the shooting of a fanatic turncoat, alongside passing information on where to source gunpowder ingredients to the fanatics. Furthermore, she was the one who hired Doberman squad and lured them into an ambush as a wider ploy to cripple the Blue Hounds and prevent their investigation into the Nebulans' activities.
Due to Canary squad's investigations, she was eventually outed and arrested. Shortly after The Canaries left to sail north, she was executed for treason.
Her motivations for aiding New Illuminetres fanatics despite being born an Aquatine citizen remains somewhat muddled. When questioned, her parents said they had disowned her after her failures in the trade exams. It's believed she was found and indoctrinated by Numerian fanatics, who then used her to infiltrate the guards at the Right Claw.
Former members of the powder corps in the Conclave of the Steel Faeries, steel faery Ulysses and his pixie Basilan were exceptional soldiers, masters of alchemy and martial arts. Strikingly, Ulysses always wears a silver mask covering the left half of his face which is horrifically disfigured, whilst Basilan has his two right wings replaced with silver prosthetics. Furthermore, Ulysses' eyes have no irises. The duo were originally exiles who earned their way back into the conclave due to their incredible prowess. Although they served for distinction for many years, their true loyalties were revealed during the months leading up to the Tyranny of the Stars.
The two were part of the cursed voyage by Gehang Mannlicher, and were also part of the security detail of the faery trade ship, the Grey Manta, which was attacked at sea and ran aground. It's believed they assisted the Nebulans in attacking the Grey Manta, and are also the ones who provided the New Illuminetres fanatics with the knowledge to make lesser gunpowder for their attacks during the Insurrection at the Claw.
When the Tyranny of the Stars began, a small number of Nebulan ships were outfitted with gunpowder cannons, believed to have been made for them by the duo.
Their motivations are ultimately unknown, but it's believed that they were exiled from the Conclave of the Steel Faeries due to their physical disabilities, leading them to plot their revenge and collude with the Nebulans to destroy The Citadel. They are believed to be responsible for the Nebulans targeting The Citadel at the very start of the war.
Like the others, Ulysses and Basilan were found dead on the Isle of Andromeda, apparently having died fighting the Nebulans.Besides the traitor faery and pixie and fanatics, it's also believed Gehang used his wealth to hire various mercenary groups and ships to aid in his plots. Whether these mercenaries knew they were aiding the conquest of the continent remains a matter of debate.

item.title: The Canaries
item.description:
This group of scouts was awarded the name of "The Canaries" posthumously, after they gave their lives to bring valuable intel and forewarning of the Nebulan invasion. Their efforts contributed to The Right Claw's proper defence and holdout against the Nebulans, as well as allowing the Conclave of the Steel Faeries to synthesis a counter to Stardust earlier, preventing further destruction and death. Much of their story remains unknown as they perished on the Isle of Andromeda, far north of the continent. Strangely, they were found to have died fighting alongside the Shadows of the Nebulans against the invaders. Many speculate the two opposing parties found common ground in the end. Their remains were only discovered by The Last Legion after the Nebulans had already been repelled.
Most of the accounts about the Canaries come from Captain Hong Li Ma, captain of the town guards in the Right Claw, as well as various townsfolk who survived the invasion. After the war, Captain Li Ma set up a memorial to them in the town, marked by a distinctive blue oak sapling, a small beacon of hope in the wasteland of Marander Gas.
Canary squad is a reconnaissance squad under the larger mercenary company, the Blue Hounds. A team of 5 various greenhorns and their handler Charlie, Canary squad was formed less than a month before the Tyranny of the Stars in order to help investigate missing ships off the coast of The Right Claw.
Playing a major role in uncovering the Numerian fisherman conspiracy during the Insurrection at the Claw, they helped uncover traitor guardswomen Utari Sanyaja as an agent of the Shadows of the Nebulans. In addition, they discovered an encampment outside the town being used as storage for materials to create lesser gunpowder for the New Illuminetres fanatics and slew their leader, Thaddeus, in combat during the burning of the Claw.
After the dust settled, Canary squad sailed north with the rest of the Canaries, investigating clues left behind by the fanatics. Days before the Nebulan Invasion, two ravens were sent by the Canaries. One was sent to The Right Claw, warning of imminent invasion by a massive fleet of foreign creatures, capable of secreting a deadly mist. Because of this, The Right Claw remains one of the few places properly prepared for the invasion. Without the Canaries' warning, the coastal town would likely have been destroyed in the first night of the invasion. The second was sent to The Citadel, with detailed plans of the Nebulans' attack plans, crucially warning of a Nebulan ploy to use the missing ships as a Trojan horse to weaken the Citadel's defences. Alongside this message, Canary squad had also managed to send a small container containing a sample of Stardust. This container, named "The Cage of the Stars" remains the only known vessel able to contain Stardust. Thanks to their intel, the Citadel was able to foil the Nebulan's Trojan horse plans, and begin research on Stardust early, leading to the reaction turning Stardust into Marander Gas being discovered much earlier. Strangely, a blue acorn was also sent with the raven, but the significance of this is not known. The acorn was later planted at their memorial site in The Right Claw.Despite their contributions, Canary squad never returned to the continent. It's believed they gave their lives to gather the information they sent. The squad consisted of:
A steel faery, Fregsworth is described as a timid person, often trying to hide his faery wings under a cloak. He exiled himself from the Citadel, joining Canary squad in hopes of finding his pixie, Llyod, who had also left. Despite his shy nature and propensity to default to authority, Fregsworth would show bravery in the moments where it mattered most. During The Burning of the Claw, Fregsworth gave his life to slay Thaddeus, leader of the New Illuminetres fanatics.
A steel pixie, Llyod was originally bonded to Fregsworth. Most describe him as being rather obnoxious and difficult to work with, as well as having a strange accent. The Conclave of the Steel Faeries report him as a problematic individual who sought to break the nature of faery-pixie relationships, seeking independence for pixies alone. Despite this, he played an important role in the investigation into gunpowder production by the New Illuminetres fanatics, and saved the other members of Canary squad on occasion using his mastery over light. After Fregsworth's death, he was bonded to Zodiac.A Wingardian from the sands of the south, Wonnie joined Canary squad as a way of furthering his medical research. Having been taught by a unorthodox doctor, he showed a somewhat concerning interest in the brewing of different drugs and medicines, as well as the different anatomy of the various other races. Reported to have been absorbed in investigating a strange substance left by his mentor, Wonnie was an eccentric but valuable member of the squad.
A young Numerian boy who had apparently lied about his age to get onto the squad, Jacob was an optimistic boy, an avid bookworm and a believer in New Illuminetres. Curious to a fault, Jacob left home and joined Canary squad to explore the world. He would face the ugly side of his faith directly during the Insurrection at the Claw. Local firekeeper in the Right Claw, Renly Smith, laments that he was too young to be partaking in his dangerous mission, but admits he was brave for one facing such horrors at such an age.
A crocodilian of the Steelscale Clan, Rangarangarang joined Canary squad in the hopes of testing and proving himself, independent of his family. A boisterous fellow, he is described as direct and strange, known to argue at length over 2 gold pieces. Also well known is his large appetite for alcohol, often seen hauling around egregious amounts of beer, and rumoured to have participated in a drinking competition with goblins. Though rough around the edges, his heart was in the right place.A young Aquatine citizen, Kara set out to join Canary squad to widen her world view and seek adventure. Her parents describe her to be chasing after her mentor, who vanished trying to investigate the Red Oaks for a way to further the agriculture of the empire. A person chasing the shadows of her past, Kara started as an inexperienced wide-eyed rookie, but proved herself in her actions defending and protecting the continent. It's rumoured the blue acorn was sent by her.
A scout of the steel faeries' powder corps, Zodiac lost his pixie in combat and was brought aboard Canary squad after Fregsworth death to bond with Llyod. Having limited interactions with the people of the Right Claw, his powder corps records detail him as a straight-laced soldier, obedient and unquestioning to a fault. He served well, laying down his life on the Isle of Andromeda alongside the rest of Canary Squad.The handler for Canary squad, Charlie is the only member who had been working in the Blue Hounds before the formation of Canary squad. Described as an industrious fellow, he is most often seen in the town post office collating intel and writing letters begging the Blue Hounds higher ups for more resources. At times, townsfolk also see him being dragged out of town by the rest of his squad during investigations, despite being a non-combatant himself.
Doberman squad is a combat squad of 4 crocodilians under the larger Blue Hounds mercenary company. Operating independently of a handler, Doberman squad was hired by the traitor guardswoman Utari Sanjaya to destroy a bandit camp near the Right Claw that doesn't exist. As part of the greater ploy by the New Illuminetres fanatics to weaken Blue Hounds and stop their investigation into the missing vessels, Doberman squad was ambushed enroute, suffering one killed and one grievously wounded. Despite their losses, Doberman squad killed their ambushers, and proceeded to aid in the takedown of the fanatics during the burning of the Claw, and joining Canary squad when they sailed north. Like Canary squad, Doberman squad was killed on the Isle of Andromeda getting information to the continent. Their members are:
Described to be freakishly large, even for a female crocodilian, Acrila is the leader of Doberman squad. A berserker of the Steelscale Clan, Acrila wields their terrifying Berserker Chain, embodying the larger than life rowdiness and ferocity of a berserker. Many accounts detail her brushing off serious injuries that would put down lesser beings, and revelling in the heat of battle.The second in command of Doberman squad and veteran of numerous missions, Killian is described as a stoic person, having lost an eye during his various battles in service of the Redclaw clan. Representing the discipline to Acrila's fury, he was often seen going over maps and plans with the local guards.
A youngblood from the Steelscale Clan, Yoholk was a promising warrior getting real battle experience working for Doberman squad. He gave his life saving Acrila from a hail of arbalest bolts when the squad was ambushed by the fanatics.Another youngblood, this time from the Amberclan, Rinnie was an elite lance thrower. She suffered grevious injuries during the ambush by the fanatics and was left behind to recover when the Canaries sailed north. She is the only surviving member of Doberman squad.
Elite scouts from the powder corps of the Conclave of the Steel Faeries, steel faery Pollie Usted and her pixie Felixanderilyacobrutusimoniago the twelfth (real name of Iago) were sent to the Right Claw to investigate the missing faery trade ship, the Grey Manta. An elusive duo, their exact involvement in the events at the Claw remains unknown. Their records within the Citadel details them as hailing from the prestigious House Ourobous, the latest in a long line of famous warriors. Skilled with musket, gunpowder and stealth alike, the duo accompanied Canary squad when they sailed north, and likewise did not return.
A former Numerian paladin in The East-West War, Alexander has since turned to mercenary work. Despite his past allegiances to the fanatics of New Illuminetres, he helped quell the uprising during the burning of the Claw, and accompanied Canary squad on their voyage north. Local firekeeper Renly Smith describes him as a grizzled old man with a gaze that seemed to stretch until the end of the world. He is rumoured to be former comrades in arms with Thaddeus, leader of the fanatics, the two meeting again on opposite sides of the conflict.
Headed by Captain Yacob Said, these Wingardian marines were sent to the Right Claw aboard the warship, Kelissa, in order to investigate missing Wingardian trade vessels. Highly disciplined and wielding their distinctive falces, they were the first target of the fanatics when the Kelissa was bombed and rendered unseaworthy. Despite this, they proved instrumental in helping repel the fanatics during the the burning of the Claw, and accompanied Canary squad aboard a borrowed Aquatine patrol boat, the Lance of Urumi, as an armed escort when they sailed north.

item.title: Tyranny of the Stars
item.description:
The night of 21st July 1214 marks the start of the Nebulan invasion of the continent that would change it forever. The following is a timeline of events during the invasion, now termed "The tyranny of the Stars". The Nebulans sent about 250000 soldiers, embarked upon over 1000 warships. A race of lanky, purple-skinned humanoids, the Nebulans wield strange, glowing crystal weapons and secrete Stardust. Stardust is a shimmering like mist with terrifying properties, killing any non-Nebulan creature within seconds. It cannot be displaced by wind or be contained by regular containers. Upon first contact, the people of the continent had no way to fight against it.
Thanks to information sent by The Canaries, the general war plan of the Nebulans was made known before their invasion. First, the Nebulans aimed to destroy the Aquatine Empire first, eliminating the largest army on the continent and crippling food supply. Simultaneously, they aimed to destroy the Conclave of the Steel Faeries, for fear that the pixies may engineer a way to counter Stardust.
The very first settlement to come under attack, a fleet of almost 500 ships landed near the north-eastern shore of the continent. Having be forewarned by The Canaries, Captain Li Ma, head of the local guard had organised a proper defence, evacuating civilians, preparing food stockpiles, fortifications and scattering debris in the sea surrounding the claw to impede the incoming ships. With the Aquatine Empire's second legion already garrisoned there due to the Insurrection at the Claw, the defenders were able to hold out, attempting to delay melee combat for as long as possible. However, the rest of the empire did not heed The Canaries or Captain Li Ma's warnings. The attack commenced on the night of 21st July 1214, but by the morning, the Claw was the only place on the north-eastern shores not covered in shimmering mist.
Months before the invasion, various ships had been disappearing off the northern coastline. Shortly after the invasion of the Claw, the missing ships arrive at the Citadel in an attempt to launch a Trojan horse attack. Having received warning from The Canaries, the Citadel's heavy cannons fire on the fleet before they have the chance to get close. Following this failure, the rest of the Nebulan fleet began a protracted siege. The Citadel's defences prove formidable, and the Nebulans would be stuck attempting to breach its walls for the remainder of the war. Forces from the Kingdom of Numeria attempted to help, but were no match for the Nebulan's Stardust.
As news of the Nebulan threat sweeps through the empire, a mass panic began. Millions of citizens flooded south, creating a massive humanitarian crisis. The Imperial legions, once the hallmark of human military might, find themselves powerless against the Nebulans' Stardust. The empire attempts to adapt away from their conventional tactics, focusing on defensive forts and horse archers to better counter this new threat. Whilst these measures help, they are nowhere near enough to turn the tide. By 19th August 1214, almost all of the Empire's lands have fallen. Only The Right Claw and the mighty walls of the capital, Stonebasin, continue to hold out. But with food reserves slowly dwindling and the survivable area of each settlement being chipped away each day as stardust is catapulted over the walls, their days are numbered. Emperor Marcus Callier the First is slain during the defense of Stonebasin, alongside his heir, princess Mikayla Callier.
After the Aquatine Empire has all but shattered, the Nebulans turn their attention to the other factions. Curiously, the Kingdom of Numeria remains untouched. As the Nebulans invade the Crocodilian islands, they find them already evacuated, with only a few berserkers of the Steelscale Clan remaining to test their mettle against this new threat. They last impressively long within the stardust, ripping and tearing, but eventually they all fall. When the Nebulan fleet attempts to invade Snake's Throat, the smaller but more agile Wingardian navy conducts harassing attacks to disrupt them. On land, the Wingard Collective evacuate their people and deny the Nebulans a pitched engagement, making use of their familiarity of their home terrain to delay them in skirmishes. Despite this, the Nebulans eventually start claiming the southern coastlines, and force the Wingardians further inland, towards Numerian land.
As the Aquatine Empire crumbles and the Nebulan fleet begins moving down the eastern coast, the wealthy elites of Sonostra promptly abandon their city, fleeing with their mercenary soldiers to the mainland. The city is left in disarray, and most people try to flee as well. But with most ships being sent to war, many are left stranded, too poor to bribe their way aboard the few available vessels. Many die attempting to swim to the mainland, and many more die when the stardust descends upon the city.
On 3rd September 1214, news comes from the scientists of the Citadel: Thanks to the sample of stardust sent in advance by The Canaries, a counter has been engineered to stardust. A chemical process can be done quickly by the Pixies to convert Stardust into Marander Gas. Marander Gas is still toxic to most living beings, but Crocodilians are immune to it, and protective breathing apparatus can be made to filter it, unlike Stardust. With this knowledge, a coalition is rapidly formed amongst the surviving factions. The Faeries and Pixies convert Stardust into Marander Gas, whilst the crocodilians and humans with hastily made breathing equipment act as frontline soldiers. This new coalition army launches a series of counter attacks against the Nebulans, and see much initial success. The Nebulan's stardust is turned against them, and without protection of their own against the Marander gas, they are rapidly driven back by the coalition. The situation is not all good news, as while Marander Gas can be broken down into safe components, the process is long and laborious, leaving most of the conquered lands still uninhabitable.
On 15th December 1214, the last of the Nebulans are chased off the continent. The Right Claw, Stonebasin and The Citadel are relieved of their sieges, and the coalition begins to plan their next move. All the surviving leaders agree on one thing: The Nebulans cannot be allowed to return. With the Wingardian and Numerian navy still somewhat intact, as well as numerous captured Nebulan ships, the coalition form an expeditionary force, The Last Legion. With the Aquatine lands covered in toxic Marander Gas, the continent suffers a massive food shortage. The Nebulans brought with them a fungus, capable of surviving Stardust and growing off of corpses. With no shortage of bodies following the devastation, the coalition resorts to this grim source of sustenance for their expeditionary army.
As the Last Legion chases the Nebulans back North, they pass the Isle of Andromeda, discovering the remains of The Canaries and Shadows of the Nebulans. Upon sailing further north, they come across the home continent of the Nebulans, the Eye of the Storm. With long nights and an extensive underground cave system, the Last Legion endures on their arduous task with grim determination: The genocide of the Nebulan species. Conditions are horrible, and the Last Legion endures starvation, disease and atrocity alike. After 5 long years, their duty is complete.
Although the Nebulans were defeated, the continent is ruined. The once fertile lands of the Aquatine Empire are no more, alongside the empire itself. Of the 60 million Aquatine humans, only 15 million survive, with more dying everyday to starvation and disease. Whilst the second legion of the empire manage to survive by holding out in The Right Claw, most chose to join The Last Legion to seek revenge. The only semblance of governance and military of the Aquatine Empire comes from the few ruling mayors and generals who managed to survive in Stonebasin. Now, the Aquatines are in a dire sorry state, living as refugees in the Numerian and Wingardian lands, a far cry from their dominance before the war.
The Numerians were the least affected, with 24 out of 30 million surviving. Although the Numerians claim not to know why the Nebulans avoided targeting them, many accuse them of collaborating with the Nebulans, especially after the actions of the Shadows of the Nebulans come to light, where New Illuminetres fanatics seemingly carried out the bidding of the Nebulans to prepare for their invasion. Despite this, the Numerian people still suffer greatly, with many dying of famine and the overcrowding of refugees in their lands. The Wingardians managed to mitigate their losses somewhat by denying the Nebulans a direct confrontation, but still end up with only 7 out of 10 million of their population surviving. Quick to adapt, they set up new settlements in the desert, but ultimately still feel the massive manpower drain and severe food shortage.The Conclave of the steel faeries saw half of their population of 1.5 million faeries and pixies dead, with most dying defending the Citadel or fighting as part of the coalition army. The Citadel remains largely intact, and faery society is still somewhat stable. But, with a severe pixie shortage after the war, they are left with limited ability to cleanse the land of Marander Gas or leverage their technology for rebuilding.The Crocodilians see only 3 million of their original 7 million population surviving. Being immune to Marander Gas, the coalition relied heavily on them as soldiers for the war, with many dying fighting the Nebulans and more sent to pursue them as part of the Last Legion. Thanks to their immunity to Marander Gas, the crocodilians are the few who avoid the overcrowding of refugees by settling back in their original islands and parts of the now destroyed Aquatine Empire. However, they are still heavily affected by the food crisis.The continent will never be the same again, and with the common enemy gone, the factions begin to turn on each other again. Accusations are leveraged against the Numerians for cooperating with the invaders, people lament the faeries for not doing more to cleanse the Marander Gas, and hateful rhetoric is directed at the refugees of the Aquatine Empire for taking up valuable resources. It will likely take centuries, maybe even millennia before things can even start to go back to the way it was...

item.title: Character Sheet & Stats
item.description:
Self-explanatory. When health reaches 0, you enter a moment of mortality.
Additional health on top of your health bar that gets depleted first. Temporary health cannot be restored, and is lost on long rest. Temporary health is considered as regular health for all calculations, such as for reaper's grace.Gaining more temporary health when you already have some will override your existing value if the new value is greater. If it isn't, then nothing happens.
Represents protection from damage. Armour is mostly gained through equipment. In some popular ttrpgs, such as DND, armour is used to determine if an attack roll will hit, but here that role is fulfilled by Melee Defence and Ranged Defence.
Instead, armour reduces damage once you are hit: Your armour value is subtracted from the incoming damage. More detailed calculation details and how armour interacts with penetration and blunt force is discussed in Damage Calculations.
Shamelessly ripped off from darkest dungeon. When stress reaches max, it reduces to 0 and you suffer a temporary insanity until 2 long rests have passed.Stress accumulates from reaching critical health, having allies die, failing critically and generally whenever something bad happens.Stress is reduced when resting, winning tough fights, succeeding critically and generally whenever something good happens.Veterancy is a stat mainly used to cap certain abilities as a balancing method. It is calculated by your level/3, rounded up. Levels 0 - 3: Veterancy 1 Levels 4 - 6: Veterancy 2 Levels 7 - 9: Veterancy 3Core stats start from an average of 0, and are added directly as modifiers to skill checks. Due to the lack of spellcasting, mental stats are not as prevalent, hence during character creation, your stat point pool is split into two: physical and mental.Combat: Important for strength based weapons like axes and bows. Usually used to determine additional blunt force trauma damage, useful against armour. Roleplay: Used for activities requiring burst power. (e.g. lifting, throwing, smashing)Combat: Important for dexterity based weapons like swords. Usually used to determine additional defences, helping survivability. Roleplay: Used for activities requiring speed and agility. (e.g. running, acrobatics, pickpocketing)Combat: Important for increasing health and equipment capacity. Roleplay: Used for activities requiring sustained power or resisting effects. (e.g. negating poison, carrying heavy loads for a long time)Roleplay: Used for technical and scholarly knowledge. (e.g. recalling history, brewing chemicals, performing first aid)Roleplay: Used for intuition and observation. (e.g. scouting, figuring out lies, finding patterns) Roleplay: Used for social interactions. (e.g. persuading, lying, bartering)
How far you can move in a single round of combat. Default is 6m, with Faeries having 7m.
How far you can jump. Default is 2m, with Faeries having 4m.
Initiative determines who goes first during the zig-zag cycle of combat.
By default, initiative is calculated by a d20 + dexterity, but Faeries have an additional +2 initiative, and being in light load allows you to double your dexterity modifier.The value the enemy's melee attack roll needs to be higher than to hit. All races have a default value of 10.
The value the enemy's ranged attack roll needs to be higher than to hit. All races have a default value of 10. Crocodilians have 8.Think of your inventory as split into two different groups:
Equipment Load, which represents weapons, armour and items that are readily accessible and that you can use in combat.
Backpack Load, which represents items that you won't use in combat, such as treasure, food, tools etc. How much combat ready equipment you can equip. Any items you want to use in combat or secondary weapons you want to swap to count towards your equipment load. If an item is not in your equipment load, you cannot readily use it. This includes medicine and armour.Each point in endurance increases the thresholds by 2kg. Each point of negative endurance subtracts 2kg instead.The default thresholds are: Low load (<10kg): +1m movement speed and jump distance, and...
Add your dexterity score as melee defense (capped by your Veterancy).
Add your dexterity score as ranged defense (capped by your Veterancy). Add your dexterity score as initiative. Medium load (>=10, <20kg): You get no penalties or benefits. High load (>=20, <30kg): -1m movement speed. -1m jump distance. -2 initiative.
Take +1 blunt force trauma every level when taking fall damage. Overloaded (>=30, <40kg): -2m movement speed. -2m jump distance. -4 initiative -1 to strength and dexterity.
Take +2 blunt force trauma every level when taking fall damage. Rock Cosplay(>=40kg): Your movement speed is capped to 1m You cannot jump. You always go last in initiative. Strength and Dexterity are set to -4.
Take +3 blunt force trauma every level when taking fall damage.
Crocodilians have different thresholds.
How much you can carry in total. Default is 70kg, with each point of endurance adding 5kg. Each point of negative endurance subtracts 5kg instead. Your equipment load counts towards your carrying capacity.Carrying capacity cannot go below the maximum threshold of your equipment load.Going overweight will result in disadvantage on all rolls.
Backpack load is simply your carrying capacity - equipment load. It represents all the stuff you are carrying that is not in your equipment load. You cannot access your backpack items readily during combat.
Your characters will usually jettison their backpacks at the start of combat. Choosing to fight with your backpack on will result in your backpack weight being added to your equipment load.
Weapon proficiencies determine which weapons you can wield properly.
Traits are perks with specific functions. You get them every level up.Paths are lifestyles your character chooses that influence their gameplay. You get to choose a path at level 3, which then levels up every subsequent 3rd level. See the path folder under playable races for more details.
Skills are a generic representation of what your character specialises in beyond their generic Core Stats. They are split into 2 types: Major: Major skills are those that are more likely to be used/useful, or have some crafting system tied to them. Minor: Minor skills are niche skills that are less likely to be used and have no systems tied to them. When do these skills come into play? They are used in skill checks, where you make a d20 roll with your skill and core stat modifiers against a difficulty class specified by the GM. For instance: GM asks: "Make a scouting check with dexterity, DC15". This means to roll a d20 with your dexterity and scouting skill added as modifiers against a target of 15. You ask: "Can I use my acrobatics with dexterity to avoid the trap?" When doing these skill checks, you are restricted to only using 1 skill and 1 core stat at a time. If you lack the appropriate skill to achieve something, you may be asked to roll with disadvantage, roll against a higher DC or not be allowed to roll at all. Skills start at 1 and go up to a maximum of 3. Note that 1 is not the "minimum", not having the skill at all is the "minimum". Acrobatics Used to perform acts of agility, like jumping from rooftops, dodging traps etc. Alchemy
Allows you to do Alchemy, creating your own customised potions and medicine. Armour-Smithing
Allows you to do Armour Smithing, creating your own customised armour pieces. Bartering Used in haggling, getting better trade deals etc. Cooking Used to cook better meals that grant bonuses to the party. Deception Used to lie. Fishing
Used to obtain food in the appropriate environment. Foraging
Used to obtain food/herbs in the appropriate environment. Gunpowder Chemistry
Allows you to do Gunpowder Chemistry, creating your own customised gunpowder consumables. Hunting
Used to obtain food by hunting animals. Intimidation Used to align people to your views and perspectives in an aggressive and not-nice manner. Medicine Used in healing and curing ailments. Night Vision
Allows you to see further in dark conditions, see lighting rules. Persuasion Used to align people to your views and perspectives in a calm and nice manner. Riding Used in mounted combat and training horses faster. Sailing Used when acting as captain of a ship. Scouting Used for detecting oddities, finding clues or enemies. Stealth Used for sneaking around, hiding things. Swimming
Used for movement in water. Weapon-Smithing
Allows you to do Weapon Smithing, creating your own customised weapons and ammunition. Art Brewing Carpentry Farming Fire making High class mannerism Low class mannerism Literacy Speaking Aquatine Tongue Numerian Tongue Crocodilian Tongue Wingardian Tongue Writing Aquatine Script Numerian Script Crocodilian Script Wingardian Script Lockpicking Mining Performance Dance Music Speech Ranching Scholarship Stonemasonry Tailoring
