item.title: Horse Rules
item.description:
A word of caution: Horseback combat can be a bit complicated, so make sure you are familiar with the base game mechanics first, especially concerning view cones.
A horse has numerous stats that influence its performance. Many of these are shared with normal characters and can be viewed at Character Sheet & Stats. The stats unique to horses/work differently for horses are listed below:
A horse's initiative acts as a bonus/malus to their rider's initiative.Influences how likely a horse is to follow orders.How much can a horse carry directly.How hard a horse can hit during charge attacks.How much a horse can change its course when charging.A horse takes up 2m by 2m space. A rider is considered to be on top of the horse. Any attack that can reach the horse can also reach the rider. A horse has a default view cone of 90 degrees. A rider shares the same view cone as the horse.
Normally your view cone can be rotated freely at any time, so long as it fits the current view cone restrictions. On horseback, you cannot rotate your view cone freely. Horses need 1m movement speed to rotate their view cone by 45 degrees, and once your turn ends your view cone is stuck in that position until your next turn. This act of rotating your view cone does not trigger opportunity attacks.
On horseback, you still inflict but are not affected by view cone restrictions.Rotating your view cone by 45 degrees takes 1m of movement speed. You can only move directly forwards or backwards with reference to your view cone.Moving backwards costs twice the movement speed. Horses can only jump forwards.Riders can mount/dismount with a regular action + all remaining movement speed. Horses can unlock new forms of movement during training.When attacking a rider, you can choose to target either rider or horse. Targeting the horse will use the horse's stats and defenses for calculations.
A weapon move that successfully moves the rider will knock them off, causing them to fall prone. Where they fall will depend on terrain, but usually they will fall in the direction they were moved.
Horses can be moved.A successful grappling attempt against the rider will result in the rider being dragged off the horse. The rider will still be standing, but be locked in a grapple with the attacker. Where they dismount depends on the attacker and available space. Horses cannot be grappled.
Opportunity or zoning attacks that hit the horse/rider do not remove their movement speed.When attacking as a rider, you can use most of the weapon moves as normal, however weapon moves that also move you cannot be used normally.Horses cannot act independently of their rider beyond some simple circumstances. A horse's actions will use the rider's action resources.You may choose to charge in one of 8 directions on a square grid (+ and x) when riding a horse. Charging will use up all your remaining movement speed and and allow the horse to move twice that movement. You must move the entire distance when charging, you cannot stop early. Picture the horse's charge distance split into two equal halves, called the "build up" and the "slow down".
The build up is the first half of the charge movement, when Charge Force builds up. Imagine this as the horse gaining acceleration, reaching top speed at the end of the build up phase.
The slow down is the latter half of the charge movement, when Charge Force depletes. Imagine this as the horse slowing down to a safe speed after charging.
Every 3m travelled during The Build Up, you add your horse's charge acceleration to the total charge force.
Every 3m travelled during The Slow Down, you remove your horse's charge acceleration from the total charge force These intervals are 3m travelled on the map, not 3m movement speed expended by the horse.When charging, there are two forms of damage you can do:
If there are enemies in your charge path, you will run them over with the following rules: Your horse will be considered to have impacted the enemy when they are 1m away. (i.e. adjacent to the horse)
DC for the run over status is determined by DC 10 + charge force built up at the moment of impact. Your horse deals its built up charge force as blunt force trauma to run over enemies.
If an enemy succeeds their save against the run over check, they will stop the rest of your charge at the point of impact, reflecting the run over blunt force trauma onto the horse. If an enemy fails their save instead, you will pass through them and carry on the rest of the charge.
You can use any melee weapon move on horseback and it will grant you the horse's built up charge force as damage, hit chance and DC if the move has a status. The target must still fit in your view cone during the charge. The exception is the on foot charge action, which cannot be done. Ranged attacks do not gain this bonus.
When charging, any enemy opportunity or zoning attacks against you or your horse will gain your Weapon Charge bonuses.Each point of charge manoeuvrability allows you to make a 45 degree turn at any point in your charge. At the start of your charge, you can trade half of your charge acceleration for +1 charge manoeuvrability, up to twice.You can use actions at any point in the charge. Charging can be used as a mobility tool, not just for damage.The higher a horse's temperament, the more likely it is to obey your commands. A temperament check is rolled as such: Roll a d20 and add your horse's temperance + your riding skill against the DC of the check. Horses roll their temperament checks during the following situations: Having a charge stopped prematurely: Happens when stopped by terrain or by enemies. DC 10 + charge force built up by the horse. Rider being dismounted: DC 20. Horse is under half health: Temperament check is triggered at the start of the turn. DC 10. Horses have a tiered system of skills. You unlock skills one at a time. Each tier of skills requires a certain number of skills from the tier below to be unlocked before they can be trained.Horses can be trained during rests by spending time units. How much time a skill requires differs from skill to skill and is listed on the skill. This time is also reduced by the level of your riding skill. (i.e. A trainer with 3 riding skill will take 3 less time units when training a skill.)A horse's carrying capacity indicates how heavy the rider can be when riding. This is calculated by the sum of:
The rider's equipment load and backpack load.
During combat, you can eject your backpack to remove your backpack load from the calculations, just like on foot. The rider's race's weight. The horse's equipment. Going overweight will cut the horse's movement speed in half and remove their access to their skills.Going over twice the weight limit will result in the horse being unable to move.When pulling a cart, a horse will multiply it's carrying capacity by the cart's modifier. Horses cannot be ridden into battle when pulling a cart. Multiple horses can pull the same cart, adding their carrying capacities together.Carts do not count towards a horse's equipment weight.Horses need food every long rest like regular characters and can suffer the same penalties if they don't eat enough.
Horses can eat raw grain or rice and gain the full nutrition. Horses cannot eat meat or fish.If the environment allows, horses can simply graze instead of needing to be fed.

item.title: Pixie Masteries
item.description:
Pixie traits work differently than normal traits. When a pixie gets to choose a trait, they may choose to evolve any one mastery. Evolving the same mastery multiple times will unlock higher tier effects. Tier effects do not stack with previous tiers.At the final tier of mastery, you can spend a focus point to perform a pixie revelation. Revelations can be activated at anytime without an action, even during the enemy's turn.Only 1 offensive mastery and 1 utility mastery can be active at any 1 time. This does not apply to the skill gain from the masteries.Skill totals cannot go above 3. If not stated otherwise, all effects use the normal saving throw DC of 10 + your pixie's intelligence, which is usually 5 + your veterancy.The acute study of materials has also yielded acute ways to destroy them. Pixie chemists studying acid are able to create finely tuned particles that weaken or dissolve enemy armour whilst leaving the blades of their allies intact. Add +1 penetration to your weapon attacks. You can spend a focus point to double the effect for 1 turn. Gain +1 chemistry(acid) skill. Add +2 penetration to your weapon attacks. You can spend a focus point to double the effect for 2 turns. Gain +2 chemistry(acid) skill.
Spend a focus point to gain a Revelation of Null. Add +2 penetration to your weapon attacks. You can spend a focus point to double the effect for 3 turns. Gain +3 chemistry(acid) skill. The peak of acid engineering comes in the null acid, able to dissolve through metal as though it wasn't there to begin with. Coat your weapon with a shimmering mist of null acid, allowing your next successful attack to: Ignore armour. Ignore the melee defense bonuses from the target's weapons. Damage the target's weapon(s) beyond use. If an attack would successfully hit you, you may choose to damage the incoming weapon beyond use to nullify the attack, removing the coating in the process. The coating is limited to 1 use. The coating is not visible without a perception check. The coating lasts for 1 hour. The oldest experiment in the world, fire-making, still bears relevance as the ages advance. An essential part of life often taken for granted, pixies harness the use of fire for more than just cooking or warmth.
Inflict burning(1) on hit. Limited to once a turn. You can spend a focus point to double the effect and make the DC expert level for 1 turn. Gain +1 fire making skill.
Inflict burning(2) on hit. Limited to once a turn. You can spend a focus point to double the effect and make the DC expert level for 2 turns. Gain +2 fire making skill.
Spend a focus point to gain a Revelation of Ashes.
Inflict burning(2) on hit. Limited to once a turn. You can spend a focus point to double the effect and make the DC expert level for 3 turns. Gain +3 fire making skill.
Numerian fire is greenish-blue, developed to counter the heavily armoured human warriors during The War of the Meadows. Once ignited, it cannot be stopped.
Coat your weapon with a shimmering mist of potent fuel, allowing your next successful attack to ignite and inflict Numerian fire(2). The coating is limited to 1 use. The coating is not visible without a perception check. The coating lasts for 1 hour. The art of poison making is one that is ever evolving, and is also a controversial aspect of pixie experimentation. Many in the ruling council cite concerns over ethics and legality, but behind closed doors, the work continues.
Inflict poison(1) on hit. Limited to once a turn.
You can spend a focus point to inflict deadly poison(1) and make the DC expert level for 1 turn. Gain +1 chemistry(poison) skill.
Inflict poison(2) on hit. Limited to once a turn.
You can spend a focus point to inflict deadly poison(2) and make the DC expert level for 2 turns. Gain +2 chemistry(poison) skill.
Spend a focus point to gain a Revelation of Death.
Inflict poison(2) on hit. Limited to once a turn.
You can spend a focus point to inflict deadly poison(2) and make the DC expert level for 3 turns. Gain +3 chemistry(poison) skill. Neurotoxin is the magnum opus of pixie poisoners. Causing brain death in moments, the only hope for one afflicted by neurotoxin is the intervention of a master pixie.
Coat your weapon with a shimmering mist of engineered neurotoxin, allowing your next successful attack to inflict neurotoxin(5). If an attack's regular damage is completely negated by armour, the revelation will not activate. The coating is limited to 1 use. The coating is not visible without a perception check. The coating lasts for 1 hour.
Gunpowder is a relatively new invention amongst pixies, brought about after the formation of the Conclave of the Steel Faeries. Such is the power of gunpowder that many other factions try to create their own, but never to the standards that pixies are capable of.
Inflict dazed(1) on hit. Limited to once a turn. You can spend a focus point to double the effect and make the DC expert level for 1 turn. Gain +1 chemistry(powder) skill.
Inflict dazed(1) on hit. Limited to once a turn. Enemies within a 1m radius around the target are also affected. You can spend a focus point to double the effect and make the DC expert level for 2 turns. Gain +2 chemistry(powder) skill.
Spend a focus point to gain a Revelation of Thunder.
Inflict dazed(1) on hit. Limited to once a turn. Enemies within a 1m radius around the target are also affected. You can spend a focus point to double the effect and make the DC expert level for 3 turns. Gain +3 chemistry(powder) skill. With the invention of gunpowder, many faeries and pixies sought to create weapons and means to utilise it. Despite the advancement of grenades, cannons and muskets, sometimes the best way is to just use the powder straight up. Your pixie spreads a fine dust of concentrated black powder amongst the enemy, allowing you to detonate up to 4 tiles within 3m of you, dealing 2d6 blunt force trauma to those tiles.
Inflicts shellshock(1), guaranteed. The tiles do not need to be next to each other. With the increasing amount of creative ways pixies come up with to kill people came a sudden realisation amongst the leading council of faeries and pixies. And so, the school of counter mastery was born, seeking to put a lid on the growing power of the alchemists in case of a civil war. Lower all pixie effects within 2m by 1 tier. You can spend a focus point to remove 1 effect within 3m.
This acts as a free action, using your pixie's intelligence on the d20 roll.
This cures any poison, deadly poison, burning, bleeding, dazed, broken ankles or broken wrists automatically. Lower all pixie effects within 2m by 2 tiers. You can spend a focus point to gain 2 counter charges that negate effects within 3m.
Each charge lasts for 1 hour and can only negate 1 effect/count as 1 free action.
This acts as a free action, using your pixie's intelligence on the d20 roll.
This cures any poison, deadly poison, burning, bleeding, dazed, broken ankles or broken wrists automatically.
Spend a focus point to gain a Revelation of Neutrality. Lower all pixie effects within 2m by 3 tiers. You can spend a focus point to gain 3 counter charges that negate effects within 3m.
Each charge lasts for 1 hour and can only negate 1 effect/count as 1 free action.
This acts as a free action, using your pixie's intelligence on the d20 roll.
This cures any poison, deadly poison, burning, bleeding, dazed, broken ankles or broken wrists automatically. Gain +1 to: Chemistry(acid) skill. Chemistry(gunpowder) skill. Chemistry(poison) skill. Fire making skill. To destroy is easy; To build is difficult. This principle applies to how the revelations can wreak havoc in the blink of an eye, but also applies to these revelations themselves. Your pixie enters a trance of active defense, allowing you to neutralise any other revelation within 2m. The revelation has only 1 use. The neutralisation can activate automatically when another revelation activates. You may choose not to activate your revelation automatically. The trance lasts for 1 hour. This mastery is given for free. The most basic form of alchemy taught to a pixie is the ability to create light. A simple and useful reaction, light can be harnessed to achieve incredible means.
Spend a focus point to impose disadvantage on 1 attack against you or an ally within 3m. Weapon moves that attack multiple times have the entire attack affected. This is done through a bright flash of light. Gain +1 ranged weapon optimal range. Gain +1 night vision skill.
Spend a focus point to gain 2 light charges which allow you to impose disadvantage on attacks against you or an ally within 3m. This is done through a bright flash of light. Each charge only affects 1 attack. Weapon moves that attack multiple times have the entire attack affected. These light charges last for 1 hour. Gain +1 ranged weapon optimal range. Gain +2 night vision skill.
Spend a focus point to gain a Revelation of the Sun.
Spend a focus point to gain 3 light charges which allow you to impose disadvantage on attacks against you or an ally within 3m. This is done through a bright flash of light. Each charge only affects 1 attack. Weapon moves that attack multiple times have the entire attack affected. These light charges last for 1 hour. Gain +1 ranged weapon optimal range. Gain +3 night vision skill. The humble light flare, taken to its extreme, is able to turn night into day.
Drop a blinding flare in a range of 3m with a effect radius of 3m, inflicting blinded(2) on all enemies within. Through careful adjustment for your companion's retinas, this does not inflict friendly fire. This effect cannot be saved against.
Steel-making was the very first major breakthrough in pixie technology, and it was pioneered by a faery, Lady Numeria. Now, pixie smelters and smiths continuously seek to improve and create new blends of finer steel.
Spend a focus point to inflict metal plague(1) on a target within 3m. Expert level DC. Gain +1 armour. Gain +1 Smithing.
Spend a focus point to inflict metal plague(1) on two targets within 3m. Expert level DC. Gain +1 armour. Gain +2 Smithing.
Spend a focus point to gain a Revelation of Steel.
Spend a focus point to inflict metal plague(1) on three targets within 3m. Expert level DC. Gain +1 armour. Gain +3 Smithing. Trust in the surety of pixie steel. Double all allies' armour within 3m of you for 3 turns. In addition, all allies take half blunt force trauma. Pixie mist masters spend great effort learning how to make mist droplets of specialised chemicals that reflect light at just the right angles to render someone invisible.
Spend a focus point to turn invisible(1). Gain +1 ranged defence. Gain +1 stealth skill.
Spend a focus point to turn invisible(2). Gain +2 ranged defence. Gain +2 stealth skill.
Spend a focus point to gain a Revelation of Emptiness.
Spend a focus point to turn invisible(50). This lasts for 5 minutes. Gain +3 ranged defence. Gain +3 stealth skill. A faery's martial prowess, paired alongside a pixie's intense concentration, allows for a silent and unseen prowler to haunt the battlefield.
Become unknowable(2).

item.title: Statuses
item.description:
Timed statuses lose 1 stack at the end of your turn, after the related effect happens.Some statuses can be avoided using a saving throw against a difficulty class (DC for short).Saving throw calculation is given by a d20 + relevant core stat. If your saving throw is greater than the difficulty class, you avoid the status.Some statuses, such as those used by coatings, have a fixed DC value declared on their wiki page. Other statuses may have no DC value declared, or simply declare "Expert DC". For these statuses, use the below calculations:For statuses inflicted by weapons: Normal saving throw DC is given by 10 + relevant core stat of attacker + attacker weapon proficiency. Expert saving throw DC is given by 15 + relevant core stat of attacker + attacker weapon proficiency. For other statuses: Normal saving throw DC is given by 10 + relevant core stat of attacker + attacker veterancy. Expert saving throw DC is given by 15 + relevant core stat of attacker + attacker veterancy. The relevant core stat of the attacker is usually the same as the hit chance bonus of the weapon.When dealing with an area of effect, such as a pool of fire/cloud of poison, you suffer their relevant effect when entering and when ending your turn in the area. This is limited to once a turn, so repeatedly entering and leaving an area of effect on the same turn will not trigger its effects multiple times.Endurance saving throw.
If you don't take the relevant substance at least once per long rest, you gain 2 points of "addiction' exhaustion, which functions the same as regular exhaustion and stacks with it but cannot be removed through long resting unlike normal exhaustion. This "addiction" exhaustion is only removed by taking the relevant substance or by clearing the addiction. Taking the related substance will cancel the effects of addiction until the next long rest. Going two long rests without taking the relevant substance will clear the addiction. Saves start at DC10 and increases by 5 every time you use a substance over its daily safe amount. This resets on long rest. Endurance saving throw.
If a weapon attack's penetration is not greater than the target's armour (i.e. effective armour > 0), the status is not applied.
The exception is with the bloodhound trait, which has the bleed status lose 1 stack for every point of effective armour instead of being removed outright. Take 1 direct damage at the end of your turn. On reaching 6 or more stacks, lose 6 stacks and take 10 direct damage or half your health as direct damage immediately, depending on which is greater. Endurance saving throw. Become unable to see, limiting your perception to just 2m, and imposing disadvantage on all attacks. All attacks against you have advantage.Endurance saving throw. Half your movement speed, and you can no longer use any moves that move you.Endurance saving throw. Half your regular damage, penetration and blunt force trauma. Direct damage is not affected.Endurance saving throw. Take 1 direct damage per stack at the end of your turn.
Can be put out by using the free action or having someone else use the free action from you. DC 10 + 1 for every stack. A free action that fails will still remove 2 stacks. Endurance saving throw. Lose 1 armour per stack active on you.Endurance saving throw. You can now only do one type of action on your turn: Move Regular action Bonus action Endurance saving throw. Take 4 direct damage at the end of your turn. Suffer -3 to your hit chance and defenses for the duration of the poison.Strength | Dexterity saving throw. Drop your weapon on the same tile.Endurance saving throw. Being drunk has stages, lasting an hour each:
Level 1: -1 to core mental stats, Dexterity and hit chance, +1 to Strength. Level 2: All successes are rolled with complication.
Level 3: Black out, suffer the same effects of minor food poisoning. Effects are cumulative. When the timer for 1 level expires, the timer for the previous level begins.
With the big drinker trait: Effects of level 1 are doubled. Level 3 effects are replaced with: All enemy successes against you are rolled with complication. Level 3 with big drinker only lasts 1 turn. Endurance saving throw. Starts at DC10, increasing by 2 for every consecutive check. Failing the check will make you take 20% of your max health as direct damage.For every exhaustion point:
Suffer -1 to all core stats, melee defense and ranged defense. In addition, from the third exhaustion point and onwards: -5 or 25% max health, whichever is higher. This can kill you if it reduces your max health to 0. Endurance saving throw. Minor: Default DC 12 save. Your max health is reduced by 25% until your next long rest, -1 endurance. Major: Default DC 20 save. Your max health is reduced by 50% until your next long rest, -2 endurance. You may suffer stomach aches/vomiting at the DM's convenience.Strength | Dexterity saving throw. Both grappler and target are unable to move or use most weapon moves, and lose the defense bonuses from their weapons. Grappling is removed when:
One party uses a free action or has the free action used on them.
One party is moved by an outside force. Whilst grappled, both sides must have the other as a view cone restriction.
Bear in mind the initiator cannot leave the grapple freely. They must succeed in the free action or have the opponent agree to let them go. Endurance saving throw. Movement speed halved, equipment load thresholds lowered by 5kg, take 1d4 direct damage every hour.Endurance saving throw. Movement speed halved, equipment load thresholds lowered by 5kg, take 1d4 direct damage every hour.
Cannot be seen. All attacks count as flanking attacks. Enemies cannot shift their view cone to defend your attack. Enemies that know your general location can attempt to hit you with disadvantage. Invisibility is broken on performing any regular action or attack. Invisibility is broken on being damaged.
DC15 endurance saving throw. Crocodilians are immune to this status. Suffer -2 to hit chance and defenses, alongside taking 1d4 direct damage.Endurance saving throw. If you are wearing metal armour, suffer the following: Half your movement speed. Disadvantage on attacks, and attacks against you have advantage. Half your armour. Strength | Dexterity saving throw. Get moved a specified distance and direction. Being moved usually does not trigger opportunity attacks, but can trigger zoning attacks. If you are moved into a space that's already occupied, you take 1d4 blunt force trauma instead. If a character is the one occupying the space, they take the same blunt force trauma.No saving throw. Neurotoxin has several properties: Take 20% of your health or 5 direct damage at the end of your turn, depending on which is higher. The direct damage bypasses temporary health. You cannot heal. Using healing items can still confer their other positive effects, but will not give you any health. Neurotoxin stacks cannot be reduced through bonuses that reduce the stack count of negative effects.
Neurotoxin cannot be cured and will result in death, unless stopped with a revelation of neutrality. No saving throw. Numerian fire has several effects: At the end of your turn, take 1 direct damage per stack. Lose armour equivalent to the number of stacks. Numerian fire doubles in stack at the end of the turn instead of decaying. Once Numerian fire has enough stacks to nullify all your armour, you can make a DC15 Strength | Dexterity check to remove all body armour, removing all stacks of fire.
Numerian fire cannot be put out if you are not wearing armour, unless with a revelation of neutrality. If used on the environment, numerian fire spreads to a maximum of 10m. No saving throw. Become pinned, which:
Removes your ability to dash. Any weapon move that allows you to move whilst ignoring opportunity attacks now only gives incoming opportunity attacks disadvantage. Endurance saving throw. Take 2 direct damage at the end of your turn. Suffer -2 to your hit chance and defenses for the duration of the poison.Strength | Dexterity saving throw. Being prone has many properties: If on your turn, lose 3/4 of your max movement speed. Movement speed is capped at 1/4.
Attacks against you count as flanking attacks. Suffer disadvantage on all your attacks. You can only use moves with a range of 1m. You cannot use moves that move you.
This status lasts until you use a free action or someone uses the free action on you, Dexterity DC10.
Failing the free action to get up will result in the removal of this condition anyway, but the next attack against you still counts as a flanking attack.
Strength | Dexterity saving throw. Take the horse's built up charge force as blunt force trauma. Regardless of saving throw success, you cannot execute opportunity or zoning attacks against the thing running you over for the duration of the charge. On successful save: Take half the runover blunt force trauma and stop the horse's charge, reflecting the full runover blunt force trauma onto the horse.
On failure: Fall Prone and get sent flying back 1m for every 3 charge force the horse has built up. If you are moved into a space that's already occupied, you stop short and take 1d4 blunt force trauma. If a character is the one occupying the space, they take the same blunt force trauma. Endurance saving throw. Suffer -2 to your defences and -2 to hit chance.
Endurance saving throw. Lose all bonuses from your shield, cancel all shield moves in effect, and prevent you from using any shield moves until your next turn. Bucklers are not affected.
No saving throw. Nebulans are immune. Stardust deals 5 direct damage or 25% of your max health, whichever is higher.
Strength | Dexterity saving throw. Take direct damage equal to the attacker's strength modifier at the end of their turn. Your vision cone is forced to face directly away from the attacker. The condition is cancelled when you make a successful grappling move against the attacker or if the grapple is removed.Endurance saving throw. Gain disadvantage on ranged attacks and half movement speed.
Strength | Dexterity saving throw. You cannot move or use weapon moves that move you, and suffer -2 to your attacks and defenses. Status ends once you use a free action or someone uses the free action on you.Strength | Dexterity saving throw. Your weapon is restricted by something. You cannot use weapon moves. Tangled weapon is removed when:
You use a free action or has the free action used on you. You drop the weapon.
Cannot be seen. All attacks count as flanking attacks. Enemies cannot shift their view cone to defend against your attacks. Enemies that know your general location can attempt to hit you with disadvantage.
This form of invisibility can only be broken with a revelation of neutrality.You are subject to some kind of insanity. These last for 2 long rests or a duration at the GM's discretion. Hyper-fixation: In combat, you become hyper-fixated on a random target, becoming unable to attack anyone other than them. Once your target is down, you hyper-fixate on a new target. Ramblings: You ramble incoherently, making stealth impossible and gaining disadvantage in social interactions. Penitent Silence: You become voluntarily mute. Cowardice: You will never voluntarily step into range of a enemy melee weapon. Uncoordinated Speech: You can only say the opposite of what you mean. Uncoordinated Listening: You understand the opposite of anything you hear. Uncoordinated in General: Any targeted action has a 50% chance to be redirected onto you. Hallucinations: You gain a new imaginary friend. Or foe :0. Substance Abuse: Anytime you come into contact with any alcohol/drugs, you have to take them. Selective Blindness: You become unable to see a type of thing or person. Identity Theft: Adopt the mannerisms, philosophy and dress of someone else. Lucky Charm: Form an obsession with some inconvenient object, suffering disadvantage to everything if not within 5m of it. Unlucky Charm: Form an obsession with some inconvenient object, suffering disadvantage to everything if within 5m of it. Masochist: Your melee defense is set to 0. Gambler: Base all decisions on a dice roll. Naturalist: Refuse to use any metallic item. Unnaturalist: Refuse to use any non-metallic item. Duck: Become only able to say and write the word "Duck". Placebo Remodeling: Swap your lowest and highest core stats. Glare back into the Abyss: Heal up to half your health, and all other party members lose 2 stress.

item.title: Human Paths (Wingardian)
item.description:
Wingardian human paths are specific perks that unlock at levels 3. They are upgraded at levels 6 and 9. Once a perk path is chosen, you cannot take the others. The tiers do not stack with each other.Paths represent a lifestyle your character embodies. You may choose not to take a path.Between the merchant clans and the poison brewers in the Wingardian desert, there are those who practice an ancient, deadly and efficient artform, and then there are those who brew poisons. The Wingard Collective made use of light troops who specialised in toxin delivery. Known as "Sand Vipers", these troops moved quickly to outflank the enemy and spread poison amongst their ranks whilst the other elements of the army moved in for the kill.Once you choose the viper life, you are required to always be vipering. Successful flanking/stealth attacks with poison lower stress whilst going through combat without flanking increases stress. On successful flanking attacks or when attacking from stealth using poison, gain +5 DC to your poison check. Gain +1 hit chance against poisoned enemies. On successful flanking attacks or when attacking from stealth using poison, gain +5 DC to your poison check. Gain +1 hit chance and +1 damage against poisoned enemies. All poisons you use gain +5 DC. Gain +1 hit chance and +1 damage against poisoned enemies.
Gain access to Kiss of Death.
With a regular action, use a poison coating to target an enemy within 1m, dealing the direct damage the coating would have done over the course of all its turns all at once.
If the target is already poisoned, you instead consume all poison stacks active on them and deal the sum of their over-time direct damage immediately. A poison coating is not required in this case. This requires the target to be flanked or attacked from stealth. This damage is guaranteed.
With the importance of naval trade to the Wingard Collective, their marines are some of the best fighting forces on the continent. In the close confines of ship to ship combat, Wingardian marines lead their assault with a volley of javelins, before crashing into the enemy lines with primal ferocity. Once you join the marines, the marines never leave you. Lose stress when fighting naval battles. Gain stress when you spend too long away from a ship. Opportunity/Zoning attacks no longer have bonuses against you when charging. Gain +1 hit chance and damage against targets that have been struck with ranged attacks this round. Opportunity/Zoning attacks no longer have bonuses against you when charging. Gain +2 hit chance and damage against targets that have been struck with ranged attacks this round. Opportunity/Zoning attacks now have disadvantage against you when charging. Gain +3 hit chance and damage against targets that have been struck with ranged attacks this round.
Gain access to Marine Shock Tactics. Once per combat, carry forward any leftover actions/movement to your next turn. For example, if you didn't use your bonus action in round 1, you gain access to 2 bonus actions in round 2. You may choose not to do anything to effectively be able to take two turns next round. This must be actively declared on the turn you intend to carry forwards, you cannot retroactively activate it to gain resources from a previous turn.
Fortune telling is a popular tradition within the Wingard Collective. Whilst few actually believe fortune tellers can really divine the future, the practice persists due to its flamboyant and entertaining nature. Performance, deception and reading context clues are all valued skills, after all.Once you peer into the fates, you are required to follow them. Every long rest, make a prediction on what will happen the next day. If this prediction comes true, lose stress. Otherwise, gain stress. This prediction must be meaningful and not obvious. (i.e. no predictions like "I will talk to someone" or "I will eat food".). If you would fail a d20 check, roll a d6 and add it to the total score. If you would pass a d20 check, roll a d4 and subtract it from the total score. Nat 1s and 20s are not affected. If you would fail a d20 check, roll a d8 and add it to the total score. If you would pass a d20 check, roll a d4 and subtract it from the total score. Nat 1s and 20s are not affected. If you would fail a d20 check, roll a d10 and add it to the total score. If you would pass a d20 check, roll a d4 and subtract it from the total score. Nat 1s and 20s are not affected. Three times per long rest, change any succeed/fail roll into a coin flip. This includes enemy rolls. You can activate this ability on the same roll multiple times.

item.title: Crocodilian Paths
item.description:
Crocodilian paths are specific perks that unlock at levels 3. They are upgraded at levels 6 and 9. Once a perk path is chosen, you cannot take the others. The tiers do not stack with each other.Paths represent a lifestyle your character embodies. You may choose not to take a path.Berserkers represent the most fearsome warriors of the Steelscale Clan, most often seen wielding the Berserker Chain, a large and crude iron chain made to flatten a man in a single blow. A berserker seeks to meet a worthy match in battle, craving the addicting thrill of risking their life in mortal combat. Such is their bloodlust that many continue to fight even after sustaining injuries that would fell any other crocodilian.
Once you choose the berserker life, you are required to always go out in a blaze of glory when facing a Moment of Mortality. You lose stress from getting heavily wounded, and gain stress if you didn't lose at least half your health during combat. On taking damage: Gain +1 hit chance and damage on your next attack. Gain +1 Strength/Dexterity when below 25% health.
Reaper's Grace now activates as long as you have more than 1 health. On taking damage: Gain +2 hit chance and damage on your next attack. Gain +2 Strength/Dexterity when below 25% health.
Reaper's Grace now activates as long as you have more than 1 health. On taking damage: Gain +3 hit chance and damage on your next attack. Gain +3 Strength/Dexterity when below 25% health.
Reaper's Grace now activates as long as you have more than 1 health.
Gain access to the Berserker Death State. On taking fatal damage: Gain up to half your maximum health as temporary health. Gain +3 to a core stat of your choice. After taking 3 turns you die, regardless of your health.
During this "berserker death state", you may choose to activate the buffs granted by going out in a blaze of glory at anytime, but doing so will cause you to die immediately afterwards. In addition, this super turn counts towards one of your 3 turns before dying, meaning you cannot take 3 turns then go out in a blaze of glory. Many crocodilian scholars say that metal working and the advancements in medicine were the most influential discoveries the crocodilians received after making contact with the other races of the continent, but alcohol is probably the third. Drinking has become something of a way of life, and strange things often happen to those who drink.
Once you choose the alcoholic life, you are required to always be drinking. Going a long rest without alcohol or fighting whilst sober will make you gain stress. The big drinker trait is taken automatically. You are refunded a tier 1 trait of your choice if you already have big drinker prior to taking this mastery. Drinking alcohol now heals for 1d4 health.
During level 3 drunkenness, you no longer suffer from complications when succeeding. Drinking alcohol now heals for 1d6 health.
During level 2 and 3 drunkenness, you no longer suffer from complications when succeeding. Drinking alcohol now heals for 1d8 health.
You no longer suffer any downsides when drunk. When sober, you suffer downsides equivalent to regular level 2 drunkenness.
Gain access to Accidental Genius.
Once per combat, during level 3 drunkenness, turn any successful enemy melee attack against you back at the attacker. This will always hit. Alternatively, with the same restrictions, turn any failed attack you make into a success. Fishing is a staple of crocodilian culture, and the most common way to do so by far is harpooning. Many also go after larger quarries in the open seas, slowing and reeling in their prey with harpoons before finishing them with their powerful jaws. Life amongst the waves teaches crocodilians a sense of ebb and flow that translates to a flexible fighting style.Once you choose the wave harpooner life, you are required to always be wave harpooning. Spending too long away from water will make you gain stress, whilst swimming and other such aquatic activities will make you lose stress.
Thrown weapons such as Amber Lances, Javelins and Throwing Axes gain +1 optimal range. Gain +1 on swimming, fishing and stealth checks when in the water.
Thrown weapons such as Amber Lances, Javelins and Throwing Axes gain +2 optimal range. Gain +2 on swimming, fishing and stealth checks when in the water.
Thrown weapons such as Amber Lances, Javelins and Throwing Axes gain +3 optimal range. Gain advantage on swimming, fishing and stealth checks when in the water.
Gain access to Tide Rider. Gain +2 damage to your next melee attack on a successful ranged attack. Gain +2 damage to your next ranged attack on a successful melee attack. Buffs only last 1 turn.

item.title: Faery Paths
item.description:
Faery paths are specific perks that unlock at levels 3. They are upgraded at levels 6 and 9. Once a perk path is chosen, you cannot take the others. The tiers do not stack with each other.Paths represent a lifestyle your character embodies. You may choose not to take a path. Lady Numeria is the founder of the Old Numerian Empire. Revered by many faeries and pixies, her story has been twisted and exaggerated to the point where the original is no longer knowable. The only true known legacy left by her is the art of the Numerian Blades.
Once you choose Lady Numeria, you are required to always follow her example. You form an idea of what Lady Numeria is like, lose stress when you follow it and gain stress whenever you deviate from it.
Gain +1 kg to your equipment load thresholds.
When wielding a Numerian blade, gain +1m movement speed and jump distance.
Gain +2 kg to your equipment load thresholds.
When wielding a Numerian blade, gain +1m movement speed and jump distance.
Gain +3 kg to your equipment load thresholds.
When wielding a Numerian blade, gain +1m movement speed and jump distance.
Gain access to a Revelation of Her Majesty.
Gunpowder is a somewhat new invention, coming about after the formation of the Conclave of the Steel Faeries. Used in firearms and explosives, it has become a staple of the faery military. The very nature of pixies and faeries pushes them to be ever curious, looking for more and more ways to understand, exploit and change the world around them.Once you choose the alchemist life, you are required to always be experimenting. Going a long rest without crafting with faery reagents will increase stress, whilst crafting with them will decrease stress. Likewise, fighting without using your creations will add stress.
All gunpowder items/Firearm Shot crafted by you deal +1 Blunt Force Trauma.
This also applies to Revelations of Thunder.
All gunpowder items/Firearm Shot crafted by you deal +2 Blunt Force Trauma.
This also applies to Revelations of Thunder.
All gunpowder items/Firearm Shot crafted by you deal +3 Blunt Force Trauma.
This also applies to Revelations of Thunder.
Gain access to a Close Observation. If you are caught in the explosion from a gunpowder item you made, you take half damage whilst enemies take 50% more damage.
This also applies to Revelations of Thunder if you choose yourself as one of the targets.
During the war against the Nebulans, the most important role in a coalition squad fell to the faery and pixie who converted Stardust to Marander Gas. In the disease and toxic laden aftermath, the most sought after people were the faeries and pixies who could provide some semblance of healing and recovery. And there was no shortage of work to be done.Once you choose the scourge life, you are required to always be scrubbing. Curing significant poisons, ailments or other bad statuses allows you to lose stress, but using poisons and drugs will cause you to gain stress. All negative effects inflict 1 less stack, until a minimum of 1. +1 to all endurance saving throws. All negative effects inflict 2 less stacks, until a minimum of 1. +2 to all endurance saving throws. All negative effects inflict 3 less stacks, until a minimum of 1. +3 to all endurance saving throws.
Gain access to Dire Purge. Whenever you cure someone of a condition, they also heal 1d6 and gain +1 to a core stat of their choice for 1 turn. If this condition would have killed them on their next turn without your action, the bonus effects are tripled.

item.title: Human Paths (Aquatine)
item.description:
Aquatine human paths are specific perks that unlock at levels 3. They are upgraded at levels 6 and 9. Once a perk path is chosen, you cannot take the others. The tiers do not stack with each other.Paths represent a lifestyle your character embodies. You may choose not to take a path.Tamira, goddess of rain, was perhaps the most popular deity of the continent. Some might argue she was even larger then New Illuminetres itself. But as the Aquatine Empire crumbled, Tamira's shrines and her dancers went with it. Even so, in the cursed and desolate wasteland that once was, rain still falls.
Once you choose the dancer life, you are bound to be always be dancing. When you dance in the rain, you lose stress. Failing to do so makes you gain stress. Gain +1 movement speed and defences. Lose 1 hit chance. Gain +2 movement speed and defences. Lose 2 hit chance. Gain +3 movement speed and defences. Lose 3 hit chance.
Gain access to Dancer's Grief. Spend a regular action dancing. All allies who can see you gain the tier 3 path buffs for 2 turns. The next attack against you has disadvantage/You roll with advantage against grappling checks. This buff lasts 1 turn. Does not stack.
The Aquatine Empire fielded some of the most disciplined and organised forces in all of the continent. The backbone of their military was the imperial legionnaire. The legionnaire wore heavy armour, bore large shields and spears, but what truly set them apart was their camaraderie. Legionnaires ate, slept and lived together as one. Brothers and sisters, not bound by blood. Lost, but never forgotten.Once you join the legions, they never leave you. Going though a fight without being outflanked will lower stress, whilst not doing so will raise it. When equipped with 3 layers of armour and a helmet: Gain +1 Armour. When equipped with 3 layers of armour and a helmet: Gain +1 Armour.
Gain +2 kg to your equipment load thresholds. When equipped with 3 layers of armour and a helmet: Gain +1 Armour. Getting hit by opportunity/zoning attacks no longer removes movement speed.
Gain +2 kg to your equipment load thresholds.
Gain access to Pangolin Wall. Whenever an adjacent ally takes an incoming attack, you can spend your next turn's bonus action to redirect the attack to you. The decision must be made before the attack is rolled. If redirected, the attack is rolled against you as normal.
This inflicts and is subject to view cone restrictions as normal. If you cannot turn to face the incoming attack, you can still redirect it, but you will be considered flanked for the attack roll.
The hammer to the legionnaires' anvil, the cavalry fielded by the Aquatine Empire were second to none. Taking great pride in their pedigrees and horses, the cavalry men and women of the empire could move with their mounts as if they were one. Even as the fields rot and the stables turn to ash, the riders carry on. They must carry on.Once you choose to be a rider, you must ride. Executing a successful charge on horseback will reduce stress whilst going through combat completely on foot will raise it.
Horses ridden by you have +3 temperament, melee and ranged defences. Mounting/Dismounting can now be done with bonus action.
Horses ridden by you have +3 temperament, melee and ranged defences. Mounting/Dismounting can now be done with bonus action.
Your saves against being dismounted are rolled with advantage, and you no longer fall prone if dismounted.
Horses ridden by you have +3 temperament, melee and ranged defences. Mounting/Dismounting can now be done with bonus action, and you gain back half of your movement speed after doing so.
Your saves against being dismounted are rolled with advantage, and you no longer fall prone if dismounted.
Gain access to Lance of the East. Once per combat, deal double damage with a mounted, melee weapon charge attack at the cost of destroying the weapon's shaft.

item.title: Armour Smithing
item.description:
Armour smithing is separated into helmets and the 3 layers of body armour, all of which have their own unique compositions and base stats. You decide the customisation for each stage, which determines the stats, cost, weight, time-to-craft and adjustment score of the final piece.All the standard armour pieces found in the Body Armours and Head Armours pages are calculated based off the mechanics below.
To do anything listed below, you require the smithing(armour) skill, alongside a set of smithing tools. Some customisations may also require a pixie with certain masteries alongside the smithing tools and skill, or pixie smithing tools alongside the skill. A piece's armour value cannot fall below 0. A piece's adjustment score cannot fall below 0. Percentage modifiers are additive. (i.e. two +50% modifiers stack to be +100%) Weight cannot be reduced below 1kg. Round up all calculations to the next whole number, except weight, which is rounded up to the next 0.25kg interval. Each armour piece's final cost is derived as such: (Total Cost of Material) x (Time-units taken x 0.20) x (Customisation Modifier)You can smelt down or scrap an armour piece to get back 50% of the materials used to make them. The time-unit cost and skill requirement to scrap a weapon part is equal to the tier of the material the armour is made of. (e.g. A piece made of tier 1 materials needs skill 1 in armour smithing and 1 time-unit to scrap.)
Armour can be readjusted to fit another person to avoid incurring fitting penalties. You will need the relevant materials and time units equal to the armour's adjustment score.If not otherwise stated, the requirements is as such: 1 Adjustment Score: no skill needed, no material needed, no smithing kit needed. 2 Adjustment Score: Level 1 skill + 2 material units. 3 Adjustment Score: Level 2 skill + 3 material units. 4+ Adjustment Score: Level 3 skill + 4 material units. Repairing a damaged piece of armour takes half the resources and time it took to make it. The same skill and tool requirements apply.Armour: 0 Adjustment Score: 2 Weight: 2kg Material Cost: 4 fabric units Craft Time: 4 time-units
Medium Grade Fabric (Skill 2) Standard material, no effects.
Low Grade Fabric (Skill 1) +50% weight. -1 adjustment score. -50% time-unit cost.
High Grade Fabric (Skill 3) -50% weight. +1 adjustment score. +100% time-unit cost. Standard (Skill 1) Standard weave, no effects. Silent Weave (Skill 2) +2 to stealth. +1 adjustment score. +50% time-unit cost. Harness Weave (Skill 3)
+2kg to equipment load thresholds. +2 adjustment score. +50% time-unit cost. Steel-Linen Weave (Skill 3)
Makes the piece pixie-metal-forged, needs a pixie with metal mastery or pixie smithing tools. +1 armour. +1 adjustment score. +50% time-unit cost. Armour: 2 Adjustment Score: 2 Weight: 9kg Stealth: Disadvantage Material Cost: 8 metal units Craft Time: 8 time-units
Steel (Skill 2) Standard material, no effects.
Iron (Skill 1) +33% weight. -1 adjustment score. -25% time-unit cost.
Pixie-forged Steel (Skill 3) -33% weight. +1 adjustment score. +50% time-unit cost. Riveted (Skill 2) Standard material, no effects. Butted (Skill 1) -1 armour. -1 adjustment score. -25% time-unit cost. -50% armour piece monetary value. Welded (Skill 3)
Makes the piece pixie-metal-forged, needs a pixie with metal mastery or pixie smithing tools. +50% material cost. +1 armour. +1 adjustment score. +50% time-unit cost. Standard (Skill 1) Standard circular rings, no effect. Large (Skill 1) -1 armour. -33% weight. -25% time-unit cost. Small (Skill 3) +1 armour. +33% weight. +50% time-unit cost. Armour: 3 Adjustment Score: 2 Weight: 15kg Stealth: Disadvantage Material Cost: 10 metal units Craft Time: 10 time-units
Steel (Skill 2) Standard material, no effects.
Iron (Skill 1) +20% weight. -1 adjustment score. -20% time-unit cost.
Pixie-forged Steel (Skill 3) -20% weight. +1 adjustment score. +40% time-unit cost. Riveted (Skill 2) Standard material, no effects. Butted (Skill 1) -1 armour. -1 adjustment score. -20% time-unit cost. -50% armour piece monetary value. Welded (Skill 3)
Makes the piece pixie-metal-forged, needs a pixie with metal mastery or pixie smithing tools. +50% material cost. +1 armour. +1 adjustment score. +40% time-unit cost. Standard (Skill 1) Standard circular rings, no effect. Large (Skill 1) -1 armour. -20% weight. -20% time-unit cost. Small (Skill 3) +1 armour. +20% weight. +40% time-unit cost. Armour: 1 Adjustment Score: 1 Weight: 4kg Material Cost: 8 fabric units Craft Time: 4 time-units
Medium Grade Fabric (Skill 1) Standard material, no effects.
Low Grade Fabric (Skill 1) +25% weight. -1 adjustment score. -25% time-unit cost.
High Grade Fabric (Skill 2) -25% weight. +1 adjustment score. +50% time-unit cost. Standard (Skill 1) Standard pattern, no effects. Diamond (Skill 1) -1 melee defence. -25% weight. Composite Pattern (Skill 2) -25% weight +50% time-unit cost. Standard (Skill 1) Standard layers, no effects. Extra Layers (Skill 2) +50% material cost. +1 armour. +50% time-unit cost. +100% weight. Extra-Extra Layers (Skill 2) +100% material cost. +2 armour. -2 melee and ranged defences. +100% time-unit cost. +200% weight. Armour: 2 Adjustment Score: 3 Weight: 6kg Stealth: Disadvantage Material Cost: 8 metal/leather units Craft Time: 8 time-units

item.title: Ammunition Crafting
item.description:
This page details crafting system for ammunitions, including Bolts, Arrows, Firearm Shot, Stones and some Throwables. Each craftable here has many customisations available, you must pick 1 and only 1 option per customisation. Next to some choices is a bracket with the prerequisites needed to craft that customisation. For stat modifiers like damage, penetration etc. These act on whatever weapon uses the ammunition. For stat modifiers like craft-time, material cost, weight etc. These act on the base stats of the crafting recipe. Each bundle of ammunition's final cost is derived as such: (Total Cost of Materials) x (Time-units taken x 0.1)Material Cost: 1 metal unit, 1 wood unit, 1 leather unit Craft-Time: 4 time-units Craft Amount: 5 Weight: 5x0.1kg This customisation determines what the metal unit used is.
Steel (Weapon-Smithing 2, Smithing Tools) Standard material, no effects.
Iron (Weapon-Smithing 1, Smithing Tools) -1 penetration. (Double for slow-firing weapons) -1 damage. (Double for slow-firing weapons) -25% craft time.
Pixie-Forged Steel (Weapon-Smithing 3, Smithing Tools) +1 damage. (Double for slow-firing weapons) +25% craft time.
Nebulan Starshard (Weapon-Smithing 3, Smithing Tools) +2 penetration. (+3 for slow-firing weapons) +25% craft time. No Arrowhead Does not need metal unit. -50% damage. -25% craft time. Padded Arrowhead Does not need metal unit. -75% damage. -25% craft time. Standard (Weapon-Smithing 1, Smithing Tools) Standard shape, no effects. Broad (Weapon-Smithing 2, Smithing Tools) +2 damage. (+3 for slow-firing weapons) -3 penetration. (-4 for slow-firing weapons) +25% craft time. Piercing (Weapon-Smithing 3, Smithing Tools) +3 penetration. (+4 for slow-firing weapons) -2 damage. (-3 for slow-firing weapons) +25% craft time. Serrated (Weapon-Smithing 3, Smithing Tools)
Inflict bleeding(2) on hit. (Bleeding(3) for slow-firing weapons) -1 penetration. (Double for slow-firing weapons) +25% craft time. This customisation determines what the wood unit used is.
Medium Grade Wood (Weapon-Smithing 2, Smithing Tools) Standard, no effects.
Scrap Wood (Weapon-Smithing 1) -25% craft time. This ammunition is always destroyed on use and cannot be recovered.
High Grade Wood (Weapon-Smithing 3, Smithing Tools) +25% craft time. -50% weight. Standard (Weapon-Smithing 1) Standard, no effects. Hollow (Weapon-Smithing 2, Smithing Tools) -1 damage. (Double for slow-firing weapons) +2m optimal range. +25% craft time. Whistling (Weapon-Smithing 2, Smithing Tools) The arrow produces a whistling sound. No direct combat effect but could have impact in roleplay depending on how you use it. +25% craft time. This customisation determines what the leather unit used is.
Medium Grade Leather (Weapon-Smithing 2, Smithing Tools) Standard, no effects.
Low Grade Leather (Weapon-Smithing 1) -1 hit chance. -25% craft time.
High Grade Leather (Weapon-Smithing 3, Smithing Tools) +1 hit chance. +25% craft time. Standard (Weapon-Smithing 1) Standard shape, no effects. Helical (Weapon-Smithing 2, Smithing Tools) +1 hit chance. -1m optimal range. Low Profile (Weapon-Smithing 2, Smithing Tools) -1 hit chance. +1m optimal range. Nothing No add ons, no effects. Gunpowder Payload Arrow/Bolt cannot be recovered. Requires a gunpowder unit. The gunpowder's explosion will act as an additional attack on the tile where the projectile lands. The explosion's potency is halved or reduced by 1, whichever is the bigger penalty. On a miss, roll a d8 to see which adjacent tile the explosion is centred on. +25% craft time. Rocket Booster Arrow/Bolt cannot be recovered. Requires a gunpowder unit. +1d4 blunt force trauma per level of potency. +1d4 damage instead if using lesser gunpowder. -1 hit chance per level of potency. +1m optimal range per level of potency. The gunpowder's own damage/blunt force trauma stats and status effects are not inflicted. +25% craft time. Each bundle of ammunition's final cost is derived as such: (Total Cost of Materials) x (Time-units taken x 0.2)Material Cost: 1 metal unit Craft-Time: 1 time-units Craft Amount: 5 Weight: 5x0.1kg This customisation determines what the metal unit used is. Stones Does not require metal units. The monetary value of this ammunition is set to 0. Standard material, no effect.
Iron (Weapon-Smithing 1, Smithing Tools) +1m optimal range. +200% craft time.
Steel (Weapon-Smithing 2, Smithing Tools) +1m optimal range. +1 penetration. (Double for slow-firing weapons) +300% craft time.
Pixie-Forged Steel (Weapon-Smithing 3, Smithing Tools) +2m optimal range. +1 penetration. (Double for slow-firing weapons) +400% craft time. Standard Standard shape, no effect. Almond (Weapon-Smithing 2, Smithing Tools) +1 hit chance. +200% craft time. Nothing Standard filler, no effect. Whistling (Weapon-Smithing 2, Smithing Tools) The stone produces a whistling sound. No direct combat effect but could have impact in roleplay depending on how you use it. +100% craft time. Gunpowder Filler Cannot be used with stone material. Requires a gunpowder unit. The gunpowder's explosion will act as an additional attack on the tile where the projectile lands. The explosion's potency is halved or reduced by 1, whichever is the bigger penalty. On a miss, roll a d8 to see which adjacent tile the explosion is centred on. +100% craft time.

item.title: Gunpowder Chemistry
item.description:
Gunpowder chemistry covers the making of gunpowder, and the making of consumables that use gunpowder. Gunpowder is considered contraband, so beware of using it carelessly, especially for non-faery players.You need an alchemy set and gunpowder chemistry skill as a bare minimum to do any gunpowder chemistry. Some chemistry will also require a pixie with certain masteries alongside an alchemy set and skills, or a pixie alchemy set alongside the skills.Customisable gunpowder can be made, with differing effects depending on the ingredient composition. Each gunpowder unit is made with these main ingredients: Faery Reagents: Essence F, or just "F"
Saltpeter: Essence SP, or just "SP"
Sulfur: Essence S, or just "S"
High Grade Wood: Essence W, or just "W" Each 1 of the ingredients listed above provides 1 essence. Choose whether to make lesser or true gunpowder. Both share the same customisations. Go down the list of gunpowder customisations. You must choose 1 and only 1 option for each customisation. Add the modifiers from the customisations to the base stats. Spend resources to make gunpowder during rests. Each gunpowder unit's final cost is derived as such: (Total Cost of Essence) x (Time-units taken x 0.50) Total cost of essence uses the base ingredient costs.Gunpowder stats have something called "potency", along side "XXX per potency". Simply multiply these together to get the final stat. If potency is reduced to 0, the gunpowder does no damage/blunt force trauma, but still inflicts statuses as though it had a potency of 1.If used by itself, gunpowder needs a regular action to activate, loses 1 potency and can only be used on the user's tile in a 1m radius. Requirements: Gunpowder Chemistry 1 Potency: 2 Damage per potency: 1d6 Penetration per potency: 2 Area of Effect: 1m radius around target tile. Essence cost: 2S, 2SP, 2W Time-unit cost: 2 Weight: 1kg Requirements: Gunpowder Chemistry 3, pixie with gunpowder mastery or pixie alchemy set. Potency: 2 Blunt Force Trauma per potency: 1d6
Inflicts shellshock(1) per 2 potency, DC15 + Gunpowder Chemistry Skill. Area of Effect: 1m radius around target tile. Essence cost: 2S, 2SP, 2W, 1F Craft time: 2 time-units Weight: 1kg Standard Rate (Gunpowder Chemistry 1) No effects. Slow Burning (Gunpowder Chemistry 2) -1 potency. +1SP essence cost. +1m area of effect radius. Fast Burning (Gunpowder Chemistry 3) +1 potency. +1S essence cost. -1m area of effect radius. Unstable Powder (Gunpowder Chemistry 3) +2 potency. +1SP, 1S essence cost. Make a dexterity DC5 check every time this powder or an consumable made from this powder is handled. Failing this will result in the item detonating on the user's tile. Ultimatum (Gunpowder Chemistry 3, pixie with gunpowder mastery or pixie alchemy set) +4 potency. +2m area of effect radius,
Shellshock effect is guaranteed. +6F essence cost. +4 time-unit cost. Standard (Gunpowder Chemistry 1) No effects. Incendiary (Gunpowder Chemistry 2)
Inflict burning(1) per potency, DC15 + Gunpowder Chemistry Skill. +1W essence cost. +1 time-unit cost. Corrosive (Gunpowder Chemistry 2)
Inflict corroded(1) per potency, DC15 + Gunpowder Chemistry Skill. +1S essence cost. +1 time-unit cost. Blinding (Gunpowder Chemistry 3)
Inflict blinded(1) per potency, DC15 + Gunpowder Chemistry Skill. +1S, 1SP essence cost. +2 time-unit cost. Choose a gunpowder unit. Its stats will be the explosion stats for the grenade. Go down the list of grenade customisations. You must choose 1 and only 1 option for each customisation. Add the modifiers from the customisations to the base stats. Spend resources to make the grenade during rests. Each grenade's final cost is derived as such: (Total Cost of Materials) x (Time-units taken x 0.25) Throw Range: 5m Throw dexterity DC: 12 Damage and blast radius dependent on gunpowder used. Material Cost: 4 metal units, 1 gunpowder unit. Craft time: 4 time-units This determines what the metal units used are.
Steel (Weapon-Smithing 2, smithing tools) Standard material, no effect.
Iron (Weapon-Smithing 1, smithing tools) -1m range. -1 time-unit cost.
Pixie-Forged Steel (Weapon-Smithing 3, smithing tools) +1m range. +1 time-unit cost. Bottles
Does not need metal units, uses 1 clay, glass or crystal bottles instead. +1m range. -1 potency. -2 time-unit cost. Standard (Weapon-Smithing 1, smithing tools) Standard construction, no effect. Fragmentation (Weapon-Smithing 3, smithing tools) Anyone in a radius 1m more than the grenade's is hit by shrapnel. Shrapnel deals 1d4 damage with 0 penetration. The number of shrapnel inflicted is equal to the potency of the grenade. Each individual shrapnel is counted as its own attack. +2 time-unit cost. Dart (Weapon-Smithing 3, smithing tools) +2m range. -7 throw DC. +2 time-unit cost. Standard Standard fuse time, grenade explodes on landing. Long Fuse
Grenade explodes at the start or the end of the next round. This must be decided before throwing and cannot be changed after. +1W essence cost. Unpredictable Fuse Roll a d4 at the below points. The grenade explodes on a 1. On initial landing.
At the start of every subsequent zig-zag cycle.
The grenade will detonate at the end of the next round, regardless of the d4 roll. Choose a gunpowder unit. Its stats will be stats for the firearm shot with some caveats, see below. Go down the list of firearm shot customisations. You must choose 1 and only 1 option for each customisation. Add the modifiers from the customisations to the base stats. Spend resources to make the firearm shots during rests. Each gunpowder unit's final cost is derived as such: (Total Cost of Materials) x (Time-units taken x 0.5)Unlike grenades, firearm shot does not use all the stats from the gunpowder unit directly. Blunt Force Trauma is determined by the weapon's stats. For each level of potency above 2, gain +2 blunt force trauma. For each level of potency below 2, lose -2 blunt force trauma. For lesser gunpowder, convert blunt force trauma to regular damage with 4 penetration. Regular damage bonuses from paths, traits etc. are applied to blunt force trauma if using true gunpowder. Firearm shots do not use the area of effect stat.
Status effects still apply, but use the weapon's normal saving throw DC calculations. Crafting amount: 3 Craft time: 2 time-units Material Cost: 2 metal units, 1 gunpowder unit. Weight: 3 x 0.1kg This determines what the metal units used are.
Steel (Weapon-Smithing 2, smithing tools) Standard material, no effect.
Iron (Weapon-Smithing 1, smithing tools) -2 blunt force trauma. -1 time-unit cost.
Pixie-Forged Steel (Weapon-Smithing 3, smithing tools) +2 blunt force trauma. +1 time-unit cost. Round (Weapon-Smithing 1, smithing tools) Standard shape, no effects. Needle (Weapon-Smithing 3, smithing tools) Hit chance: Adv Optimal Range: +5m Blunt Force Trauma: x1/2 Maximum range is doubled. +2 time-unit cost. Grapeshot (Weapon-Smithing 3, smithing tools) Take the maximum possible blunt force trauma the round shot customisation would do out of the weapon and divide by 3 to get the number of pellets in the grapeshot. (Rounded up) For each pellet, deal 1d6 blunt force trauma. -5 hit chance. Maximum range is cut to a quarter its original. +2 time-unit cost. Standard Standard load, no effects. Under-loaded -50% blunt force trauma. Loading this ammunition does not need an action. +2 crafted amount. Over-loaded +50% blunt force trauma. Firing this ammunition requires a d4 roll.
If this roll is greater than the level of material used in the firearm's barrel part, the barrel explodes and is damaged, dealing half the blunt force damage to the user. The shot is still fired in case of an overload explosion. -1 crafted amount.

item.title: Weapon Smithing
item.description:
Weapon smithing involves going to the weapon's individual wiki page and finding out what parts make up a weapon. Then, expend time-units during short and long rests to craft the individual parts until you have a complete weapon. Detailed below are all the different weapon parts, and how they can be customised. Customisation works off the weapon's/weapon part's base stats, which is what is listed on the individual weapon sheets.To do anything listed below, you require the smithing(weapon) skill, alongside a set of smithing tools. Some customisations may require a pixie with certain masteries alongside the tools and skills, or a set of pixie smithing tools alongside the skill.Each weapon part has 4 parameters to consider: Material: What the part is made of. There are 3 types: Metal, Wood and Leather. Craft Time: How long it takes to make in time-units. Cost: Value of the part. Weight: Weight of the part.
The base stats for each weapon part and weapon are the values set when using the standard material types, which are steel bars, medium grade wood and medium grade leather. Each weapon part has a list of customisation types that can be applied to it. For each customisation type, you may only choose 1 option. Each customisation title has a number next to it, this is the level of weapon smithing skill you need to have to apply that customisation. Weapons with a negative damage modifier from will always do at least 1 damage. Weapons that deal blunt force trauma with a negative blunt force trauma modifier will always do at least 1 blunt force trauma. Weapons with a negative penetration modifier will not increase enemy effective armour and will be treated as having 0 penetration. Weapons with a positive penetration modifier can bypass the veterancy cap if present. Customisation effects are additive: Having two +50% modifiers will result in a +100% modifier. Round any decimals from calculations up to the next whole number, apart from weight calculations, which are rounded to the next 0.25kg. Some stat modifiers are changed depending on if the weapon is 2-handed. In this case, weapons that are 1-handed/2-handed will receive the appropriate stat modifier depending on if they are used as 1-handed or 2-handed weapons.
Status effect DC uses the same calculations as normal saving throws the weapon uses. Each weapon part's final cost is derived as such:(Total Cost of Material) x (Time-units taken x 0.20) x (Customisation Modifier)Changes to material or time cost will affect the final price but are not directly stated below in the customisation pros and cons, so be sure to factor those in! Or you can ignore calculating cost if you're never planning on selling your weapon I guess.Weapons can be disassembled to their base parts, allowing you to swap individual parts out without the need to reforge the entire weapon. It takes 1 time-unit to remove or attach 1 weapon part from a weapon. Weapon parts are not interchangeable between weapons. Players can ask the GM for exceptions to this rule if two weapons share a part with the same base ingredient costs, craft times, and make sense logically to be interchangeable. (e.g. The long-haft part of a spear and halberd, or the grip part for most one-handed/two-handed weapons) You can scrap individual weapon parts to recover 50% of the materials used to create them. The time-unit cost and skill requirement to scrap a weapon part is equal to the tier of the material the part is made of. (e.g. A part made of tier 1 materials needs skill 1 in weapon smithing and 1 time-unit to scrap.)A broken/damaged weapon part can be repaired with half of the required materials and time-unit cost.

item.title: Alchemy
item.description:
Alchemy is used to make potions/salves that cover a wide range of effects: from buffs and poisons to healing. You need an alchemy set to brew potions.All alchemy requires an alchemy set and alchemy skill. Some will also require a pixie with certain masteries alongside an alchemy set and skills, or a pixie alchemy set alongside the skills.These are the main ingredients used in alchemy, and they will be abbreviated as such: Albino Beetle: Essence A, or just "A"
Blackriver Berry: Essence B, or just "B"
Celusian Flower: Essence C, or just "C"
Medical Herbs: Essence M, or just "M"
Faery Reagents: Essence F, or just "F"
Poisonous Stuff: Essence P, or just "P"
Sulfur: Essence S, or just "S" Potions/Salves are made out of a combination of these essences. Each 1 of the ingredients listed above provides 1 essence.
You can also use essence from their derivatives in the Medicine, Coatings and Throwables pages. Essence capacity represents how much essence you can stuff into a potion before it becomes chemically unstable. This is primarily determined by the quality of the bottle.A reaction is an effect/multiple effects a potion can have. Each reaction needs a certain number and type of essence to perform. There's only a limited amount of reactions that you can put in a potion, depending on the bottle. A potion cannot have duplicate reactions.Potion making follows these steps: Prepare what bottle and essences you have available. Select the type and number of reactions you want in your potion that fit your bottle and essence restrictions. Add up the time-unit and essence cost of your reactions and spend the resources to make the potion.
You can use other potions, medicine, coatings or throwables as ingredients, but with some limitations: You must use all of the item, you cannot separate out specific essences to use. If the item contains essence that isn't included in the recipe or has essence that exceeds the amount in the recipe, it cannot be used. Calculate the monetary cost of the potion if you're planning on selling it. These are the default stats potions use, unless otherwise stated. Weight: 1kg Bonus action to drink.
Bonus action to apply as coating. By default, coating a weapon with a potion will not allow you to apply the effects on hit. You need specific reactions for that. Regular action to throw, DC12 dexterity, 6m range. Throwing a potion will destroy the bottle. By default, throwing a potion will not allow you to apply the effects on hit. You need specific reactions for that. Failing the throw will result in the potion landing in one of the adjacent tiles, determined by a d8 roll.
The safe daily amount of a potion is determined by the lowest value of all the reactions. Taking more than the safe daily amount needs an increasingly difficult addiction check. Each potion can only be used once. Unless destroyed, potion bottles can be reused once the potion is expended. Monetary value of a potion is decided as such: Sum of all reaction costs + bottle cost. A reaction's cost is determined as such: (Total Cost of Essences) x (Time-units taken). Total cost of essences is based off the essence's base ingredient costs. If your time-units taken is 0, change it to 1 for the value calculations. The following list contains the different bottle type and their effects on the potion.Essence Capacity: 2 Reaction Limit: 1Essence Capacity: 4 Reaction Limit: 2Essence Capacity: 6 Reaction Limit: 3Some reactions are tiered. Potions cannot have duplicate reactions, and the different tiers count as duplicate reactions. (i.e. If you take tier 1 of movement speed increase, you cannot take any other tier of movement speed increase.)Requirements: Alchemy 1 Effects: +1m movement speed for 3 turns. Essence Cost: 3A Safe Daily Amount: 1 Time-Unit Cost: 2 Requirements: Alchemy 1 Effects: +1 melee damage for 3 turns. Essence Cost: 1B Safe Daily Amount: No limit. Time-Unit Cost: 0 Requirements: Alchemy 2 Effects: +2 melee damage for 2 turns. Essence Cost: 2B Safe Daily Amount: 2 Time-Unit Cost: 1 Requirements: Alchemy 3 Effects: +3 melee damage for 1 turn. item.title: Materials
item.description:
Tier 1 material. Consists of rough hemp cloth and various scraps of fabric. Weight: 1kg Cost: 10g Tier 2 material. Consists of linen and cotton, or other various decent quality cloth. Weight: 1kg Cost: 25g Tier 3 material. Consists of silk and velvet, or other luxury cloth. Weight: 1kg Cost: 100g Tier 1 material. Consists of rough cheap scraps and patched leather. Weight: 1kg Cost: 10g Tier 2 material. Properly tanned, boiled and treated leather. The standard. Weight: 1kg Cost: 25g Tier 3 material. Consists of the best pieces from specially bred animals, treated with fine-tuned methods. Weight: 1kg Cost: 50g Tier 1 material. Less intensive to make than steel and easier to forge, but softer and weaker. Weight: 1kg Cost: 25g Tier 2 material. Steel-making was pioneered by Lady Numeria, and serves as the standard for metals. Weight: 1kg Cost: 50g Tier 3 material. Centuries of research has yielded a long, laborious method to produce a steel blend with stronger properties. Weight: 1kg Cost: 100g Tier 3 material. The Nebulans brought many strange crystal rocks with them. Whilst most are seemingly useless compared to contemporary materials, certain special crystals were clearly brought over for weapon smithing, and possess unnaturally hard properties. Weight: 1kg Cost: 100g Tier 1 material. Leftover scraps and low quality trimmings, barely fit for use as firewood. Weight: 1kg Cost: 1g Tier 2 material. Strong and flexible, the standard for most purposes. Weight: 1kg Cost: 25g Tier 3 material. Harvested from carefully cultivated and grown forests, this wood is the best there is. Weight: 1kg Cost: 50g
Gunpowder requires proper handling to be useful. See Gunpowder Chemistry for more. Gunpowder is considered contraband, be wary of flouting it, especially if you're not a faery/pixie.
