item.title: Melee Attacks
item.description:
I've tried to make melee combat feel more immersive and strategic, so now there are several new mechanics tied to melee combat. Bear in mind that combat maps are separate into 1m by 1m grids to calculate distance.Each weapon type now has a unique set of moves. Moves can be unlocked by investing proficiency points during level ups.Each melee weapon now has a default optimum range. This represents the range the weapon is usually most effective at. Short weapons like one-handed swords, maces, etc. now usually have a range of 1m. Long weapons like pikes, polearms etc. now have a range of 2-3m. Note that this range is move-specific, so a weapon can have multiple optimum ranges besides their default one.For attacks with >1m range, if there is an obstruction between you and the target, you roll with disadvantage, the same as to obstructions used by ranged attacks.
A character has a zone of attention when attacking and defending. Imagine your character has a view cone extending from them with a default FOV of 90 degrees.
Making an attack will automatically lock your view cone such that the target has to be within it. This applies to opportunity/zoning attacks.
In order to attack someone else, you must be able to shift your view cone to include the new target whilst still encompassing all old enemiesUpon being attacked by another enemy:
If you can shift your view cone to include the new enemy whilst still encompassing all old enemies, you defend as normal, but your view cone restrictions must now include the new enemy. If you can't, the new enemy gets a flanking attack on you. Flanking attacks grant advantage, and remove the defence bonuses of the target's weapons.
You may choose to deliberately avoid defending attacks so that your view cone isn't as restricted, allowing you to defend against potentially more dangerous enemies that might flank you.
View cone restrictions are reset at the start of your next turn. They can also be lifted for specific enemies depending on the situation.Upon leaving melee range of the enemy:
If you are both out of range, the view cone restrictions for both of you are lifted. If you are in range but the enemy isn't, you may chose to break your restrictions, but doing so will cause the enemy's to be lifted as well. If the enemy is in range but you aren't, your restrictions are only lifted if the enemy decides to. This does not apply to ranged attacks. Those restrictions can only be removed at the start of your next turn or by view cone cracking.
In the case where an enemy already in your view cone restriction list manages to move in such a way that you are no longer able to encompass them and everyone else in the restriction list, they are removed from your view cone restriction list, and you are removed from theirs.If an enemy moves out of or within your weapon's default optimal range, you may attack them. Bear in mind this imposes and is subject to view cone restrictions until your next turn. Opportunity attacks don't trigger on entering your optimal range. You only have 1 opportunity attack a turn.
Enemies hit by opportunity attacks have their movement cancelled, and all remaining movement speed removed. Enemies can still use their regular action to dash afterwards.Some weapon moves allow you to gain a zoning buff, where you can attack enemies that enter your weapon's optimal range. Bear in mind this imposes and is subject to view cone restrictions until your next turn. Zoning attacks don't trigger on enemies leaving or moving within your weapon's optimal range.You have unlimited zoning attacks until the buff wears off.
Enemies hit by zoning attacks have their movement cancelled, and all remaining movement speed removed. Enemies can still use their regular action to dash afterwards.Charging on foot requires you to move in a straight line along one of the 8 directions on a square grid (+ and x). For every 3m moved, add your strength | dexterity modifier as bonuses to your weapon's hit chance and regular damage. The 3m intervals refer to distance moved on the ground, not movement spent.
Enemy opportunity and zoning attacks made against you during the charge will gain your charge bonuses against you. You finish the charge from the enemy at the range your weapon's default attack is. You cannot charge through obstacles, allies or enemies. Each point of charge mobility allows you to make a 45 degree turn at any point during your charge.
Moves that try to move a target must hit, then the target must fail the move saving throw to succeed. The damage from the hit is still applied even if the target succeeds the saving throw.
Moves that allow the user and hit a target and move must hit for the user to be able to move without triggering opportunity attacks. The user may choose to not move if they miss. If they hit, they must move.

item.title: Weapon Rules
item.description:
There are three weapon types, depending on how many hands they take to wield. With some exceptions, each weapon you wield can only attack once per turn, regardless of any actions you have remaining. (e.g. If you use a weapon's bonus action move, you cannot use any of its regular action moves and vice versa.)These weapons can be wielded alone or with an off-hand weapon.Two-handed weapons require both hands to wielded and cannot be used alongside another weapon.Off-handed weapons can be used to dual wield without penalty. They are always one-handed.Dual wielding allows you to use both regular and bonus action for attacking in the same turn, but comes with some restrictions.Dual wielding can only be done without penalty with a one-handed weapon and a off-handed weapon. Using two off-handed weapons also has no penalty.Dual wielding with two one-handed weapons will remove your stat bonuses from the stats of both weapons. The exception is if you have the dual wielder trait.When dual wielding, only the defences from one of the weapons is applied.
You may choose which weapon you want to make opportunity attacks with. You still only have 1 opportunity attack a turn.Without proficiency, you gain no bonuses from your stats for the weapon. For shields, lose -2 to the bonus melee and ranged defence (minimum of 0). The tier 1 moveset of all weapons are always available, regardless of proficiency.
There are 3 tiers of proficiency. Higher tiers can be unlocked when levelling up. You gain your weapon proficiency tier in hit chance. The following stats are not cumulative. Tier 1: Allows you to use the weapon with your stat bonuses. Gives+1 hit chance. Tier 2: Intermediate, provides additional utility moves. Gives +2 hit chance.
Tier 3: Advanced, provides unique and combo moves. Gives +3 hit chance. Roll minor complications instead of major ones on natural 1s.
Unarmed proficiency works differently. Tier 1: Gives +1 hit chance and +1 to grappling checks and DCs. Tier 2: Gives +2 hit chance and +2 to grappling checks and DCs (stacks with previous tiers).
Tier 3: Gives +3 hit chance and +3 to grappling checks and DCs. Roll minor complications instead of major one on nat 1s. Bear in mind weapon proficiencies require the previous tier. A tier 3 proficiency requires you have tier 2 proficiency, and a tier 2 proficiency requires a tier 1 proficiency.Some weapons require special training from their specific faction to gain tier 1 proficiency. Afterwards, you gain tier 2 and 3 proficiency as normal. The melee weapons are:
One-handed Flails / Two-handed Flails (Kingdom of Numeria)
One-handed Falces / Two-handed Falces (Wingard Collective)
Moonspades (Aquatine Empire)
Numerian Blades (Conclave of the Steel Faeries)
Berserker Chain (Steelscale Clan) The ranged weapons are:
Arbalest (Kingdom of Numeria)
Hand Crossbows (Wingard Collective)
Repeating Crossbow (Aquatine Empire)
Muskets / Pistols (Conclave of the Steel Faeries)
Amber Lances (Steelscale Clan) Ranged weapons require ammunition to use. Thrown weapons don't require separate ammunition, the weapon itself is the ammunition.By default, you can recover up to 50% of spent ammunition if you spend time scouring the battlefield after.
Firearm Shot cannot be recovered. Certain types of ammunition, such as gunpowder-type ammunitions, also cannot be recovered. Thrown weapons can be 100% recovered.
You begin combat with your weapon loadout set. To switch/equip weapons during combat, you must use the manage items action. For thrown weapons like Javelins, throwing them will automatically "reload" another one into your hand if available in your equipment load.

item.title: Resting and Other Activities
item.description:
Resting is divided into two types, short and long. During each type of rest, you have a resource called time-units to spend. This mechanic represents the amount of time you have to do things like crafting.If your personal time-units are not enough to complete an action, you can borrow a party member's to finish the job. For actions that have skill and/or tool prerequisites, your party members' time will only count for half as much if they don't also fulfil the prerequisite. There are no "half" time-units, so in such a case a party member must commit their time-units in multiples of 2. This only applies if you spend at least 1 time-unit yourself. Spend at least 1 hour resting, during which all party members: Heal 1d6 health, with the party's highest medical skill added as a bonus. Short rests are limited to once per long rest. You are given 2 time-units during short rests. With the appropriate tools, you can follow the given recipes to make provisions, craft throwables, medicine, potions etc.Spend at least 8 hours resting. Long rests are limited to once per day. If you have not short rested for the day, add on the health and time-unit bonuses you would have gotten.
Long resting is required everyday. Failing to do so results in +1 exhaustion for each day that goes by without long resting.Each party member may consume food, and the effects depend on how much is eaten:
Consume 2 units: Heal for a value equal to half your max health, -1 exhaustion.
Extra bonuses may apply depending on variety. Consume 1 unit: Heal to half of your max health.
Consume nothing: Heal to half of your max health, +1 exhaustion. Party members may roleplay with skill checks like performance, cooking etc. to further reduce stress. Each destressing attempt takes 1 time-unit and each party member can only make 1 attempt per long rest. An attempt involves making a DC15 check, which will result in -1 stress to all party members on success. Each success adds +5 to the next check. You are given 4 time-units during long rests.
With the appropriate tools, you can follow the given recipes to make provisions, craft throwables, medicine, potions etc.After long resting, remember to go through your inventory and update the timers on your perishable goods.You can use time-units during rests to forage, if the environment allows. Foraging requires you to specify what you are looking for:Spend 4 time-units, and gain 1d4 + (foraging/fishing skill) pieces of food. The food you find will depend on the environment and the skill used. In difficult environments, you may need to roll a d20 check as well. Failing the check will result in a 1d4 penalty to the amount of things found. Spend 4 time-units, and gain 1 + (foraging skill) pieces of herbs/drug items. The things you find will be dependent on the environment.
Items found are: medical herbs, albino beetles, blackriver berries and celusian flowers. In difficult environments, you may need to roll a d20 check as well. Failing the check will result in a 1d4 penalty to the amount of things found. Spend time-units to hunt an animal. You must specify the size of the animal you are trying to hunt. The values you see are a general guide for the GM, they may change depending on environment and circumstance.
The size of the animal changes how you hunt, see the Small Game and Large Game sections below.Small animals like rabbits, fowl, rodents etc. are delicate and die easily. Careless use of heavy weapons can cause the meat and skin to be damaged. Hunting small game takes place in cycles of 1 time-unit and is split into 2 phases: Tracking and Shooting. Hunting Cycle: Tracking Phase: Roll a tracking check, DC15 On success: Proceed to shooting phase. On failure: Give up and return to camp or proceed to next hunting cycle. For all remaining hunting cycles, you gain +2 to your tracking checks. This stacks. Shooting Phase: Perform an attack roll with a ranged weapon you use for hunting, DC15 On hit: See below. On miss: Give up or proceed to next hunting cycle. For all remaining hunting cycles, you gain +2 to your tracking checks. This stacks. You can roll a DC10 stealth check to gain advantage on this attack if successful. On failure, the shot will automatically be considered a miss. Small game have 2-4 health. If your damage roll is below or equal to the animal's health, it dies and you get the normal rewards. If your damage roll is above the animal's health, it dies and the body is considered damaged. You may chose to not include any stat modifiers or other bonuses in your damage roll.
On successful hunt: Gain 1d4 raw meat and 1d4 medium grade leather.
If the animal's body is damaged: Subtract 1d4 from the meat gains and receive low grade leather instead.
If your damage roll matches the animal's health perfectly: Add 1d4 to the meat gains and receive high grade leather instead. Big animals like boar, deer etc. are sturdy and may survive a single shot. It's not uncommon to have to chase down a struck animal multiple times to secure the kill. Taking too many shots to kill the animal can damage the meat and leather. Hunting large game takes place in cycles of 1 time-unit and is split into 2 phases: Tracking and Shooting. Hunting Cycle: Tracking Phase: Roll a tracking check, DC12 On success: Proceed to shooting phase. On failure: Give up and return to camp or proceed to next hunting cycle. For all remaining hunting cycles, you gain +2 to your tracking checks. This stacks. Shooting Phase: Perform an attack roll with a ranged weapon you use for hunting, DC10 On hit: See below. On miss: Give up or proceed to next hunting cycle. For all remaining hunting cycles, you gain +2 to your tracking checks. This stacks. You can roll a DC10 stealth check to gain advantage on this attack if successful. On failure, the shot will automatically be considered a miss. Large game have 10-20 health. If you did not kill the animal but wounded it, you can choose to give up or proceed to the next hunting cycle. For all remaining hunting cycles, you gain +4 to your tracking checks. This stacks. The animal's health is tracked across cycles for that long rest, unless you choose to hunt something else.
On successful hunt: Gain 3d4 raw meat and 3d4 medium grade leather.
If the animal took 3 or more shots to down: Subtract 1d4 from the meat gains and receive low grade leather instead.
If you succeed on the first shot: Add 1d4 to the meat gains and receive high grade leather instead. You cannot initiate another big game hunt if successful for the remainder of the rest.

item.title: Levels
item.description:
Bear in mind weapon proficiencies require the previous tier. A tier 3 proficiency requires you have tier 2 proficiency, and a tier 1 proficiency requires a tier 2 proficiency.Some weapons require special training from their specific faction to gain tier 1 proficiency. Afterwards, you gain tier 2 and 3 proficiency as normal. See proficiency rules.Your health at a particular level is calculated as such: Base health + (level * (endurance)) + levelYour stress maximum increases by 1 every 3 levels.During level up, core stats are increased directly by the stated value, not the point buy system used during character creation.
Veterancy is calculated by your level / 3, rounded up. Levels 0 - 3: Veterancy 1 Levels 4 - 6: Veterancy 2 Levels 7 - 9: Veterancy 3 During level up, skill increases use a point buy system. Point costs become more expensive the higher the skill is: Nothing to 0: 1 0 to 1: 1 1 to 2: 2 2 to 3: 3 Note that level 0 is not the baseline. Having no skill at all is the baseline, so you will need to spend 1 point to get level 0. Skills cannot go higher than 3. For faeries, skill bonuses from your pixie's masteries are not counted during skill allocation. They act as an add-on afterwards. Unspent skillpoints can be carried forwards to be spent later. You begin at level 0. Gain tier 1 weapon proficiency with a weapon.
Choose one tier 1 trait. Gain +2 base skill points to allocate. Add health. Gain tier 1 weapon proficiency with a weapon
Choose one tier 1 trait. Gain +2 base skill points to allocate. Add health and stress. Gain tier 2 or lower weapon proficiency with a weapon.
Choose one tier 1 trait. Gain +2 skill points to allocate. Gain +1 to some physical core stat. Gain +1 to some mental core stat. Gain +1 melee and ranged defense.
Choose a tier 1 path. Add health. Gain tier 2 or lower weapon proficiency with a weapon.
Choose one tier 2 or lower trait. Gain +2 base skill points to allocate. Add health. Gain tier 2 or lower weapon proficiency with a weapon.
Choose one tier 2 or lower trait. Gain +2 base skill points to allocate. Add health and stress. Gain tier 3 or lower weapon proficiency with a weapon.
Choose one tier 2 or lower trait. Gain +2 skill points to allocate. Gain +1 to some physical core stat. Gain +1 to some mental core stat. Gain +1 base melee and ranged defense.
Level up your path to tier 2. Add health. Gain tier 3 or lower weapon proficiency with a weapon.
Choose one tier 3 or lower trait. Gain +2 base skill points to allocate. Add health. Gain tier 3 or lower weapon proficiency with a weapon.
Choose one tier 3 or lower trait. Gain +2 base skill points to allocate. Add health and stress. Gain tier 3 or lower weapon proficiency with a weapon.
Choose one tier 3 or lower trait. Gain +2 skill points to allocate. Gain +1 to some physical core stat. Gain +1 to some mental core stat. Gain +1 base melee and ranged defense.
Level up your path to tier 3. Faeries get their pixies at level 3. Pixies level up together with their faeries.
Gain tier 1 of light mastery.
Gain a tier 1 pixie mastery.
Gain a tier 1 pixie mastery.
Gain a tier 2 or lower pixie mastery.
Gain tier 2 of light mastery.
Gain a tier 2 or lower pixie mastery.
Gain a tier 3 or lower pixie mastery.
Gain tier 3 of light mastery.
Gain a tier 3 or lower pixie mastery.
Gain +1 to max focus points.

item.title: Armour Rules
item.description:
You can equip: 1 helmet. Up to 3 layers of body armour. 1 cosmetic clothing 1 cosmetic cloak 1 cosmetic hat Body armour is separated into 3 layers: Layer 1: Closest layer to your body, usually used for padding like arming jackets. Layer 2: Usually used for mail armour. Layer 3: Furthest layer from your body, usually used for plate armour. You can equip up to one of each type. Your head and body layers are different. Helmets don't use the layer system, you simply equip 1 helmet. Layer 1 is required in order to wear layers 2 and 3.You have a clothing slot, a cloak slot and a hat slot. Clothing is equipped under your armour. Cloaks are equipped over your armour. Hats are equipped over your helmet. These provide no protection, but can influence roleplay and skill checks.Certain types of armour need to be properly tailored to the user, or they'll suffer some penalty.Amour needs to be fitted to a person's body. Adjustment score represents how hard it is for the armour to be altered for use by someone else. Adjusting armour will require smithing tools or tailoring tools, depending on material type. Tier 1: Can just be used as is. Tier 2: Requires a quick adjustment during short rest. Tier 3: Requires adjustment during long rest by someone with significant experience in smithing. Tier 4+: Requires dedicated equipment and an expert to drastically alter the piece. Adjusting crocodilian armour to the other races and vice versa will increase the adjustment score by 2.Wearing armour not suited for you imposes certain downsides, depending on the armour's adjustment score: Tier 1: No effect. Tier 2: -1 Hit chance to all attacks. -1 Melee and ranged defence. -1 to grappling saving throws. Tier 3: -1 Hit chance to all attacks. -2 Melee and ranged defence. -2 to grappling saving throws. Tier 4+: Suffer disadvantage on all attacks and grappling saves. Enemies get advantage on you with all attacks.
Suffer the effects of a broken ankle whilst wearing the armour. You can get a town smith to refit a piece of armour for you, depending on the adjustment score: Tier 2: 25% of armour's price. Tier 3: 40% of armour's price. Tier 4+: 50% of armour's price Note that the smith will need to be of sufficient skill to do this. A human smith won't know how to work faery metal, for instance.
See Armour Smithing for more information on refitting armour yourself.

item.title: Damage Calculations
item.description:
To determine the effect of an attack on someone, there are two layers of defense.Melee/Ranged defence is how you avoid getting hit at all from the respective attacks. This is determined by the AC system from DnD. You make an attack roll with relevant modifiers, and see if it's higher than the opponent's relevant defence score. If so, you hit. Otherwise, they dodge or parry or whatever, and you do no damage.Bear in mind you need to roll higher, not not higher than or equal to like in DnD 5e. Rolling equal to the enemy's defence will give the choice of succeeding the attack with complications or failing.By default, all races have a base melee and ranged defence of 10, apart from crocodilians who only have 8 ranged defence.This simply refers to normal damage that is affected by the armour and penetration mechanics detailed below. It is distinct from Blunt Force Trauma and Direct Damage. If not otherwise stated, whenever you see "damage" in this wiki, it is referring to regular damage.
Direct damage is distinct from regular damage, it is not affected by armour and penetration mechanics. Direct damage is typically used for status effects like bleeding and burning. Depending on the source, direct damage may be subject to certain effects. For example, direct damage from burning is reduced by the Lightbearer path, and direct damage from Neurotoxin bypasses temporary health.The regular damage of the attack is negated by armour. Simply subtract the armour value from the regular damage.Some weapons/moves have penetration values. Penetration reduces the armour value by that amount during damage calculations.This is how much armour you have left after accounting for the attacker's penetration stat. Essentially it's just (your armour) - (enemy's penetration). Effective armour cannot drop below 0.Some weapons/moves deal blunt force. This damage ignores armour and serves as additional damage on top of your regular damage. By default, all values are rounded up.For example, if you use a melee attack with these values:Strength: 2 Dexterity: 2 Hit chance: +Dexterity Damage: 1d6 + 2 Penetration: +2 Blunt Force Trauma: +StrengthAgainst an enemy with these defences:Armour: 4 Melee defence: 12You would first roll a d20 and add your hit chance modifier. If this resulting value is higher than the enemy's melee defence, you hit.Let's say we rolled 11, we add our hit chance bonus modifier, which is +Dexterity. We have 2 Dexterity, so we add 2.Hit chance = 11 from d20 roll + 2 from modifier bonus = 13Since our hit chance of 13 is just greater than their melee defence of 12, we just barely hit!We must now roll for damage. Our regular damage is 1d6 + 2, meaning we roll a d6, then add the +2 modifier to the value.Let's say we roll a 4 on the d6, now the calculations are as follows:Add damage modifiers: 4 rolled damage + 2 modifier bonus damage = 6 regular damage before armourCalculate effective armour by subtracting penetration from it: 4 enemy armour - 2 penetration = 2 effective enemy armourCalculate how much regular damage we do by subtracting the enemy's effective armour: 6 regular damage - 2 effective enemy armour = 4 regular damage to enemyFinally, add on blunt damage, which in this case is our Strength: 4 regular damage + 2 blunt force trauma = 6 total damage to enemy's health.The enemy's effective melee defence divided by 20 gives you the odds of hitting. Effective melee defence = melee defence - hit chance.E.g. An enemy with 10 effective melee defence gives you 50% odds to hit them.To calculate the average value of a die, sum its minimum and maximum and divide by 2.E.g. The average of a d6 = (1 + 6) / 2 = 3.5

item.title: Goliaths
item.description:
Selectively bred and fed from the plentiful fields of the Aquatine Empire, Goliath horses are massive, towering far above even crocodilians and needing special equipment to just mount. These horses were made with only one purpose: War. The feared Imperial Pagoda Cataphracts rode upon these towering beasts, fully barded in layers of lamellar armour, delivering unstoppable charges. Even the mere sight of these instruments of war on the horizon was enough to drive many an army to rout. However, an ungodly size brings an ungodly appetite. With the fall of the empire and the breeding farms a distant memory, these giants are just another fading reminder of what once was. Average Height: 3m Average Weight: >2000kgHealth: 80 Armour: 0 Movement Speed: 7m Jump Distance: 3m Carrying Capacity: 600kg Temperament: 8 Charge Acceleration: 4 Charge Maneuverability: 0Melee Defense: 3 Ranged Defense: 3 Initiative: +0Strength: 10 Dexterity: 5 Endurance: 10Food Intake per day: 10 units Cost: Goliaths can no longer be found for sale.Hit chance: +Strength Damage: 0 Penetration: 0 Blunt Force Trauma: +Strength Total Range: 1m Optimal Range: 1mGoliaths are large enough for a secondary rider. The primary rider is the one who controls the horse. The secondary rider takes their turn together with the primary rider. There are two ways the secondary rider can be seated: Front-facing: The secondary rider shares the same view cone as the primary rider.
Rear-facing: The secondary rider's view cone is the opposite of the primary rider's, and they cannot perform charged weapon attacks when the horse is charging. Seating like this prevents both riders from being flanked. Takes a regular action to swap seating facings. Values are organised as such: (Hit chance | Damage | Penetration | BFT | Range) Values below serve as add-ons to the horse's base stats, apart from range. +S or +D means to add the horse's strength or dexterity modifier. +S/D means to add either strength or dexterity modifier, whichever is higher. +0 means no bonuses or maluses. =x means the value is set to x.(+0 | +0 | +0 | +0 | 1m) Regular action. Can only target enemies opposite of the horse's view cone.
The goliath can be fed 4 less units of food without suffering exhaustion penalties, at the cost of -1 to charge force and -1m to movement speed. Underfeeding the goliath at long rest will result in the downsides taking effect until the next long rest. Training time-unit cost: 4 The goliath can be fed 4 more units of food in order to gain +1 to charge force and +1m to movement speed. Overfeeding the goliath at long rest will result in the buffs taking effect until the next long rest. Training time-unit cost: 4
The goliath can no longer be moved. All negative effects inflicted on the goliath will have 1 fewer stack, down to a minimum of 1. Training time-unit cost: 4 Raise the charge maneuverability of the goliath by 1. Training time-unit cost: 4 Requires 2 tier 1 skills.
Deal double the run-over damage to enemies. Training time-unit cost: 8 Allows the goliath to move left/right with reference to their view cone at the penalty of double movement speed cost when doing so. You cannot charge sideways. Training time-unit cost: 8 Rider gains +2 to melee and ranged defence. Training time-unit cost: 8 Requires 2 tier 2 skills.
The goliath will automatically succeed all temperament checks.
The goliath cannot be stopped in its charge by enemies succeeding their run over saves. Training time-unit cost: 12

item.title: Destriers
item.description: Destriers are warhorses bred for size and power. Almost never seen in the hands of commoners, destriers are a status symbol for the rich or used for the spearheads of cavalry formations. Known for their obedience and bravery, destriers are the prime choice for a commander looking to deliver a devastating charge. Average Height: 1.8m Average Weight: 1000kgHealth: 50 Armour: 0 Movement Speed: 7m Jump Distance: 3m Carrying Capacity: 250kg Temperament: 6 Charge Acceleration: 3 Charge Maneuverability: 0Melee Defense: 5 Ranged Defense: 5 Initiative: +2Strength: 6 Dexterity: 4 Endurance: 6Food Intake per day: 5 units Cost: 4000gHit chance: +Strength Damage: 0 Penetration: 0 Blunt Force Trauma: +Strength Total Range: 1m Optimal Range: 1mValues are organised as such: (Hit chance | Damage | Penetration | BFT | Range) Values below serve as add-ons to the horse's base stats, apart from range. +S or +D means to add the horse's strength or dexterity modifier. +S/D means to add either strength or dexterity modifier, whichever is higher. +0 means no bonuses or maluses. =x means the value is set to x.(+0 | +0 | +0 | +0 | 1m) Regular action. You cannot charge sideways. Training time-unit cost: 8 Allows the destrier to spend half their movement speed in order to move up to 2m backwards without triggering opportunity attacks. item.title: Coursers
item.description: Coursers are horses bred for speed, generally smaller in size. Historically used by nomadic tribes and the faeries of the Old Numerian Empire, coursers are now seen all over the continent. They are used by civilians for courier work, general travel and their relatively low food upkeep. Whilst their smaller size results in weaker charges, militaries still make plenty use of coursers for horse archery, scouting or flanking and chasing down disorganised infantry. Average Height: 1.5m Average Weight: 400kgHealth: 40 Armour: 0 Movement Speed: 8m Jump Distance: 4m Carrying Capacity: 200kg Temperament: 4 Charge Acceleration: 2 Charge Maneuverability: 1Melee Defense: 7 Ranged Defense: 7 Initiative: +4Strength: 3 Dexterity: 5 Endurance: 5Food Intake per day: 4 units Cost: 2000gHit chance: +Strength Damage: 0 Penetration: 0 Blunt Force Trauma: +Strength Total Range: 1m Optimal Range: 1mValues are organised as such: (Hit chance | Damage | Penetration | BFT | Range) Values below serve as add-ons to the horse's base stats, apart from range. +S or +D means to add the horse's strength or dexterity modifier. +S/D means to add either strength or dexterity modifier, whichever is higher. +0 means no bonuses or maluses. =x means the value is set to x.(+0 | +0 | +0 | +0 | 1m) Regular action. Can only target enemies opposite of the horse's view cone. Allows the courser to turn 180 degrees at the cost of 2m movement speed. Training time-unit cost: 4 Allows the courser to move left/right with reference to their view cone at the penalty of double movement speed cost when doing so. You cannot charge sideways. Training time-unit cost: 4 Raise the charge maneuverability of the courser by 1. Training time-unit cost: 4 Requires 2 tier 1 skills. Allows the courser to spend half their movement speed in order to move up to 2m backwards without triggering opportunity attacks. Training time-unit cost: 8 Ranged attacks made during charges are no longer subject to view cone restrictions. Training time-unit cost: 8 Raise the temperament of the courser by 4. Training time-unit cost: 8 Requires 2 tier 2 skills. Raise the charge maneuverability of the courser by 1. Training time-unit cost: 12 Flanking attacks made on horseback deal +2 damage. Training time-unit cost: 12

item.title: Actions
item.description:
Each turn of combat, you get three expendable resources: Movement speed Regular action Bonus action Map tiles are 1m x 1m squares.Movement speed dictate how far you can move in a turn. You can take your actions and move in any order, including moving before and after you act.Distance calculation goes by the every second diagonal rule.You can move through allies but not enemies.
Each race has a default jump value, which is affected by equipment load. Jumping distance cannot exceed your movement speed.Regular action. Double your movement speed this turn.Dropping your weapon/helmet is a free action. Taking off armour is not possible in combat without serious penalty.Regular action. Free yourself/someone else, adding your strength | dexterity to a d20 roll. DC determined by the condition. Regular action. Improvised attacks have no bonuses to hit, and deal 1d4 damage with no penetration or blunt force trauma. Bonuses/Maluses may be given depending on context.Bonus action. The distance you jump is subtracted from your movement speed. You cannot jump without sufficient movement speed.
Picking up items takes a regular action unless you have quick hands. You can only pick things up within a 1m range.
Regular action. Allows you to swap your weapons and helmets from your equipment load as much as you want. If you have access to your backpack load, you can bring 1 item from it into your equipment load. This effect ends once you move/take an action.
See martial arts for the unarmed moveset.See the individual weapon pages under items for each weapon's moveset.

item.title: Human Paths (Numerian)
item.description:
Numerian human paths are specific perks that unlock at levels 3. They are upgraded at levels 6 and 9. Once a perk path is chosen, you cannot take the others. The tiers do not stack with each other.Paths represent a lifestyle your character embodies. You may choose not to take a path.The practice of self-immolation in New Illuminetres comes from a verse in the Bible, where an unnamed miner lit himself on fire so that his fellow workers could see and flee a collapsing mine. The practice is frowned upon by certain factions of the clergy, but what other way can allow one to feel as close to their god's embrace?Once you choose the lightbearer life, you are required to always be lightbearing. You must maintain a constant flame with you or close to you. Doing so will lower stress, whilst letting the flame burn out will make you gain stress.
Gain hit chance and damage equivalent to the number of burning stacks you have.
Burning deals half damage to you.
Gain hit chance and damage equivalent to the number of burning stacks you have.
Burning deals half damage to you.
When using fire coatings, missed attacks still inflict the burning effects.
Gain hit chance and damage equivalent to the number of burning stacks you have.
Burning deals half damage to you and can no longer kill you. It can only reduce you to 1 health.
When using fire coatings, missed attacks still inflict the burning effects.
Gain access to Beacon of Light.
Spend a bonus/regular action to double the number of burning stacks you have.
Doing so removes all poison, deadly poison and bleeding you currently have.
Can only be done if you are burning.
In the aftermath of The East-West War and the Tyranny of the Stars, some within New Illuminetres became jaded by the scale of death and destruction in the world. Resolving to never get blood on their hands, they turned to training and rearing fireflies, hoping that these divine creatures may show them the way out of the misery and decay of war.Once you choose the firefly life, you are required to be pacifist-ish. Whilst not necessarily opposed to violence, you abhor doing it yourself. You lose stress from interacting with small critters and gain severe stress from inflicting damage. You gain the ability to train and use fireflies in combat. When using fireflies, you are limited to two groups of fireflies, meaning you can only mark up to 2 allies/enemies at a time. You can recall fireflies from marking a target for free.
Gain access to Lamplighter.
Gain access to Lampshader. Allows you to choose to deal no damage when using weapon moves, allowing you to benefit from utility skills without gaining stress. (e.g. weapon moves that move you/move an enemy)
Gain access to Lamplighter.
Gain access to Lampshader.
Allows Lamplighter and Lampshader to be used with bonus actions. Allows you to choose to deal no damage when using weapon moves, allowing you to benefit from utility skills without gaining stress. (e.g. weapon moves that move you/move an enemy)
Gain access to Lamplighter.
Gain access to Lampshader.
Allows Lamplighter and Lampshader to be used with bonus actions.
Lamplighter and Lampshader can now affect 1 more person in a 1m radius. Allows you to choose to deal no damage when using weapon moves, allowing you to benefit from utility skills without gaining stress. (e.g. weapon moves that move you/move an enemy) Spend a regular action to mark an enemy within line of sight using fireflies, giving allies advantage to hit on the next attack. Spend a regular action to shield an ally within line of sight using fireflies, causing enemies disadvantage when attacking them. Some Numerians, fed up with the inaction and safe rhetoric from the clergy, take things into their own hands. To close your eyes and ignore the darkness will only invite further harm. To achieve a better tomorrow, some evils are necessary. The shadow lurks, so that the light may shine ever brighter.Once you choose the haunted life, you are required to always be haunting. You lose stress when slinking in the shadows, and gain stress from prolonged exposure to the light. Gain +1 hit chance when there is no enemy within 2m of you. (Flanked enemies don't count) Suffer -1 hit chance otherwise.
Attacks are unaffected by lighting. Gain +2 hit chance when there is no enemy within 2m of you. (Flanked enemies don't count) Suffer -2 hit chance otherwise.
Attacks are unaffected by lighting. Gain +3 hit chance when there is no enemy within 2m of you. (Flanked enemies don't count) Suffer -3 hit chance otherwise.
Attacks are unaffected by lighting.
Gain access to Perch of the Raven. Spend a bonus action to toggle a perch stance. During this stance, gain the following effects: Advantage on all ranged attacks. Lose the ability to move. All melee attacks against you count as flanking attacks.

item.title: Moment of Mortality
item.description:
If you are at or above half health, any killing blow will reduce you to 1 health instead.On reaching 0 health, instead of dying or being downed, you are instead given a choice:Accept your fate and go all out, one last time.You take your turn immediately and: Ignore all negative effects/injuries. Take no damage from any attacks. Get one guaranteed critical hit/success. At the end of your turn, you die. The rest of the party gains a vengeance buff, giving them one roll with advantage on anything for the rest of the session.Or you can...Tear your gaze away from the abyss to live another day.You: Fall unconscious and become unable to act for half a day, or for a length at the DM's discretion. Gain a permanent injury. Gain a temporary insanity. A list of potential injuries: Torn muscles: -1 Strength Torn tendons: -1 Dexterity Collapsed lungs: -1 Endurance Brain damage: -1 Intelligence Memory damage: -1 Wisdom Cut tongue: -1 Charisma. Become unable to speak if you get cut tongue twice.
Destroyed eye: -1 hit chance on all attacks. Become permanently blind upon losing both eyes. Damaged corneas: Become unable to see beyond 10m. Destroyed arm: Lose one arm, removing your ability to dual wield and wield two handed weapons with disadvantage. Remove your ability to wield anything on losing both arms.
Destroyed leg: Half your movement speed and jump distance. Become permanently prone on losing both legs. Amnesia: Forget things at the DM's convenience. Phobia: Become deathly afraid of the thing that caused the moment of mortality, refusing to use it, and suffering disadvantage against it.

item.title: Environment and Terrain
item.description:
Certain environmental factors will influence combat.Obstacles block movement and cannot be stood on. They function as cover and can obstruct attacks.
Refer to ranged attack height advantages and disadvantages for bonuses/maluses to ranged attacks when regarding ranged attacks.Difference in height between terrain is determined with an arbitrary "level" unit, representing roughly 1m difference in height.Navigating onto higher ground under duress requires a jump action. Each level requires 2m of jumping distance to reach. Alternatively, you can climb, which uses 2m of regular movement but requires a regular action per level.When attempting to use melee attacks at someone higher/lower than you, the weapon range takes height level into account. For instance, someone can use a 2m range melee attack on someone directly adjacent if they are on terrain 1 level higher or lower. Ranged attacks are also affected by this, but only when shooting from low ground to high ground. You can safely fall 2 levels before incurring damage. From the 3rd level on: Take 1d6 blunt force trauma for every level you fall. Difficult terrain represents terrain that is hard to navigate, such as thick mud or slippery floors.Moving across difficult terrain costs twice the movement points. Jumping is not affected.
Water prevents you from swinging your weapons properly. When swimming, you can only grapple or use weapon moves that can be used during grappling. If afflicted with statuses like prone when swimming, you will be inflicted with drowning instead.Swimming speed is determined by swimming skill.
If you have no skill, you cannot swim and will start drowning. With 1 skill, your swimming speed is 33% that of your normal movement. With 2 skill, your swimming speed is 66% that of your normal movement. With 3 skill, your swimming speed is the same as your normal movement. You cannot jump when swimming.
Certain items like fire bottles will leave a lingering area of effect. For such areas, you are afflicted with the effect when entering the area and when you end your turn on them. The affliction on entering the area is limited to once a turn, so you cannot proc the effect over and over by leaving and entering the area again and again.Debuffs inflicted when attacking in the dark are only applied when the target is in the dark, not the attacker.When attacking a target in the dark, all ranged weapons have their optimal range halved. In addition, hit chance is at disadvantage by 4 for all attacks.
Night Vision skill extends your vision in the dark by 1-3m, starting at 1m when at skill level 1 and increasing by 1m with each skill level. Night vision extending buffs work additively. (For instance, with level 3 night vision you would be able to see everything within 3m as normal. Using a torch with a 2m lighting radius, you would be able to see up to 2 + 3 = 5m.)

item.title: Pixies
item.description:
*Pixies are not playable characters, but rather a personal follower for a faery pc.Pixies are a tiny humanoid species who share a symbiotic relationship with Faeries. Pixies have four translucent wings sprouting from their back, allowing them to fly. Pixies possess incredible mastery over matter, allowing them to manipulate material to achieve certain effects. Akin to master chemists and engineers, Pixies lend their expertise to Faeries in exchange for food, shelter, safety and labour for the heavy tools and items Pixies cannot carry. The two species have a innate built-in connection, allowing them to work together much more efficiently and fluidly than any other two species.
Most pixies fall under the Conclave of the Steel Faeries, worshipping The Old Wildwoods. Pixies are usually introduced to a faery early on as a child in a formal ceremony of bonding. Most Pixies spend their entire lives with the same faery. Pixies who lose their faeries are usually re-bonded to a faery without a pixie. On occasion, exceptional pixies may choose to join an already bonded faery if they prove themselves to be exceptional as well. Pixies follow their faeries through the education system, preparing them for whatever trade they choose. Pixies also follow their faeries into mandatory military service, and are required to support them in case of war. Most pixies spend their lives on the Ear, and leaving the island requires special permission. Usually, only pixies tied to emissaries or professional soldiers are allowed to leave. Pixies that leave without permission are considered outcast and are forbidden from returning.Average height: 2cm (Males), 2cm (Females) Average weight: 0.005kg (Males), 0.005kg (Females) Lifespan: 150 yearsHealth: 2 Movement Speed: 10m Jump Distance: 10m Melee Defense: 20 Ranged Defense: 20 *pixies cannot carry or use any regular equipment, or be targeted in normal combat.
Pixies can choose to specialise in a certain field during level ups to grant their faeries some bonus.Pixies have a set amount of focus points, which recover 1 per short rest and all per long rest. The base amount is 1.
Pixies can turn produce 1 unit of faery reagents every long rest. Strength: -4 Dexterity: +4 Endurance: -4 Intelligence: +5
Pixies gain light mastery tiers for free at levels 3, 6 and 8. Pixies can help you on one skill check once per short rest.

item.title: Initiative and Turn Order
item.description: Combat starts on round 1. Once every person has taken their turn, the round ends and another begins. This continues until the battle is over.During a round, the order in which players and enemies go is determined by a zig-zag cycle. Once one zig-zag cycle is complete, the next begins until the round is over.Each side chooses a person who hasn't taken their turn this round to be next. Both chosen persons then roll their initiative against each other. The higher will get to determine who goes first. Both persons must take their turns before the next zig-zag cycle begins.In the event one party outnumbers the other, the zig-zag cycle will proceed as normal until the outnumbered side have all taken their turn, then those leftover will take their turns.

item.title: The Right Claw
item.description:
Originally a small fishing town, the right claw came to prominence after the founding of the Aquatine Empire in 703. The town gets its name from the geography it inhabits, looking like a claw on the right side of the map. The town holds economic significance in the empire, being the largest settlement with a port within the borders.The latest governor of the town was Pranav Mahit. The local captain of the guard was Hong Li Ma.
During the Tyranny of the Stars, the Right Claw remained one of only two Aquatine settlements that held out against the Nebulans until the end of the invasion, the other being the capital of Stonebasin. Despite the military victory, due to the surrounding lands being devastated by Stardust and Marander Gas, as well as the logistics of getting supplies to the town having long since broken into nothing, the Right Claw was abandoned.
A memorial to The Canaries was built within the town on request of Captain Li Ma, a reminder of their sacrifice. A blue oak sapling is planted in the middle of the memorial, a small beacon of hope in a wasteland.The blacksmith sells all weapons, apart from the specialist faction weapons. The melee weapons not sold are:
One-handed Flails / Two-handed Flails (Kingdom of Numeria)
One-handed Falces / Two-handed Falces (Wingard Collective)
Numerian Blades (Conclave of the Steel Faeries)
Berserker Chain (Steelscale Clan) The ranged weapons not sold are:
Arbalest (Kingdom of Numeria)
Hand Crossbows (Wingard Collective)
Muskets / Pistols (Conclave of the Steel Faeries)
Amber Lances (Steelscale Clan)
The blacksmith will only sell you moonspades and repeating crossbows with permission from the local rulers. The blacksmith also sells:
All body armours and helmets apart from faerian items.
Fletching kits
Smithing tools
Metal bars The local communal church has shrines to:
Tamira
Kiawan
New Illuminetres At the bustling markets, you can buy:
Bottles

Feathers
Hide
Leather
Timber
All food items except:
Faerian items, moonshine and concentrated alcohol. Due to shortages, all fish items are doubled in price.
Cooking implements
The herbalist sells all healing items apart from faerian items and drugs. You can also request the herbalist patch you up for 2g per health point.The houndmaster, Ulot Ragnar, sells dogs and dog armour. The party will need to prove they can take care of a dog, and can only buy 1 dog maximum.
Guard Dogs
Herd Dogs
War Dogs
The houndmaster sells all available dog armour.You can visit the library to look up specific knowledge. You can loan a book for 2 days for 50g. Books can increase a relevant utility skill by 1 whilst in your inventory. You can only loan 1 book at a time. Failing to return your book results in a further 5g late fee per day. You can visit the postmaster to deliver or receive messages. It costs 5g to deliver a message, and an additional 5g to have the postmaster write/read it if you are not literate.The current shipmaster, Sumi, is missing. His apprentice, Khaligudar is standing in.There is only one ship available, a small nimble craft that can carry ~8 people called the "Blue Jay". Khaligudar will sell it for 5000g
The local tailor sells all Clothing, Cloaks and Hats.They also sell:
Tailoring tools The blackmarket is not readily accessible. You will need to get in their good graces first.The blackmarket sells:
Drugs
Poisonous stuff
Sulfur

item.title: Aquatine Empire
item.description:
The Aquatine Empire is no more. Following the Tyranny of the Stars, almost all land within the Empire is covered by toxic Marander Gas, rendering growing crops and living impossible. The surviving Aquatine citizens are homeless refugees, seeking shelter in neighbouring lands. The only living things left in the empire's lands are a few scattered groups of crocodilians and the corpse fungus brought over by the Nebulan invaders.The information below details the legacy of the empire before it's destruction.
Founded in 703 by Augustine the Third, the Aquatine Empire holds fertile lands to the North-East of the continent, boasting the largest population of 60 million humans. Its capital alone holds a million within its mighty walls. After the East-West war in 1181, the Aquatine Empire holds a tentative peace with its neighbouring Kingdom of Numeria.The Aquatine Empire rules by absolute monarchy, with the latest emperor being Marcus Callier the First. Succession is determined by the Emperor's choice, and although the heir need not be related, they often are. Augustine the third founded the empire through conquest, merging together multiple peoples and their cultures. As such, the Aquatine Empire sees great diversity in both religion and races, especially in large cities and coastal settlements.
When the empire was founded, Augustine took the major gods of the people he conquered and put them into a huge pantheon. Under his orders, all religions and gods were to be considered equal, and the people could worship any or all of them, with one caveat: The worship of the gods comes second to the mandate of the emperor. The government is secular, if you don't count worship of the emperor himself.Despite its agrarian society, the Aquatine Empire still has a large proportion of middle class trade workers, and are probably the second most technologically advanced besides the faeries. Aquatine literacy and education rates are second only to the faeries.It's territory is divided into provinces, ruled over by local leaders appointed by the emperor.The Aquatine empire favours the use of disciplined, heavily armoured legions to form an impenetrable spearwall towards the enemy, before delivering devasting flanking charges by their famed pagoda cataphracts.
Elite shock troops can often be seen wielding Moonspades, able to deliver devastating hits and allowing for easy control of the enemy. Elite marksmen are usually seen wielding the Repeating Crossbow, firing hails of poisoned bolts on their targets.
The Aquatine people comprise of a diverse mix, with people bearing resemblances to east, south and south-east Asians in the real world.
The Aquatine people speak the Aquatine tongue, a common language enforced by Augustine, although dialects still exist in remote villages. Most also speak the Numerian tongue as a second language.

item.title: People of the Claw
item.description:
The Right Claw holds significance the first settlement to be attacked during the Tyranny of the Stars, as well as home to a plot of sabotage conducted by Numerian fanatics working with the Nebulans. The history books records the deeds those at the claw:
Succeeding from Captain Urumi in 1181 after his death during Kolantine's Folly, Captain Hong Li Ma served the claw for over 30 years. She is noted for heeding the early warnings given by The Canaries, and her preparations allowed The Right Claw to survive the Tyranny of the Stars. Despite the military victory, with the Claw surrounded by toxic Marander Gas at the end of the war and logistics completely breaking down, the town was abandoned, but not before a memorial was built to remember the sacrifice of The Canaries. Captain Li Ma went on to fight in The Last Legion, sailing north to meet the Nebulans on their home turf.
A relatively young firekeeper of New Illuminetres, Renly Smith moved to the Right Claw in 1209 as part of his pilgrimage. Enraptured by the local seafood and beaches, he chose to stay. Locals describe him as a nice, hardworking man. He spent much time helping others and trying to repair the reputation of New Illuminetres after The East-West War. During the Tyranny of the Stars, he stayed behind to help tend to the wounded soldiers and evacuate civilians.
The local houndmaster at the Claw, Ulot has a mixed parentage, with his mother being Aquatine and his father being Numerian. During the Insurrection at the Claw, he was placed under house arrest after a hound attack in the streets, but was later exonerated. An antisocial and somewhat nervous fellow, Ulot feels more at ease with his dogs than he does with people. During the Tyranny of the Stars, he lent his war hounds to aid in the defence of the Claw.

item.title: Batrician Polumous
item.description: The 7th Lightbringer of the Kingdom of Numeria. Batrician Polumous had humble beginnings, starting as an orphan who slowly worked his way up the ladder in the church of New Illuminetres. When a boy, a firekeeper saved him from a pack of wolves, sparking in him a religious fervour. He was said to possess incredible charisma, and the lay people viewed him as a relatable role model, as well as a champion of their rights. Batrician believed in the supremacy of New Illuminetres, viewing those that did not believe in it as dangerous and lacking in morals.He was made Lightbringer in 1175, after the passing of his predecessor. Although not popular amongst the elite classes due to his rhetoric of religious extremism straining relations with the neighbouring nations, he was still elected due to his sheer public popularity.

item.title: The War of the Meadows
item.description:
In 627, the old Numerian Empire led by the faery king Montegra Allera declared war on the small neighbouring Kingdom of East Elizabeth, now known as Stonebasin. Montegra was a corrupt leader and not a good king, spending more time indulging in his own desires rather than ruling the people. He was said to be cruel and harsh to those who stood up against him, but despite his attempt to keep the populace in an iron grip, resistance was slowly but surely mounting against him, and it was only a matter of time before full blown revolt would occur. So, Montegra decided to take heat off of himself by directing hatred and attention outwards.Tensions between the faeries and their neighbouring humans had been rising. Humans were slowly becoming less and less dependent on the faeries as they developed their own technology and society. In paticular, agricultural breakthroughs had allowed the humans to finally surpass the faeries and pixies in population. Montegra spun a rhetoric of putting the humans in their place, exaggerating the threat the humans posed, and used that as a pretext to launch an invasion, distracting from his many shortcomings as ruler.
The war was long and bloody. Whilst Montegra had successfully convinced his subjects to unite against a common enemy, he had also provided the divided humans a reason to unite at last. Although faerian technology allowed them to carve deep swaths into the Crosslands, the sheer number of humans and their dogged resistance proved too much. Slowly but surely, the faeries were ground down in a war of attrition. The War of the Meadows was by far the bloodiest conflict in the history of the continent, up until the Tyranny of the Stars. It is believed that 10 million lost their lives, accounting for over 40% of the faery, pixie and human population at the time, mostly by the famines and diseases that followed the brutal scorched earth tactics used on both sides.Eventually, the humans won with the faeries finally cementing their defeat with the ousting and execution of Montegra Allera.
After the war, both human and faery societies were a shadow of their former selves. The faeries retreated to the Ear, forming the Conclave of the Steel Faeries, where they practiced policies of isolation, cutting off the rest of the world. The humans, without a common enemy and with the effects of famine and disease running rampant, started to fragment and turn on each other.

item.title: Lady Numeria
item.description:
The founder of the Old Numerian Empire. Not to be confused with the current Kingdom of Numeria, the Numerian Empire was an empire of faeries and pixies. Lady Numeria saw the establishment of extensive mining within the Numerian region, as well as the rapid technological advancement of the faeries. It is believed she was the one who pioneered the science of steel making.The way the faeries and pixies describe her, you would almost believe Lady Numeria to be a unicorn. Supposedly fearsome in battle, unrivalled in beauty and impossibly smart, over time the feats and accomplishments of Lady Numeria have been exaggerated and twisted in story after story, to the point where she more closely resembles a fictional legend than an actual historical figure.
As for what Lady Numeria was actually like, that remains a point of hot contention amongst faery scholars, but most agree that she was the one who founded the deadly art of the Numerian Blades. Curiously, there doesn't exist much information on who Lady Numeria's pixie was, if she had one. A popular theory was that her pixie gave their life to save her during their childhood, and out of respect, she chose not to bond with another.At the time, the Numerian Empire was undisputed in its strength and territory. The humans were still fragmented into small redimentary clans and villages, whilst the crocodilians were still battling for their place on the Serpent Archipelagos. The influence of the old Numerian Empire cannot be understated. The Numerian tongue as a lingua franca and most modern technology were popularised by the Numerian Empire, and the calendar's year 0 is marked by the founding of the empire.

item.title: Wingard Collective
item.description:
The Wingard Collective has no clear date of founding, as unlike the other nations, it resembles more of a informal coalition between different settlements in the Wingard desert. Historians place the estimate at around years 400-700. Due to the scarce resources in the southern desert, the Wingard Collective are relatively small in population, and rely heavily on trade. The Wingards are said to be the first to sail round the continent, and maintain a dominant navy to protect their trade routes.The Wingard Collective was created out of necessity and practicality, weaker city states coming together to protect themselves from the more powerful northern nations. They resemble an oligarchy in government style, with powerful merchants leading the decisions. After major strikes and an uprising in 1045, the Wingardian Union is also represented on the leading council.The dominant religion within the Wingard Collective is the Bodilustra, where worshipers accentuate individualism and worship their deity Bodil for calm seas and prosperous trade deals. In line with their culture of practicality over tradition, the Wingardians are considered to be the most progressive of the human nations. With manpower constantly in demand, the Wingardians find ways to squeeze use out of every single person within their borders. That means the women, the disabled, the old, the young, everyone has a place and a duty under the Wingard Collective.Unable to match the other factions in open pitched battle, the Wingardians utilise harassing maneuvers to cripple enemy logistics, using ambushes and denying their opponent a clean engagement. As such, they favour lightly armoured troops, usually wielding quick, concealable weapons such as short swords and bucklers.
The Wingardians' elite comes in the form of their marines, tasked with the crucial job of protecting their trade routes. Wingardian marines use the one-handed and two-handed falces, wicked forward curving blades that inflict horrendous injuries, often easily cutting off limbs and heads. In addition, in the close confines of ship-to-ship battle, the marines also utilise hand crossbows with poisoned bolts, able to quickly fire at multiple targets in the heat of battle.The Wingardians are fairly diverse, resembling the peoples of the Africa and the middle east in the real world.Wingardians speak the Wingardian tongue, although most also learn the Numerian tongue for trading purposes.

item.title: Dogs
item.description:
Dogs serve as companions alongside your party, and can impose certain benefits alongside them. There are several different breeds of dogs, each with their own advantages and disadvantages. Dogs always come with the weasley miscreant trait. Dogs cannot carry items or perform skill checks for you.These dogs serve as early warning systems, informing you of impending enemies and excelling in hunting vermin. They are bred for their sensitive noses, but not their strength or power, so be wary of sending them head first into battle. item.title: Donkeys
item.description: Not actually a horse, donkeys are not suited to speed or warfare, but are superior to horses in terms of carrying weight and needing less food relative to their size. Mules are considered donkeys for gameplay purposes.
