item.title: Aquatine Pantheon
item.description:
The aquatine pantheon of the Aquatine Empire comprises of several gods and religions. Whilst many citizens are religious, religion generally doesn't play as important a role in Aquatine culture compared to others.Worshippers believe in a form of karma, where good deeds will come round to you, and so will bad deeds. Reincarnation is also a prominent belief. This religion is most often seen in rural areas.Monks and Nuns make up most of the clergy. Apart from local monastery leaders, there isn't a higher form of leadership within the clergy. Monks and Nuns live a simple, ascetic life, often performing menial tasks and labour in the local villages in exchange for food.Local monasteries are usually modest, not very distinct from any other village building. One may occasionally see small shrines in shared temples.The first disciple, Rashak is often mentioned by name and in scripture as a role model.Followers have no clothing restrictions, but jewelry and opulent clothes are not commonly seen. Most believers are vegetarian.
Jin Jiang, also known as the golden general, is a diety of war, strength and perseverance. Brought to the Aquatine Empire by Augustine the Third himself, the general makes a appearance within the forts, barracks and castles of the empire. The general's faithful silver raven, Yin Ya, is often depicted with him.There are no official clergy for the golden general, but most soldiers have his name in their war cries. Outstanding soldiers or generals are seen to be channeling his presence.Shrines to Jin Jiang can be found in barracks and training halls, but the image of the general appears the most often on banners and heraldry.Jin Jiang is typically portrayed as a tall bearded man clad in heavy gold armour, wielding a moonspade.All imperial legions carry a tamed silver raven as a mascot. To lose or have the raven die is considered a bad omen.Kiawan is a god of scholars, enlightenment and knowledge. Usually worshipped by tradesmen and students cramming last minute before the trade exams.Clergy take the form of scholars. Scholars are usually invited to give a prayer before major exams and graduations.Shrines to Kiawan can be found in every school and college.Kiawan is usually depicted as an old man with long, braided hair, wearing long neat robes and carrying a scroll and a quill.Students swear in their integrity before Kiawan. Educators have to follow this religion, although there isn't much you need to do to be a follower of Kiawan.Tamira is a goddess of crops and rain. The most popular diety within the Aquatine Empire for obvious reasons. Tamira is represented in practically every corner of the empire. Despite originally being a simple folk goddess, she has since bloomed into dominance.Clergy take the form of Rain Dancers. Rain Dancers will perform a dance ceremony during rainfall to encourage more rain, as well as after to thank Tamira.Shrines to Tamira can be found in every village that does any form of farming. Temples can be found in large farms. Tamira is the only diety with her own dedicated temple in the empire.Tamira is usually depicted as a young woman in a simple dress, holding a shepherd's cane with a bell.Rain Dancers usually wear specialised straw hats, with small bells hanging off the rim. They dance with a rain fan, and sometimes with umbrellas. A festival of rain is held annually, usually during the monsoon season.

item.title: Horse Complications
item.description:
Whenever a horse fails a temperament check, it panics, rolling one of these complications.
The horse bucks the rider off, knocking them prone, roll a d12 to see where they land.
The horse charges in a random direction for all it's remaining movement, rolling a d8 to determine direction. This will run over anyone in the way. Horses take their built up charge force as blunt force trauma if they run into an obstacle. The horse turns and kicks the closest person. If no one is in range, it will turn at kick in the direction of the nearest person. The horse turns and runs away from the enemy for all it's remaining movement.

item.title: Old Numerian Empire
item.description:
The Old Numerian Empire is no more. Following The War of the Meadows, the last faery king Montegra Allera was executed, and the steel faeries retreated to the isle of the Ear to form the Conclave of the Steel Faeries.The information below details the legacy of the Old Numerian Empire before it's dissolution.
Not to be confused with the Kingdom of Numeria, the Old Numerian Empire was one of steel faeries and pixies. The founding of the empire marks year 0 of the Numerian calendar in use today. The first major empire and the longest lasting in the history of the continent, the Old Numerian Empire's influence on the world can still be felt centuries later. Led by and named after the mythical Lady Numeria, the old empire saw the spread of technology and a common tongue across the lands. At its height, the empire stretched from the west coast until the Raven's River. Although outnumbered by their neighbouring humans, the faeries and pixies were able to push out the divided human tribes and petty kingdoms, making good use of their own technological superiority.
The Old Numerian Empire practices absolute monarchy, with succession usually determined by bloodline or noble status. Prior to the actions of Lady Numeria, the steel faeries and pixies of the continent were divided into different houses, usually jealously guarding their own prized research and knowledge from the others. With blade, word, marriage and gold alike, Lady Numeria brought the houses together, combining their research and knowledge.With the advancement in research, steel making became a major component of the empire's foundations. The old empire saw the establishment of numerous mines within the Numerian region of the continent, alongside a robust industry and military. Thanks to the relatively longer life-spans of faeries and pixies compared to the other races, the empire enjoyed a more stable regime, where good rulers would stay on the throne longer and have more time to sire and train a worthy heir.
A distinctive anomaly that has carried over to the current day Conclave of the Steel Faeries is the fascination and legend surrounding the founder, Lady Numeria. Despite being arguably the most important figure in the history of the continent, information on the lady is extremely unclear and full of holes. Given the diligent history and book keepers of the faeries, this is an oddity not understood by scholars even in the present day. Theories on why this is run rampant, but no evidence can definitively prove one way or the other.
In it's early conquests, the old empire was famed for its use of Numerian Blades, founded by Lady Numeria herself. Making use of the faery's natural agility alongside the deadly properties of pixie alchemy, the elite blade dancers of the empire were the dominant military force of the continent for centuries.Steel faeries and pixies are predominantly pale in skin colour with dark hair and eyes.The Numerian tongue was spread as a lingua franca by the empire, but predates the old empire itself. Believed to have come from Lady Numeria prior to being popularised, it's true origins remain something of a mystery.

item.title: Conclave of the Steel Faeries
item.description:
Thanks to their symbiotic relationship with Pixies, Faeries are the most technologically advanced race on the continent. Boasting better metallurgy and craftsmanship than any other race, faeries are also known for their use of gunpowder, albeit not widespreadly. Their single city, The Citadel, is one of the most efficient, clean and comfortable to live in. Although smaller in size, it rivals even Stonebasin with a population close to a million. The steel faeries once held dominion over all lands east of the Numerian mountains, but after a disastrous defeat to a human coalition in the War of the Meadows, they were pushed back to the isle of the Ear. A tentative peace period settled, and a new status quo emerged to be undisturbed for centuries.
The conclave is a republic with three head senators sharing power. Elections are held every 20 years. The latest senators are Yosia Numen, Tory Allador and Ellyia Olldenhammer. The new conclave was founded after the steel faeries' defeat in the war of the meadows in 627, leading to the ousting and subsequent execution of then dictator Montegra Allera. The faeries mainly worship The Old Wildwoods, although more and more are turning agnostic in the wake of the metallurgy revolution.Steel faeries are largely isolationist, only maintaining an embassy fort on the mainland. Advanced technology, the relative abundance of the Ear and their use of sea mining allows them to be largely self-sufficient.
The first Faerian ruler and founder of the old Faerian empire, Lady Numeria, is idolised and revered almost as a saint.The conclave practices mandatory military service for faery and pixie alike. On the battlefield, faeries utilise their superior mobility to deny and outflank the enemy, using their pixie's alchemic abilities to sow chaos and carve bloody holes in the enemy frontlines.
Elite troops can often be seen wielding numerian blades, popularised by Lady Numeria herself, dancing around the battlefield delivering quick and deadly cuts. The powder corps of the conclave wield the musket and pistol. Not many have heard the thunder of pixie gunpowder, but those that have remember it for the rest of their lives.Steel faeries and pixies are predominantly pale in skin colour with dark hair and eyes, although it is not uncommon for higher class faeries to engage in cosmetic surgery to change their appearance.Faeries are the ones who created the Numerian tongue, being the original occupants of the Numerian region. Due to this, the Numerian tongue has an incredibly long history, and also serves as the lingua franca of the continent.
The Citadel
Faerian Embassy

item.title: Stardust
item.description:
Emitted by the Nebulans, stardust is a shimmering mist like substance. It is fatal to all living creatures, with the exception of the Nebulans and some of the crops they grow. Stardust kills in seconds, causing internal organs and blood vessels to rapidly decay and fail. Those exposed to it often cough up blood and bleed from their eyes, nose and ears. Exposure does not mean instant death, as these effects only happen when lingering within the mist itself. However, recovery is a lengthy process, and most survivors are left disabled.Besides its lethality, stardust also has some other curious properties. It cannot be displaced by wind, and unlike other gases, does not disperse or diffuse on its own, lingering in the same spot. In addition, it cannot be contained, leaking through any container and rendering any protective breathing apparatus useless.
During the Tyranny of the Stars, the Conclave of the Steel Faeries managed to find a way to counter stardust by chemically turning it into Marander Gas. The process is very fast, but Marander Gas comes with its own complications too.

item.title: Food
item.description:
Food has 3 tiers of spoilage: Fresh: Yummers. Spoiling: Make a DC 12 endurance save or the effects of the food are negated, and you gain minor food poisoning.
Rotten: Make a DC 20 endurance save or the effects of the food are negated, and you gain major food poisoning. Each food item has a spoilage timer. After a fresh food item's spoilage timer expires, it will progress to become spoiling. After another day, it will become rotten.Each food item has a variety value. A meal made during long rest can give benefits depending on variety.Each food type can only confer its variety bonus once.Usually, you can only eat 2 units of food, limiting the variety of your meal. However, you may choose to attempt to make a communal meal. Communal meals can achieve greater variety by allowing you to cook everyone's portions together, thus using more ingredients. This requires a cooking check of DC 5 + variety of the meal. Failing this check imposes a 1d4 penalty to the variety of the final meal.These bonuses are subject to change depending on the size of the group. Bland (<2): No bonuses. Decent (2-4): -1 Stress. Sumptuous (5-8): -2 Stress, +1d4 temporary health. Decadent (8-10): -3 Stress, +1d6 temporary health and +1 to any core stat of your choice until next long rest. Fit for a king (>10): -4 Stress, +1d8 temporary health and +2 to any core stat of your choice until next long rest. Bland (<2): No bonuses. Decent (2-3): -1 Stress. Sumptuous (4-5): -2 Stress, +1d4 temporary health. Decadent (6-8): -3 Stress, +1d6 temporary health and +1 to any core stat of your choice until next long rest. Fit for a king (>8): -4 Stress, +1d8 temporary health and +2 to any core stat of your choice until next long rest. Bland (<1): No bonuses. Decent (1-2): -1 Stress. Sumptuous (3-4): -2 Stress, +1d4 temporary health. Decadent (4-6): -3 Stress, +1d6 temporary health and +1 to any core stat of your choice until next long rest. Fit for a king (>6): -4 Stress, +1d8 temporary health and +2 to any core stat of your choice until next long rest. Food prices are subject to availability in the region. All food weighs 1kg per unit. Raw food can be made into their cooked versions at a fire unless stated otherwise.Accoutrements provide no nutrition, but can be used in cooking to provide variety. Each spice can only provide its variety bonus once per meal. These items have no weight.You cannot survive off of alcohol alone. Each unit of alcohol weighs 1kg. Drinking takes a bonus action/regular action.
Grants 1/2 level of drunkenness if drunk. Cost per unit: 1g
Grants 1 levels of drunkenness if drunk. Variety: 1
Acts as an accoutrement. Cost per unit: 100g
Grants 2 levels of drunkenness if drunk. Not normally sold in towns. Cost per unit: 10g
Grants 3 levels of drunkenness if drunk. Not normally sold in towns. Cost per unit: 50g

item.title: Marander Gas
item.description:
A yellowish-green gas, Marander Gas was originally discovered by Pixies attempting to create weapons for the Conclave of the Steel Faeries. Although thoroughly studied, the use of the gas as a weapon was eventually discarded due to a few reasons: The process to produce Marander Gas was too intensive and laborious, considering the amount needed to effectively cover an area. The process to break down Marander Gas was equally intensive and laborious, making it hard to clean up battlefields and avoid unwanted collateral damage.
Marander Gas is toxic to most living beings, causing death over minutes due to respiratory failure. In plants, it causes their chlorophyll to breakdown, leading to death. However, Crocodilians are immune to the gas, able to function relatively fine within it. In addition, the conclave has breathing equipment capable of filtering the gas, allowing for safe exposure.
During the Tyranny of the Stars, the Conclave of the Steel Faeries managed to find a way to turn Stardust into Marander Gas. The chemical process is quick, and is the major reason for the continent's ability to repel the Nebulans.

item.title: Cannon Shot
item.description:
Each shot has a weight of 1kg. Cannon shots cannot be recovered. No bonuses/maluses. Cost: 1000g Converts blunt force trauma into regular damage. Hit chance: -1 Penetration: +10 Cost: 500g -1 d6 from the blunt force trauma roll. Gains advantage to hit when targeting sails. Overkill damage will carry over to other sails. Cost: 1500g Hit chance: -4 Blunt Force Trauma: (1d6) * d12 Optimal Range: -50m
Similar to Throwables, the user makes a DC15 Int check. Failing will result in the targeting being 1m off to either side, determined by a coin flip. Covers a 3m wide line from the cannon. The first person in each line has to defend against d6 projectiles. The projectiles do not have disadvantage against humanoid or smaller targets. This projectile does not pierce. Cost: 1500g Deals an additional 3d6 blunt force trauma in a 1m around impact, and half that at 2m around impact. When missing, splash damage is still applied at the area of impact.
Inflicts shellshock(1), DC15. This projectile does not pierce. Cost: 2000g Deals an additional 12d6 blunt force trauma in a 3m radius around impact, and half that from 3-6m around impact. When missing, splash damage is still applied at the area of impact.
Inflicts shellshock(3), guarenteed. This projectile does not pierce. Cost: 20000g

item.title: Rolling Dice
item.description:
This system uses d20 for hit chance and skill checks, rolled against the difficulty class (DC) of a certain task. You succeed if your roll is greater than the DC. Most of the time, you'll add a modifier to the roll depending on what relevant stats/skills you have. All values are rounded up.When rolling any check, if your roll matches the difficulty check exactly, you succeed at some cost. For attacks, whether the cost is a minor or major depends on proficiency. For everything else, it will usually be a major complication. The enemy gets in a counter attack. If you are at ranged and the enemy cannot reach you, another ranged enemy will make the attack if possible. If not, then reroll the complication. Your weapon/hand gets stuck. The thing can be stuck in the enemy or ground, preventing you from using it and removing the melee defense bonuses from it. Moving away/The enemy moving away will cause you to leave your weapon stuck in whatever it's in. In the case of martial arts, this will cause your next attack to be at disadvantage/enemies to have advantage against your next grappling attempt.
Requires a free action, DC12. Failing the action will still allow you to free your weapon, but your next attack will be at disadvantage. Free action can be done by someone else. Your weapon glances, doing half damage, pen and BFT.
You fumble and get dazed(1), no save. Your foot gets stuck. You become unable to move, including weapon moves that move you.
Requires a free action, DC12. Failing the action will still allow you to free your foot, but your next attack will be at disadvantage. Free action can be done by someone else. You expose yourself, the next attack against you has advantage/you have disadvantage on your next grappling saving throw until your next turn. You accidentally hit yourself for half the effect too. If the effect cannot be halved, then you take the full brunt of the action. You drop your weapon. If unarmed, drop something else in your equipment load at random. Subject to change based on situation. Your tool/item gets destroyed/disabled temporarily. You make a bunch of noise. You trip and fall on your ass. You twist something and gain disadvantage on some skill/stat. The enemy gets in a counter attack at disadvantage. If you are at ranged and the enemy cannot reach you, another ranged enemy will make the attack if possible. If not, then reroll the complication. Your weapon/hand gets slightly stuck. The thing can be stuck in the enemy or ground, preventing you from using it and removing the melee defense bonuses from it. Moving away/The enemy moving away will cause your weapon to be free, but your next attack will have disadvantage. In case of martial arts, the enemy will have advantage on saves against your next grappling attempt.
Requires a free action, DC0. Free action can be done by someone else. If stuck on an enemy, you can also free yourself by using a move that moves you/the enemy. Your foot gets slightly stuck. You become unable to move, including weapon moves that move you.
Requires a free action, DC0. Free action can be done by someone else.
You fumble and get dazed(1), DC10. When you roll a natural 1, you always fail the roll regardless of any modifiers or the DC. In addition, you suffer some form of catastrophic consequence.When you roll a natural 20, you always succeed the roll regardless of how high the DC is. In addition, you gain some tremendous benefit.If you score a critical hit on an attack you: Double your regular damage, penetration and blunt force trauma. Any damage rolls use their maximum value. Exceptional events are awarded with inspiration points. Inspiration points can be spent to reroll any roll you make, and you can have a maximum of 3 points.Inspiration is awarded when doing things like being creative, engaging in roleplay etc.

item.title: Ranged Attacks
item.description:
To make ranged gameplay more interesting than just siting in the back shooting all day, I decided to introduce some new mechanics to make ranged gameplay more interesting.Each weapon type now has a unique set of moves. Moves can be unlocked by investing proficiency points during level ups.Each ranged weapon now has three values tied to range: Optimal Range, Range Penalty and Maximum Range.Imagine a weapon's total range is cut up into intervals, which each interval being the same length as its optimal range. The weapon incurs one instance of range penalty for every interval of the optimal range.For every interval of the optimal range, suffer some defined penalty. There is a maximum amount of range penalties that can be applied. Damage cannot be reduced below 1, penetration and blunt force trauma cannot be reduced below 0.Weapons cannot shoot past this.For instance, let's say a weapon has an optimal range of 5m, and a range penalty of -1 hit chance that can be applied 5 times. At 6m, the weapon would incur -1 hit chance. For every additional 5m after, it would incur an additional -1 hit chance. Once the maximum -5 hit chance penalty has been reached at 26m, no further penalties will be incurred.Ranged attacks behave the same as melee attacks when it comes to view cone restrictions and flanking fire, with the exception that view cone stretching does not apply to ranged attacks.Most ranged weapons have relatively flat trajectories, meaning line-of-sight is now a mechanic. No more shooting through the back of your fighter into the enemy. First, see if you can even see the target. If you cannot draw an unobstructed line from any corner of your tile to any corner of the target's, you cannot see them. If you can see the target, draw a line from any corner of your character's tile to the center of the target's. If the line is obstructed, roll with disadvantage for hit chance: If both rolls succeed: You hit anyway. If one roll succeeds: You hit the obstruction instead. If both rolls fail: You don't hit. If there is more than one obstruction, they are considered fully obstructed and you cannot hit the target at all. If your target is at a lower elevation compared to you, roll with advantage for hit chance. If your target is at a higher elevation compared to you, roll with disadvantage for hit chance.Advantage/Disadvantage can cancel each other out (e.g. shooting from high ground at an obstructed target will result in a normal hit chance roll)Advantage/Disadvantages do not stack (e.g. shooting from low ground at an obstructed target will result in a regular disadvantaged roll)Ranged attacks suffer disadvantage to hit chance if you're within or closer than the default optimal range of an enemy's melee weapon.
This does not apply if you're flanking the enemy.

item.title: Money
item.description: For the sake of simplicity, 1 gold coin = 10 silver coins = 10 copper coins.To avoid complete economic meltdown, equipment you strip off of dead people will only sell back to the traders for 10% of what it's worth.Fresh stuff not pried off of dead bodies will be worth 50% instead.

item.title: The Way of the Sea
item.description: The Way of the Sea is a philosophy adopted by the Steelscale Clan. Followers don't believe in any one god, instead focusing on living life in the moment, untethered by responsibility to a higher power. Other than this, interpretations vary quite a bit from individual to individual. Some believe one should be flexible, like the ebbing flow of the tides, whilst others believe one should be firm and unrelenting, like a fierce impassable typhon. Others yet believe one should be tenacious and stand by their beliefs, like how the waves consistently splashing on shore will eventually erode stone into sand.By nature, there exists no clergy for the way of the sea. Some prominent leaders in the steelscale clan are considered to be philosophers, and young crocodilians may seek out their guidance.By nature, there exists no buildings for the way of the sea.By nature, there are no figureheads for the way of the sea.Crocodilians frequently hold competitions between clans. Other than the Blood Rites, which is held every two years to determine the ruling clan, there is also the rite of the sea, held every year. During the rite of the sea, competitors participate in sports like swimming, wrestling, throwing, sprinting and so on, like a crocodilian version of the Olympics.

item.title: New Illuminetres
item.description: New Illuminetres, or just Illuminetres, is the major religion of the Kingdom of Numeria. Followers worship the god Illum, who is seen as an all-powerful god. Illuminetres pervades almost every aspect of life in the kingdom, being part of the government itself.The clergy of New Illuminetres practice a strict hierarchy, with the following ranks: Lightbringer. The religious head. Oversees the entire kingdom, as well as emissaries in foreign lands. High overseers. Oversees religious practices of large cities and castles. Usually, they have multiple overseers as their direct subordinates. Overseers. Oversees religious practices of villages and smaller settlements. Usually, they have multiple firekeepers as their direct subordinates. Firekeepers. The lowest rank of clergy, being ordained to practice simple rites. They serve under and help overseers. Monks and Nuns. Un-ordained members who fulfil most of the menial tasks. Churches to Illum are found in every settlement within New Illuminetres, as is mandated by law. Most larger settlements have cathedrals, signifying the seat of a high overseer. The House of Light in the city of Golden Seat is the largest and most prestigious.Most churches and cathedrals feature a stained glass ceiling, as to let in Illum's grace.Illum is not represented as any living being, but rather as an abstract concept of light. As such, depictions often include fire and the sun. Titus Godwin, the first king of the Kingdom of Numeria is revered as a saint.Fireflies are considered sacred creatures, and are a common sight in the gardens of churches.Every Monday, worshippers will gather at dawn for a mass at their local church, usually carried out by an overseer. This mass is known as the mass of sunrise, and signifies Illum's blessing to the start of the week. Likewise, every Sunday worshippers will gather at sunset for a mass of sunset, signifying gratitude for Illum's guidance throughout the week.Clergy of New Illuminetres frequently go on missions, walking the continent to spread the word of their religion.Each church has a duty to maintain an ever burning flame within a stone pit, meant to signify ever lasting worship and connection to Illum. Negligence to maintain this flame will result in the responsible clergy being expelled from the holy order, and purposely putting it out carries the death penalty.Most families are provided with a special lantern from their local churches, and most choose to light it at night and hang it from their doorstep, as a way to show their worship and to ward off bad omens.

item.title: The Old Wildwoods
item.description:
The Old Wildwoods is the oldest known religion in the world, predominantly worshipped by the Conclave of the Steel Faeries. With recent technological advancements, more and more faeries are opting to become atheist or agnostic instead, but majority of the faeries still believe in the old wildwoods. Worshippers believe the land to have a spirit and mind of its own, and is the major reason why the steel faeries haven't absolutely ruined the environment in their attempts to extract more resources for their ever-growing demands.Clergy take the form of rangers. Faery rangers are responsible for appraising the quality of wildlife, plants and assessing pollution to the land, acting as guardians to keep land exploitation in check. As the faeries turn more and more to sea mining, the rangers' duties have expanded to encompass the sea as well.The Old Wildwoods don't have dedicated buildings. Worshippers will often choose to congregate or pray in gardens, parks or the wilderness instead.
Although not intrinsically linked to the religion, Lady Numeria, first founder and ruler of the old faerian empire was said to be highly connected to nature and is considered a saint and role model.Every year, worshippers will choose to shed their technological comforts and hold a festival in the wilderness of the Ear. Even non-worshippers will usually opt to participate in the revelry and festivities. Failure to take care of the environment is seen as shirking you duty to society, and it's believed the wildwoods will take their vengeance on any transgressors eventually.

item.title: Church of the Nebula
item.description:
The church of the nebula is the major religion of the Nebulan Empire. Followers worship the night sky and stars, believing that the stars determine the divine fate of their people. Nebulan society is deeply connected with the stars, so much so that being part of the church isn't considered a religion, but rather a essential part of their being and way of life. The Nebulans know nothing else, although disputes between how they interpret the stars are common.
Nebulans have no defined clergy, but do have stargazers, fortune tellers who read the stars to tell fate.
The Nebulans invented large telescopes in order to see the stars better. Observatories are commonly seen within their settlements.The phases of the moon is deeply tied to Nebulan culture. Interpretations vary, but a common one is that the full moon represents bold action and daring whilst the new moon represents restraint.
Stargazing is an avid past time, and the mist produced by the Nebulans has an ethereal, shimmering nature to it, like stars twinkling in the night sky.
The sighting of a falling star signifies a call for bloodshed and war. The Nebulans believe the stars are their domain, and all land that falls under it belong to them by right.

item.title: Bodilustra
item.description: Bodilustra is the major religion of the Wingard Collective. Followers worship the god Bodil, whose domain is that of the sea, the counting scale and the individual. Bodil's name is often used in trade deals as a way of swearing integrity.Clergy take the form of priests. Priests take care of and maintain the temples of Bodil in the Wingardian settlements, and also perform rite of prosperity. They also serve as adjudicators in trade disputes.Major churches are located within the two major Wingardian settlements, with plenty of statues dotted about.There is no one single depiction of Bodil. Their clothing and appearance changes often, usually resembling a person of ambiguous gender. One trait that does remain constant is the fact that Bodil is always portrayed holding up a coin between two fingers.Most traders keep a coin with Bodil's image as a lucky charm. Traders also usually approach a temple to perform a rite of prosperity before a major deal. During this rite, participants play a simple game, such as the shell game, during which the priest will try to cheat. If the trader can see through the deceptions and win, they are considered lucky and blessed.

item.title: Augustine the Third
item.description: First emperor of the Aquatine Empire and its founder, Augustine the Third originally hailed from the Kingdom of West Elizabeth, now known as Stonebasin. After succeeding from his uncle as the new king, he proved a talented commander and strategist, conquering East Elizabeth in 701, and across the following 2 years coopted the rest of the Crosslands into his empire, either by word or by blade.Augustine the Third's military accomplishments, whilst impressive, was nothing particularly special at the time. Before the 700s, the Crosslands was a region engulfed by constant turmoil and war. It was not uncommon for a warlord to claim massive amounts of land, only for their "empire" to fragment and split back apart, sometimes even within the same year. Augustine the Third's ability to implement stable succession for centuries to come, crush his opponents and unite the varied peoples of the Crosslands under a common banner was what set him apart.Augustine united the religions of the people into one Aquatine pantheon, mandating worship of the Emperor come before any religion. One would expect such an action to face much resistance, but the official telling was that Augustine managed to persuade the people with his glorious vision, charming personality and sharp tongue. But, the history books within the Empire are sanctioned by the Emperor and don't contain the less glamourous side of Augustine or his policies. It's likely he made use of bribes, force and manipulation to make dissenters fall in line.Augustine also created a structured education and examination system, one which would come to shape Aquatine society for generations to come.

item.title: Insurrection at the Claw
item.description:
The month before the Tyranny of the Stars, The Right Claw saw many strange events occur, culminating in an undercover group of New Illuminetres fanatics attempting to burn down the town. The series of events are told as such:
Vessels have been going missing for weeks north of the town, until no one dared to sail out anymore. In light of this, numerous parties were dispatched to investigate. Amongst them were hired mercenaries by the town guildmaster, Marius Fishbach, consisting of Canary Squad from the Blue Hounds mercenary company, and the Wingardian military frigate, the Kelissa, carrying elite marines investigating missing Wingardian trade ships. The Conclave of the Steel Faeries also sent a powder corps scout to investigate the missing faery ship, the Grey Manta. In addition, a group of Numerian fishermen were left stranded at the town after the transport ship that was supposed to pick them up also went missing. These fishermen were later discovered to be undercover New Illuminetres fanatics, working for the Nebulans.
The night before the arrival of Canary Squad, a fire broke out at a warehouse near the docks. When the Wingardian Marines went out to investigate, a large explosion rocked the Kelissa. It did not sink, but was rendered unseaworthy. Lesser gunpowder was suspected to have been used in the bombing.
After Canary Squad arrived and began investigating the bombing of the Kelissa, an attempt was made on their lives the same night, with a Numerian fisherman named Billy releasing hounds in the street to attack them. The attack was ultimately unsuccessful, with a few dogs escaping in the darkness. After this, a curfew was put into effect, targeting the Numerian fishermen. The local houndmaster, Ulot Ragnar, was put under house arrest. Attempted interrogation of Billy revealed him to be a New Illuminetres fanatic.In the noon following the hound attack, another Numerian fisherman was found dead outside the town's walls, shot dead by a crossbow bolt from the walls before he was apparently going to meet with Canary Squad. A subsequent investigation also found the bodies of the escaped hounds left in the refuse pile of the Numerian refugee camp, apparently also shot dead by crossbow from the town's walls. A few suspected guards were put under house arrest.
After investigations by Canary Squad, the fanatics were discovered to have acquired lesser gunpowder by making their own with knowledge from a rogue pixie. Lesser gunpowder has 3 components: Charcoal, easily available.
Sulfur, regulated for medical use and banned in open transport. Although the law prohibited it, the local towns guard had a deal with the black-market, allowing sulfur caravans into the town. Traitor guardswoman Utari Sanjaya took advantage of this fact to arrange for the hijacking of one such caravan for use in making gunpowder.
Saltpetre, commonly found near rotting material. The real fishermen that the fanatics were posing as had arranged for the exhuming and relocating of the remains of the Numerian soldiers who fell during Kolantine's Folly for proper funerals back in Numeria. The fanatics took advantage of this fact to gather saltpetre from the mass grave of Numerian soldiers whilst masquerading as the fishermen. Furthermore, the fanatics began planned attacks on Blue Hounds as a whole in an attempt to stop their involvement, resulting in many casualties amongst the various mercenary squads.Canary squad also discovers the fanatics wielding crudely made falces, likely attempting to frame the Wingardian marines who use similar weapons in an attempt to sow further confusion.
As Canary Squad's investigation closed in on the fanatics, coupled with the imminent arrival of the Aquatine Empire's second Legion to reinforce and bring order to the town, the New Illuminetres fanatics decided to make a final stand. Having delayed the journey of the real fishermen so they could pose as them, the fanatics called them in in the middle of the night, causing much chaos and confusion. Taking advantage of this, they launched a coordinated attack. They blew up the Blue Hound safehouse, and torched anything they could get their hands on, hiding amongst the real fishermen to evade the town guards. With the help of The Canaries, the fanatics are eventually routed after the death of their leader, Thaddeus.
Whilst their actions were not fully understood at the time, with hindsight it appears the fanatics were part of the Shadows of the Nebulans, purposely trying to sabotage investigative efforts in an attempt to prevent the discovery of the Nebulan fleet before the invasion.

item.title: The East-West War
item.description:
In early Spring of 1181, tensions between the Aquatine Empire and the Kingdom of Numeria came to a head. Then Lightbringer, Batrician Polumous, held lofty ideals of a united human kingdom under New Illuminetres and was pushing hard for a crusade against the Aquatine Empire. Conditions in the Kingdom of Numeria were also tough. Mines were running dry, and the Kingdom found itself more and more reliant on the Aquatine Empire for food imports as its population boomed.
Soon, spurred by religious fervour and anger over increasing taxes on food imports from the Aquatines, the Kingdom of Numeria struck first, launching a two pronged assault to take the mines of Silver Sally and the village of Clay Murdock. Caught off-guard, the Aquatine Empire's military had become complacent and corrupt, resulting in much time being wasted as they scrambled to reorganise and ceded much territory to the Numerians.
Over the course of a year, the Aquatines were pushed back to the Raven river. Despite their territorial losses, the Aquatines had steadily purged the incompetent and corrupt from their ranks and were regaining strength. With imports of food cut off, the Numerian people begin to suffer from food shortages. This, coupled with the drain of manpower led to war fatigue quickly taking hold. The camel's back broke when Batrician Polumous himself was slain during the battle to take Raven's Throat, resulting in the religious fanatics losing influence in government. With neither side able to conclude a quick victory over the difficult terrain of the Raven river, both sides agreed to a peace settlement.
After the death of Batrician Polumous, the zealots lead by the High Overseer Kolantine attempted a desperate maneuver to break the stalemate at the Raven river by landing their elite paladin orders at The Right Claw by sea. The zealot fleet successfully staged a distraction and slipped past the Aquatine fleet, resulting in an uncontested landing. Although able to besiege the city, the city guard were able to repel the invaders long enough for the Aquatine calvary to arrive. Even worse, the zealot fleet was discovered and suffered a decisive defeat at the hands of the Aquatine's. Surrounded by troops with superior mobility and with no hope of resupply or rescue by sea, the paladins were slowly ground down in a bloody war of attrition. Kolantine did not survive.The Aquatines were forced to cede almost all territory west of the Raven river, but the taxes on food exports to the Kingdom of Numeria were not reduced. Many Aquatine citizens were displaced as a result, causing resentment and bitterness. The reputation of New Illuminetres as a whole has taken a large hit, and not just in the Aquatine Empire.In the Kingdom of Numeria, the original issue of food costs was not solved. The territory taken was not fertile like the lands in the crossland plains, resulting in many seeing the war as a waste of lives that only served to strain the relationship between the two nations.
Many of the most fanatical New Illuminetres worshipers were the first to volunteer for battle, and the first to fall early in the war. This, combined with Batrician Polumous' death resulted in the religious sentiment for war fading away. The fanatics were scape-goated and fell from grace, resulting in many still habouring resentment to this day, seeing Batrician Polumous as a rightful martyr.Despite the Numerians' victory, the war left them in arguably a weaker state, as their relations with their neighbours worsen and their food issue remains somewhat precarious.

item.title: The Laughing Titan
item.description: This is the name given to the continent inhabited by the humans, faeries, pixies and crocodilians. Up until the Tyranny of the Stars, it was the only known land tof these civilisations.

item.title: Isle of Andromeda
item.description: A small island located between the Eye of the Storm and the continent of the laughing titan. It's believed the island was used as a staging ground Shadows of the Nebulans who sided with the them during the Tyranny of the Stars, although they appear to have betrayed or been betrayed by the Nebulans. When The Last Legion arrived, they found the isle covered in stardust, alongside the bodies of numerous Numerians, including high overseer Gehang Mannlicher and faery traitor Ulysses and his pixie Basilan. Alongside them were the bodies of The Canaries and the ships that had gone missing in the months leading up to the Nebulan invasion. Whatever exactly transpired on the island remains unknown, but it is believed the scouting force discovered the Nebulan plans for invasion there, sending ravens to The Right Claw and The Citadel warning of it before perishing in combat with the Nebulans and their supporters.

item.title: Eye of the Storm
item.description: Homeland of the Nebulans, the Eye of the Storm is a continent located far North of the continent of the laughing titan. The continent is covered in extensive underground caves, featuring many glowing crystalline structures. With the Nebulans' rise to dominance, much of the continent is covered in Stardust, at least up until the arrival of The Last Legion. The continent sees almost no daylight, with the crystals providing the only light source.

item.title: Clothing, Cloaks and Hats
item.description: Cosmetics are sorted into generic tiers. Comprises of rags, militia uniforms, hand-me-downs, peasant clothing etc. Cost: 10-100g Comprises of soldier uniforms, middle-class clothes, tradesmen's gear etc. Cost: 100-1000g Comprises of luxury silk, gold-laced whatever, faery woven stuff etc. Cost: >1000g

item.title: Wood Faeries
item.description: The wood faeries are a mysterious group of faeries, shrouded in legends and myths. They occupy the territory of the Red Oaks in the southwest of the Kingdom of Numeria, so called due to the ring of unnaturally red oak trees that signal their border. Many tall tales are told in the taverns of the land of the Laughing Titan, but there have been no credible sightings of a wood faery for the last millennium. The most famous story regards the Steel Faery king Tilion Argenhold in 222, who arrogantly marched into the Red Oaks with an army of 50000 steel faeries, only for them to never return.

item.title: Nebulan Empire
item.description:
Not native to the Continent of the Laughing Titan, the Nebulans come from a faraway northern island undiscovered by the peoples of the continent. The island was later christened "the Eye of the Storm", or "the Shadow's hollow".
The Nebulans are in a unstable situation, having just ended a civil war in 1210 with the military seizing control. With the island's resources no longer able to support the booming post war population, the dictator Millan Archae turns outwards, sending fleets of scouting ships outwards until the discovery of fishing vessels off the coast of The Right Claw. As it happens, the storms that would normally block passage from the Nebulans to the continent have died down for the first time in millennium. A series of events transpire to result in one of the worst catastrophes in the continent's history.
The dominant Nebulan religion is the Church of the Nebula, which is where their namesake comes from. With many warlords and soldiers rising to prominence in the wake of the civil war, Nebulan society is decidedly a warmongering one, just waiting for a reason...The Nebulan flag is a dark purple flag, adorned by glimmering stars.Nebulans make use of mushroom farming for food, textiles and timber, as the mushrooms they grow are the few species capable of surviving their Star Dust.The Nebulans weren't the only occupiers on their island. Originating from the hostile caves below the lands, Nebulans evolved dark skin to match the purple stones that surrounded them. The caves of the Eye of the Storm were filled with glowing crystals and plants, not dissimilar to the night sky the Nebulans would later come to revere. In the confines underground, they evolved a terrifying ability: A gas they could secrete from glands near their shoulder blades. This gas, termed as "Star Dust", has a shimmering, ghost like property, and is fatal to any who breath it in.With this, the Nebulans conquered the underworld, and spread to the surface, annihilating all other races and species, until the only ones left to turn their ire onto was themselves.The Nebulans rely on Star Dust in their initial conquests, but soon developed martial abilities, weapons and armour to fight against each other. Nebulan arms are generally inferior to those on the continent, mostly comprised of bronze, although they also make use of "Star Shards", a rare crystal native to the Eye of the Storm that posses exceptional durability and sharpness.
The Nebulan elites, called "Star-Fallen", dual wield Starlight Sickles, large sickles made out of a carefully chipped piece of Star Shard. The blades reflect and refract light in a bizarre and unusual way, and no two blades behave the same. Star-Fallen make use of this to blind and confuse their opponents before launching unpredictable slices with the strange curvature of their blades.In addition, the Nebulans store their gas in capsules and ceramic pots, before launching them with slings and catapults at the enemy.Nebulans have dark, purple skin, with grey, stone-like accents running along their cheeks, fingers and collar bones. They are physically taller but lankier compared to humans, with two long slits along their back near their shoulder blades. Their eyes are grey, with bright, piercing irises. The Nebulans speak the Nebulan tongue, a foreign language to most on the continent of the laughing titan.

item.title: Kingdom of Numeria
item.description:
The second largest kingdom on the continent of the Laughing Titan, the Kingdom of Numeria comprises mostly of humans. Originally occupying the lands west of the Numerian Mountains, the Kingdom recently captured territory up until Raven's river after The East-West War with the Aquatine Empire. Featuring much mountainous and forested terrain, the kingdom's true resources lies in its plentiful mines. After ousting the faeries in 627, the lands east of the Numerian mountains were split amongst various warlords and petty nobles, until they were united by the crusades of the Godwin house in 983.
The Kingdom of Numeria rules by a mix of theocracy and monarchy. The current King, William Godwin the first, receives counsel from a court of advisers. Within this court, the religious leader called a Lightbringer is the most influential, with the dominant and mandated religion being New Illuminetres. Apostacy is punished harshly, and outsiders were viewed with suspicion, although recent policies by the Godwins have loosened religious doctrine and opened the Kingdom to more trade and knowledge exchange. The current Lightbringer is Richard Ilysander.The Kingdom's economy revolves arounds its mines, and although the gold mines of Gold Seat have run dry long ago, the Kingdom of Numeria still holds some of the best metal workers and smiths in the lands, second only to the faeries.The lands are split amongst several lesser noble houses, jousting for power and for the chance at a seat on the King's council. Succession is through bloodlines, with the eldest son typically being the first in line.
The Kingdom of Numeria got its name from the Numerian region it inhabits. Said Numeria region got its name from the old Faerian empire and its founder, Lady Numeria.Despite their superior smiths, the Kingdom of Numeria still falls behind other factions in terms of sheer production. They specialise in armour piercing implements, using maces and crossbows to counter the heavy armour worn by their neighbours. The majority of the army is comprised of levies, supporting an elite core of superbly armed and armoured foot knights.
Elite troops can often be seen wielding powerful armour-piercing one-handed or two-handed flails, acting as the spearhead to engage enemy elites head on. Elite crossbowmen use the arbalest, the most powerful crossbow on the continent, requiring a complicated reload but paying off with a shot no armour can save you from.The people in the Kingdom of Numeria are mostly ethnically homogeneous, resembling Caucasians in the real world.Numerians mostly speak the Numerian tongue, inherited from the faeries. Local human dialects still persist, although just barely.

item.title: Miscellaneous Folk
item.description: The Wedge of the Free is a large island in the southwest of the continent. Despite its size, the island is devoid of natural resources, with its soil being barren and unsuitable for agriculture. It is theorised that the island was exploited by faeries long ago, who used up all its resources and abandoned it after. After the Kingdom of Numeria was founded, the island was used as a dumping ground for prisoners and undesirables, and although the practice has long since been discontinued, the Wedge of the Free still holds reputation as the place where criminals, the disillusioned and hermits flock to.

item.title: City of Sonostra
item.description:
The City of Sonostra is no more. Following the Tyranny of the Stars, the elites of the city fled, leaving the unfortunate citizens who could not afford passageway off the island of the Mouth to be slaughtered by the Nebulans. The city now exists as an empty shell, with Marander Gas covering the streets.The information below details the legacy of the city of Sonostra before it's destruction.
First founded in 703 by refugees fleeing from the conquest of Augustine the Third, the city of Sonostra is a city state occupying the island of the Mouth. Occupying a dominant position on the busiest trade route in the continent, Sonostra is an economic powerhouse, and rivals the powerful merchant oligarchs in the Wingard Collective.Sonostra practices democracy on paper, with elections held every five years. However, rampant corruption has led to the richest classes holding most of the power, with the elected Minister of State being little more than a puppet.Despite being the smallest human faction, the Sonostrans maintain a disproportionately large military, comprising mostly of mercenaries. Whilst the Sonostran government claims the military to be a force of external deterrence, the main use of the military is to quash worker uprisings and insurgent cells within the city. Originally, Sonostra was considered the "City of Opportunities", where anyone could come for a fresh start and rise to riches with enough hard work. Whilst maybe true during the city's earlier years, now those success stories only exist in the propaganda outlets of the Sonostran government. Working conditions are considered to be very harsh, and inequality runs rampant.
With significant immigration from all over the world, Sonostran society is diverse, and whilst the state maintains no real rules on religion, the mercantile focused religion of Bodilustra is the most popular.The Sonostrans maintain an elite city guard, comprised mainly of Aquatines with the most expensive plate armour money can buy. Most of the actual work is done by a diverse cast of mercenaries, drawn to the city under promise of coin.Sonostrans are the most diverse people in the world. The small majority is composed of the races from the Aquatine region.Most people in the city speak the Numerian Tongue. The Aquatine and Wingardian Tongues are also prevalent due to the proximity of the relevant factions.
Sonostra

item.title: The Lance of Urumi
item.description: Named after the captain who gave his life in defense of the Right Claw during Kolantine’s Folly, the Lance of Urumi is a sloop of war, made for light skirmishes and boarding.Hull integrity: 200 Base armour: 10 Base Speed: -2 Crew Capacity: 40 Cargo Capacity: 1500kg6 slots total 2 sails 2 ballistas 1 hwacha 1 boarding ramp 6 slots total 2 lifeboats 2 wingardian shredders 2 armour plating The ship's ram allows it to do d100 + (speed * d20) damage without taking damage in return.
item.guid: Bases, Transport and Companions/Ships/The Lance of Urumi.md

item.title: Ship Rules
item.description:
Ships have some stats and here's what they mean:Hull integrity: The ship's health. The ship is sunk once this reaches 0. Base armour: Works the same as regular armour but for the ship's hull integrity. Base Speed: A ship's bonuses/maluses to manoeuvre checks. Can be influenced by modules. Crew Capacity: How many crew members can fit. Cargo Capacity: How much stuff you can put on the ship in terms of weight.Ships use d20 rolls for manoeuvre checks, with the captain's sailing skill and the ship's speed as bonuses/maluses.Wind directions can impose further bonuses/maluses on this roll.A ships evasion from ranged fire is given by 5 + Speed + Captain's sailing skill.Ships have a base hull, and a number of module slots. These can be changed around for different modules, each of which serve a different function.Modules come in 2 forms: Large and small. Small modules can fit in large slots, but not the other way around.Modules can be damaged, and will stop functioning once destroyed.Modules all require a regular action to use, if applicable.Ships can be repaired with materials and a DC12 skill check, specified by each module. Each piece of material restores d12 health.
The hull is repaired with timber and carpentry. Each short rest, the ship can be repaired 1 time. Each long rest, the ship can be repaired 3 times.
Without a boarding ramp, trying to board a resisting ship will require more skill checks.Rams are pre-built into ships and cannot be changed. Ramming success chance will be determined by the two captains making manoeuvre rolls against each other.

item.title: The Blue Jay
item.description: A small and nimble craft, the Blue Jay is made of cedar planks and bears striking blue sails.Hull integrity: 50 Base armour: 5 Base Speed: 2 Crew Capacity: 9 Cargo Capacity: 500kg3 slots total 1 sail 1 crow's nest 1 empty 4 slots total 2 lifeboats 2 sails This ship does not have a dedicated ram. Ramming another ship will deal d20 + (speed * d12) damage to the target and half that to this ship.
item.guid: Bases, Transport and Companions/Ships/The Blue Jay.md

item.description: 1214/01/26: First Nebulan Contact off the coast of the tip of The Right Claw. 1214/01/26
